articles.title: HR intelligence is shaped in France — the Creandum Funds’ investment into Clustree.
articles.author: Carl Fritjofsson
articles.text: Today we're stoked to announce that the [Creandum](http://creandum.com) Fund is leading a financing round of €7m into [Clustree](http://clustree.com) - a data analytics platforms for HR used for career development, internal mobility and recruitment. Except celebrating with some enjoyable French beverages, I want to highlight the reasons behind our excitement for the company. ![Discover more at [clustree.com](http://clustree.com).](https://miro.medium.com/1*GJqa3aYN7XvLWCBu7sJLtw.png) ### Vive la ! This is our fund's first investment into France, which is a reflection of Creandum's pan-European ambition but foremost a testament to the amazing innovation currently coming out from Paris. We have already had the honor to meet with several early stage companies with impressive traction and ambitions in the region. We couldn't be more bullish on the French tech ecosystem or more excited to work closer with our local investor colleagues [Alven Capital](http://www.alvencapital.com/), [Idinvest Partners](http://www.idinvest.com/en), [Kima Ventures](http://www.kimaventures.com/) and many more. Hence, if you're a French founder looking for funding from a Euro VC with a bridge to Silicon Valley, hit us up! ### Founder authenticity. [Bénédicte](https://twitter.com/benedictedrs?lang=en), the founder and CEO of Clustree defines the kind of entrepreneurs we look for. As a mathematician, she stumbled upon the idea of Clustree when she was doing a statistical analysis to understand viable career paths for herself, and realized this data-based approach to talent management could be valuable to others. There's a strong and genuine reason behind her pursuit, which is obvious to anyone who gets the opportunity to listen to Bénédicte's visionary explanation about the company. ### Level up through AI. Like so many other VCs we're excited about the potential of artificial intelligence. The Clustree solution uses machine learning of enterprises' internal HR data and analyzes this together with 250M worldwide career paths to provide predictive HR insights and recommendations used for recruitment and internal mobility decisions. Not only is making sense of billions bytes of data exceptionally difficult for a human to do, but the AI upgrades any HR team by looking past and eliminating human bias and stereotypes in its recommendations. This AI is not about eliminating jobs, but rather augmenting human intelligence to level up your organization's people management abilities, create new opportunities for employees, and operate data driven. ### A system of intelligence for people decisions. As intelligently articulated by [Jerry Chen](None) in his search for [new moats](https://news.greylock.com/the-new-moats-53f61aeac2d9), there are three main systems of record in an enterprise: your customers (CRM), your employees (HRIS or HCM), and your assets (ERP/Financials). We now face a new era where machine learning and neural networks are used to combine these systems of record into data sets to get never-before-seen insights; a new _system of intelligence._ Clustree is building just that; a system of intelligence that governs employee data. We believe the actionable insights and recommendations generated by such a software will be tremendously important, and any company delivering this will become first of all valuable, but also defensible because of the high switching costs and obvious network effects from data collection. ### Impressive traction. With very limited sales and marketing resources, the company has been able to secure multi-year contracts with massive international enterprises like Canal+, Carrefour, Orange, and L'Oreal using its solution across 30 countries. Anyone who's ever been involved in enterprise sales knows what an achievement this is. We see the Creandum Funds' investments as enablers for growth, and with Clustree we can really see how capital can be leveraged to ramp up and scale the business. ### Macro trend redefining organizations. Creandum has been spending quite some time [thinking about how the changing landscape around "work" impacts organizations](https://medium.com/@fritjofsson/adapt-or-die-5-changes-in-the-workplace-which-will-impact-all-organizations-375409605408) and the investment into Clustree fits right into this thesis. We already had a belief that HR need to become more data driven, employee-centric and proactive, and we recognized career development and succession management are key priorities for large enterprises ([something very few do well](http://companies believe succession management is important, very few companies do it well)). When we met with Bénédicte and listened to her vision about the future and how Clustree is transforming HR we could simply nod, smile and agree! The Creandum Fund IV is super proud to lead this round and be part of the Clustree journey. It has only begun and we look forward seeing how the company will bring data-based decision making and intelligence to human resources. Onwards and upwards! ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/6tcA27KOUYV1ceajzfRcSC/556688441a144a96b767f7b8c380b50d/image_312.gif)

articles.title: The Tictail Story
articles.text: We're big fans of e-commerce, and clearly nobody does it with more Swedish style than [Tictail](http://tictail.com). We caught up with Carl Waldekranz, CEO of Tictail, to reminisce about how the Tictail family came together, and about how they became part of the greater Creandum Family. This interview was [first published on our website](https://www.creandum.com/stories/tictail). **Johan Brenner:** We've known Carl and the team for I would say 5 years, when you started Tictail... Is that right? **Carl Waldekranz:** Well the first time I got to know Creandum was actually for the company I started, Keyflow. And actually I came here to the Creandum office and pitched to Fredrik once. **Johan:** That was the nightclub booking system, right? It's still around. **Carl:** It's still around... It was before the iPhone in 2005 and we had built it on top of the Nokia N700 - you know the old Symbian device - so it was actually a super high tech project to make it work. It was really one of the first cloud-based apps. I met Fredrik when we were quite an immature business in every possible definition! **Johan:** And we met you when you recruited Kaj, then Birk came on. Then it was really interesting how you found Siavash. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/5k3u9o7VXbZq2JGVCTPf7Z/e04a98a4f9c86963a0b18b244c0b1a2e/image_308.jpg) **Carl:** Thats true - they're all great stories. Birk I met in a job interview. I met him at the agency years ago and tried to recruit him, and he was like "I'm never going to work for an agency." And then that job interview turned into a beer drinking session. I would try to hire him every 2–3 months and he would always say no, and call me an idiot. But when me and Kaj decided started a new company he was the first developer we tried to see. For a very long time we thought it would be the three of us, and we thought we would start in San Francisco. Because we were like, we are going to build the world's most used and loved e-commerce platform, and where do you build the world's biggest companies? San Francisco... with Stockholm as a close second. ![Founders Kaj, Carl, Siavash, and Birk](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/7ggGRXmbAw919JYaJamrPl/2d75374db59c456685b9f65a0c444eaf/image_309.jpg) So we got on an airplane and went over to San Francisco. But soon decided to go back when our friend Gustav at AirBNB told us, "The one thing that's more important than where you are is the people you can hire. You guys will be in such a strong position in Stockholm, but you won't be here in San Francisco." So we headed back and launched a landing page, a "get ready for launch" early access page. Birk had a really genius move [in this page's] source code, down in the bottom with Javascript inclusion to write, "Hey, if you find this message, then you're probably like us, an eager engineer, and you need to get in touch because we're building something really exciting." And this was back in October or November 2011 when we were just getting started. Just 4 or 5 people knew what we were building... and then Birk called me at 11pm and said, "Carl, you won't believe what happened. Someone just emailed us." This was like literally receiving a message from space. Someone had acknowledged that our company was a company, and not only that, they decided that they wanted to work with us. That somebody was Siavash and on paper he looked good to be true. He was the tech lead at Blocket, Sweden's largest e-commerce site, and had a really cool background too. We got on the phone with him, invited him over for coffee. The next day we all met up. The day after we all met up. And it kind of just continued. We started building stuff and then 2 months later we were like, "Hey Siavash, this is kind of crazy because two months ago we didn't even know of you. Do you want to be part of this family and start this business with us? ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/2EO6NNUgYxMZKG1cK7Dccx/063262b6a3e1cd075caaa84579fd38a8/image_310.jpg) **Johan**: That's a cute story, but that's also something we as an investor look for. There's a core trait in great teams how they recruit. Tictail was an awesome team in terms of design, but if you can recruit the right people to the team it's really important. And then when it was time for you guys to do an A-round you were certain you wanted to go to the U.S. because that was the biggest market for you. And we understood that you wanted a U.S. lead. We respected that and despite wanting to be in there, we hopefully helped get you in there. Ultimately you chose Thrive out of many, who is New York-based and had a focus on E-commerce. And in retrospect it was the right choice. **Carl**: Similarly to you guys, we as entrepreneurs bet on people, and I think with Creandum and the Thrive guys, it wasn't about the fund or the valuation, it was about the people. That's something we've thought about since day one: to hire people we think we can learn from, and enjoy working with, and also to work with investors we think we can learn from and enjoy working with. That personal relationship has really been the core foundation of our company. _[Johan Brenner](https://www.creandum.com/team/johan-brenner) is a partner at [Creandum](http://creandum.com), a venture capital fund powering innovation from Stockholm, San Francisco and Berlin. We believe any industry can be disrupted by the right entrepreneur. [We back the companies of tomorrow](https://www.creandum.com/portfolio/)._

articles.title: Creandum-backed Opbeat acquired by Elastic
articles.author: Daniel Blomquist
articles.text: Last week, [news](https://techcrunch.com/2017/06/22/elastic-enters-apm-space-with-opbeat-acquisition/) broke that Elastic has acquired Opbeat, the leader in APM (Application Performance Management) for javascript. Having followed the founders, Rasmus and Ron, from the very early days leading up to an investment from the Creandum Funds together with Founders Fund in 2015, it has been great to see them develop and build an amazing team and product which will be a perfect match for Elastic going forward. As developers, Rasmus and Ron had experienced first-hand that new tools were needed to support modern dev ops where developers are responsible for developing and maintaining the code. As Werner Vogels, CTO at Amazon used to say, "you build it, you run it!" So they decided to build the product that was missing on the market and subsequently raised capital from Instagram co-founder Mike Krieger, Facebook co-founder Andrew McCollum, and former Spotify CTO Andreas Ehn. Since then, the company has become the leading challenger for modern APM. It is the first APM supporting Javascript frameworks which is a big thing as, today, Desktop, Web and Mobile Applications are built with JavaScript frameworks (front-end) while server-side (backend) increasingly is outsourced to cloud and IAAS-providers. Javascript frameworks like React (supported by Google), Node.js, Angular (supported by Facebook) are catching fire and are the fastest-growing technologies according to StackOverflow. As Elastic is a leader in analytics, primarily on log data, the Opbeat acquisition provides a very nice product complement to also provide analytics and insights on the applications that are generating the data. And by joining forces with Elastic, Opbeat gains access to a whole new set of customers as well as the breadth of the Elastic platform. It has been a great pleasure to work with Rasmus, Ron and the whole Opbeat team and I am sure they will continue to deliver a kick-ass product experience as part of the Elastic family.

articles.title: Creandum Fund IV Invests in RFRSH
articles.author: Simon Schmincke
articles.text: When I was a teenager, Counter-Strike was the number one source of heated debates around the dinner table. My passion for the game was the reason I almost got kicked out of the house. Today, after a less heated debate around a boardroom table, we are proud to announce Creandum Fund IV's investment in RFRSH, the company that is capturing that passion better than anyone else in the world. If you haven't noticed, over the last decade, counter-strike and other multiplayer games have taken on the characteristics of traditional sports. Teams get paid significant salaries and train full time in a structured way. And just like in traditional sports, they do this in a professional setting with coaches, physical trainers, and sports psychologists. Teams fly around the world and compete in multi million dollar tournaments. Players connect with millions of followers on social media. And the content that is produced around tournaments, supported by big industry sponsoring, is bought by traditional and new media companies. While a big amount of people play the game for fun, and always will, some have decided to reach for the stars and become the best in the world. And millions of fans watch their games online and at arena filling events. We believe, this is just the beginning, and this is why today we announce Creandum Fund IV's investment in RFRSH. RFRSH was founded by [Nikolaj Nyholm](https://www.linkedin.com/in/nikolajn/), [Jakob Lund Kristensen](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jakob-lund-kristensen-3534425a/) and [Rene Rechtman](https://www.linkedin.com/in/rene-rechtman-74665/) in Copenhagen and aims to bring the most premium content to the viewers of Counter-Strike. RFRSH is hands-on with the current #1 team, [Astralis](http://astralis.gg/), as well as the powerhouses [Godsent](http://godsent.gg/) and [Heroic](http://heroic.gg/). By working with these teams, RFRSH is helping to take their skills to the next level. Think Bayern Munich Soccer Training Facilities at Säbener Street in Munich, or how Tiger Woods changed the Golf game by hitting the gym instead of whisky and cigars. The players should be able to only focus on getting better, while RFRSH's staff takes care of the rest. It's time for esports to reach the truly professional level. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/4ZzEeAVKsGCxfAzEnUOuOm/02813d305674243e1c48cf7b230e2dba/image_305.jpg) RFRSH is also a bet on counter-strike, a fast paced game played 5 vs 5 in rounds of 2 minutes. The game was first released in 2000 and 17 years later, its popularity has only grown. Across varying maps, like Italian towns or industrial facilities, one team attacks, one team defends, and the first team to win 16 rounds first wins the map. The team that wins most maps wins the game. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/7JWcTwomBuk5yupjbkBhwk/5bb42873765d62208bf3188c3173d375/image_306.jpg) All broadcasted games have professional live commentators, who explain game situations, talk about player backgrounds, specialties of maps or situations - and make watching counter-strike so entertaining. Continuing the analogy to traditional sports, today 220,000,000 people around the world watch some or multiple esport formats. These are either live coverages of tournaments - both on- and offline - or online leagues in the various games. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/6OebuAkAATh6B6ZRz2alDD/cab4a1e4331cc24f8ff878a830ea52f3/image_307.jpg) ## Our Hypothesis Today, esports is still mostly watched by people who play the game themselves. We believe, like traditional sports, that esports will become mainstream, meaning even people that do not play games start watching it. Today, content formats around esports are already attracting significant viewerships. We believe, the number of viewers will only grow from here. Today, non-endemic brands are seeing this industry as a way to reach a consumer group who has stopped watching TV, buying magazines or react to billboards. We believe esports is one of the next big channels that brands will use to engage with them. Today, most content is watched on gaming format distributors like Twitch and YouTube Gaming. We believe esports content will be distributed through a greater variety of media channels in the future, increasing reach naturally. We also believe, that the content around counter-strike can be lifted to the next level. We believe the RFRSH team is in the perfect position to do just that - for the fans of today and tomorrow. We are excited to support RFRSH in this effort. — At Creandum, we believe any industry can be disrupted by the right entrepreneur. Check out our [website](http://creandum.com) or follow [Creandum Family](http://medium.com/creandum-family) on Medium to learn more.

articles.title: The chicken and the egg
articles.excerpt: Bootstrapping a network
articles.text: We know that [network effects is the most powerful competitive advantage a business can have](https://medium.com/creandum-family/what-you-need-to-know-about-network-effects-b7f594d7b011). But until you have lots of users they work to your disadvantage: what's the value of a messaging app if your friends aren't on it? Since my [post on Network Effects](https://medium.com/creandum-family/what-you-need-to-know-about-network-effects-b7f594d7b011), a lot of people have reached out to me and asked for input on how to overcome this chicken and egg problem. Below are strategies for doing just that. ## Allow single player mode What's the first thing you should do to solve the chicken and egg problem?Make sure that you can be valuable for your first user. Your product needs value _as a tool_ more than just a marketplace or network. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/pYHIpGcecTH0YioNWFNx8/79f0a4608ac3d77a58834cecf83b936b/image_302.jpg) As you probably remember from The Social Network movie, before launch, Facebook had scraped photos from each dorm and matched the names with courses, which meant that when it launched, it was already populated, and you could browse people, see pictures of them, as well as which classes they were taking. Similarly, Pinterest offered a tool to pin photos on the internet, Instagram gave you cool filters for photos you could share elsewhere, and Vivino gave you a smart library of the wines you like. All these companies are social networks, where the entire point is to interact with other users, and yet they all made sure to have features that made them valuable for an individual user as well. In a few cases, specifically messaging platforms like Skype or Slack, it's really hard to do this, but in the vast majority of cases, this strategy is critical to success. ## Fake it til you make it Many business models with network effects somehow involve two types of users: suppliers and consumers. In marketplaces this is obvious, but in most social networks you see a similar dynamic, with some people posting content, and others mainly consuming content. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/74fAb9imlpqdR1O7KayKff/6baacfd6abf4a4f93c18c76c724fb838/image_303.jpg) If your business has this property, then here's a strategy for you. It's highly unsexy, it can feel like a waste of time, and it doesn't scale at all. Nonetheless, you need to do it: be a supplier on the network yourself. Whether you do it personally or pay someone to do it depends on how well funded you are, but no matter what, there's a lot to learn by at least doing part of it yourself. Reddit's founder, Steve Huffman, spent every morning for the first several months loading up content on Reddit for people to read, before any of the users started posting their own links. Airbnb's founders famously rented out their own couch as the first property available on Airbnb. Uber simply hired drivers to make sure that the first customers would have someone to pick them up - and they still do for the first few months when they launch a new city. There's clearly a limit to how far this can take you, but in the early days, it's often one of the most effective ways you can spend your time, plus it gives you great insight into how it is to actually use your product: Brian Chesky, Airbnb's CEO, famously still lives a significant part of the year in Airbnb's while Airbnb'ing out his own apartment. ## Be more narrow in your focus than you could possibly imagine The marginal value of an additional user depends on when or where that user joins. For me, the value of Snapchat increases a lot if one of my friends joins, and almost nothing if some person I don't know on the other side of the world joins. Similarly, [Wolt](https://wolt.com/) adding an additional restaurant in Stockholm makes me like them even more, even though I couldn't care less about them adding one in Helsinki. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/4hYV2yWQFsIvU7GaAGWwCy/b7075f8adaf77cd018a12b0dad3c27df/image_304.jpg) You need to use this to your advantage: be insanely narrow in your focus on which users to target for your network. Again, Facebook is a good example. Today people have the misconception that Mark Zuckerberg invented the social network, but in reality there were plenty others out there, such as Friendster or Myspace. What Facebook did differently was that they started out only for Harvard students. Zuckerberg wanted to make sure that they had amazing user engagement there before expanding to other colleges. Then they pursued a highly focused expansion strategy, deliberately signing up specific colleges, and each time making sure that user penetration and engagement on those colleges were high, before moving on. Zuckerberg specifically did not make Facebook available to the wider public, because he knew that having 1000 users that know each other well is 100x more valuable than having 1000 users scattered across the globe. See this [early interview where he talks about focus](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=--APdD6vejI). Other successful companies have done the same: Ebay initially focused on people buying and selling Beanie Babies (!), Airbnb focused on specific cities at exactly the dates where conferences were held in those cities, as it meant that demand would be high and hotels hard to come by, and at Vaniday, the beauty services marketplace I ran in 2015, we focused not only on cities, but on specific neighbourhoods, and even on a specific vertical (like hairdressers) within those neighborhoods: It made it easier to acquire customers that were likely to buy from the supply we had. As Paul Graham of Y Combinator says: [Do things that don't scale](http://paulgraham.com/ds.html). ## Is there a silver bullet? Each company is unique, and strategies that work for one company may not work for another one. The key to success is disciplined and never ending experimentation at the highest possible velocity: the more experiments you can run per week the bet

articles.title: “What’s a good retention rate?”
articles.text: Ability to retain customers over time is a good indicator of product-market fit and general business health and viability when looked at in cohorts. It's a vital metric that every startup should track, but can be difficult to interpret off the bat. So naturally, many entrepreneurs we meet ask us questions along the lines of: What's a good **1 week retention** for a **gaming company**? What's a good **3** **month retention** for a **marketplace**? What's a good **6 month retention** for a **consumer app**? What's a good **1 year retention** for **enterprise SaaS**? Given the number of companies we meet and our portfolio companies that we have the fortune to work with, expectations to what makes a high potential venture are natural to form (investors often refer to it as **pattern matching**). But we try to constantly challenge our thinking, and try avoid just that when we look at startup metrics. Here's why. People like to find yardsticks to calibrate their feelings around seemingly abstract concepts that various non-revenue metrics and ratios tend to be. The pitfall of benchmarking your thinking around retention is that it's rarely ever bound to be an **** s to **** s comparison, even with seemingly similar products and services. ### Peeking under the hood of retention Retention is a resultant of various factors. Factors, which sometimes render a 10% retention rate perfectly fine - something that could in most other cases be a sign of a terminal illness on your business. Counterintuitively enough, in some cases a high retention rate can also be symptomatic. Thus, it's often good to take a step back, and instead look under the proverbial hood of a retention metric. Something we as investors need to constantly remind ourselves about, and suggest entrepereneurs to follow suit. <iframe src="https://cdn.embedly.com/widgets/media.html?src=https%3A%2F%2Fgiphy.com%2Fembed%2Fl2Sq8EYhA66vdOfAI%2Ftwitter%2Fiframe&url=https%3A%2F%2Fmedia.giphy.com%2Fmedia%2Fl2Sq8EYhA66vdOfAI%2Fgiphy.gif&image=https%3A%2F%2Fmedia.giphy.com%2Fmedia%2Fl2Sq8EYhA66vdOfAI%2Fgiphy.gif&key=a19fcc184b9711e1b4764040d3dc5c07&type=text%2Fhtml&schema=giphy" title="Peeking under the hood" height="326" width="435"></iframe> Broadly speaking, retention is a function of commitment (i.e. ,⏰, etc.), product utility, frequency of use, competition and switching costs. If onboarding your platform is made very easy (kudos to your product team ), then you may on one hand increase the number of new users you onboard, but on the other hand, it can have a negative impact on your retention rate. That is because you also convert users that may not have an immediate need for your product, but decide to test it out anyhow - simply because it is very easy to do so. New technologies and press coverage can have a somewhat comparable effect - create hype and attract a broad range of users that may not have an explicit need for your product, resulting in a poor retention rate. Conversely, if users go through the trouble of filling out lengthy forms or pay to use your service in the first place - they make a commitment and go through a process of self-selection that indicates a stronger need for your product. Thus, you can expect a significantly higher retention with likely more people dropping off earlier in your onboarding funnel. So, your particular business model also affects your expected retention rate. If you sport a free(mium) model, you would likely do injustice to yourself by benchmarking your retention metrics against competitors with different business models, but otherwise similar products. To illustrate this, think Spotify vs. Soundcloud or Match.com vs. Tinder. In the case of Match.com you need to both pay to play and invest time in filling out lengthy forms, or so I've been told . As a result, Match.com ends up with a selection of far more committed users in comparison to Tinder whose potential users are just a click of a button away from starting their search for . Another good example is neobanks vs. high street banks. I often see neobanks boasting about their much lower customer acquisiton costs (CAC) in comparison to traditional banks. This, however, is a source of false confidence, and should not be treated as a benchmark. Traditional banks pay to acquire customers who have bothered to physically show up at a branch and most likely endure lengthy queues and form filling to open up an account. Whereas neobanks pay to acquire customers who can complete their swift onboarding process wherever and whenver they feel comfortable. Due to this key difference, neobanks **need to** have a much lower CAC, because they acquire less committed users and can thus expect a much lower customer lifetime value (LTV). Switching costs can further muddy the water when it comes to retention. In some cases high retention can be misinterpreted as a good product-market fit, whereas it can actually be the result of high switching costs that may help you to get away with a sub par product. Think LMSs for schools, CRMs, customer support tools, or other products that tightly integrate into your workflow and/or in which you accumulate data that is not easily transferrable. In such cases, complementary metrics such as net promoter score (NPS) can come in handy to get a clearer picture. ### A holistic approach to looking at retention To avoid any pitfalls discussed, retention should never be looked at in isolation. You should always **look at the complete funnel** - from a potential customer becoming aware (e.g. visting your website or showing an intent to onboard) to actively using or paying for your service. A high rate of retention can indicate a high drop-off rate in the top-end of your funnel, and conversely, a high conversion rate in the top-end can result in a low retention rate. At the end of the day, the crude retention rate in itself is somewhat irrelevant - it's the underlying drivers and the holistic picture you need to focus on. Figure out what makes

articles.title: Better Business Banking — Creandum Fund IV Invests in Tide
articles.author: Simon Schmincke
articles.text: It's 2017 and banking is still broken on so many levels. In my recent experience helping set up Creandum Advisor's Berlin branch at one of Europe's largest banks, it took multiple visits, countless signatures, visits to the notary, and even a powerpoint of the firm's organisational structure just to open a bank account. And now I receive paper-based account statements every three days! We need a new relationship to banking. With their [$14m Series A](https://techcrunch.com/2017/07/03/uks-tide-raises-14m-to-challenge-big-banks-with-a-mobile-first-service-for-smbs/), [George](https://www.linkedin.com/in/georgebevis/) and [Laurence](https://www.linkedin.com/in/laurence-krieger-98b8a4120/) from [Tide.co](http://www.tide.co) are on a mission to revolutionize the banking [experience](https://www.linkedin.com/in/gmarsh/) for the European SMEs. Creandum Fund is proud to co-lead this round with [Anthemis](http://www.anthemis.com/), joining [LocalGlobe](https://localglobe.vc/) and [Passion Capital](http://www.passioncapital.com/), as well as a [whole](https://www.linkedin.com/in/alex-chesterman-obe-0b83704/) [bunch](https://www.linkedin.com/in/williamreeve/) of experienced [angel](https://www.linkedin.com/in/erroldamelin/) [investors](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ianhogarth/). ### The status quo Today SMEs and sole traders are vastly underserved by the high street banks. Most established players are notoriously slow, expensive (riddled with hidden fees) and lack essential value added services and tools - there are many unmet needs in this space. On top of that, banks are still ignoring the possibilities generated through new technology. Processes are paper based, slow and not customer centric, and a lot of the communication is offline. Adoption new opportunities due to the slowly, yet steadily changing regulatory frameworks does not seem to happen. We believe there is an opportunity to fundamentally change how business banking is done. And Tide is on a mission to make that happen. SMEs, freelancers, and sole traders are changing faster than the banks. They need immediate communication. Individual employees need purchasing rights and tools. And SMEs are now more international and mobile than ever. ### Tide is the best new bank we have seen Tide provides a full fledged mobile first business account in 5 minutes - an unparalleled user experience even compared to many consumer facing neobanks. Tide aims to support multi-currency accounts and eliminate admin work by adding an array of different tools - from automated accounting to invoice management (creating/tracking/chasing). Tide's product is the central hub between customers, employees and product partners. Tide wants to be the brain of your SME when it comes to anything money. And ultimately, Tide is SME first. Functions, products, user experience, team integrations, are all catered towards the SME. And that is why the product feedback is fantastic. <iframe src="https://cdn.embedly.com/widgets/media.html?src=https%3A%2F%2Fplayer.vimeo.com%2Fvideo%2F192154419&url=https%3A%2F%2Fvimeo.com%2F192154419&image=https%3A%2F%2Fi.vimeocdn.com%2Fvideo%2F640313674_1280.jpg&key=a19fcc184b9711e1b4764040d3dc5c07&type=text%2Fhtml&schema=vimeo" title="" height="1080" width="1920"></iframe> ### Our Hypothesis **We believe** that business banking is one of the spaces in FinTech that lack innovation so far. Tide is in the position to completely revolutionize the banking experience. **We believe** that SMEs appreciate products catered towards them. The consumerization of the enterprise is visible in so many areas. Tide will hit this space as well. **We believe** fair and transparent pricing is appreciated by SMEs. And less paper, too. **We believe** that by integrating partners that have specialised within their area, one can generate a complete product experience with best of class feature sets. The partnership with Iwoca that Tide announced today is just one example. **We believe** big companies can be built by focussing on the SME segment. So it goes without saying, we're proud to back George and Laurence on the mission to build a completely new banking experience. If this is excites you as much as it excites us, Tide.co is [hiring](https://tide.workable.com/) for various positions in London. articles.title: An AI for Business Travel — Comtravo Closes Series A
articles.author: Simon Schmincke
articles.text: With the closing of its Series A, we are thrilled to finally announce Creandum Fund's investment in Comtravo. We were bullish a year ago when we began working with [Michael](https://www.linkedin.com/in/michael-riegel-1318a22/), [Jannik](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jannik-neumann-421b077/), [Marko](https://www.linkedin.com/in/marko-schilde-14095480/), [Slobodan](https://www.linkedin.com/in/utvara/), and the rest of the Comtravo team. But after seeing the progress in the product, team, and overall business we couldn't be more excited to be backing the future of business travel. Once you use it, you'll know exactly what we're talking about. Here's how it came together. We started looking into the business travel market in the Spring of 2016. The new companies we saw with self booking tools, chatbots, and concierge-like services didn't feel like the right approach for the massive SME travel market; we knew from our own experience that the approach with the least friction in the UI will win. The existing consumer solutions did not satisfy business travellers needs— though we do acknowledge the consumerization of business tools as a general trend. The incumbents were too focused on big corporate, or their products were not flexible enough (think no rebooking after 6pm on week days - what?). No one we spoke to was happy with their solution. Except for Comtravo's customers. The company was locked into product market fit before Series A. ### Comtravo is building a human-machine hybrid for business travel. Comtravo is a game changer. The product has the simplest interface you can imagine: email, skype, or text message. Just drop them a line saying, "I need to fly from Stockholm to Berlin on July 23 before my 16:00 meeting in the center. Would like a hotel in Kreuzberg and fly back in the morning." You then receive a tailor made response with a couple options to choose from. More than that, it's _smart_. Comtravo is automated and customised based on your past booking behaviour and company travel policies. This way, travellers don't need to change their preferred channel of communication. Booking is a simple click away. We tried out and loved it. And so did our accountant. The company's approach of no-frills and no-friction is perfect for the SME market. Under the hood we are even more impressed. The team around [Marko](https://www.linkedin.com/in/marko-schilde-14095480/), [Slobo](https://www.linkedin.com/in/utvara/) have been working on the machine for 1 1/2 years, now allowing fully automated requests, search and communication with the customers, as well as instant fulfillments, booking, invoicing and reporting. Today a good chunk of all requests are handled fully automated through a mix of NLP and ML in the background. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/2uyvkdklmbeJjOpkF2FdHI/8bd6ac42e326f8ce2d3b52eb21de2cfd/image_300.png) Comtravo's core focus is on the SME market: any company between 5 and 100 travellers, or 50,000 to 1,000,000€ yearly travel budget. The SME Market makes 2/3rd of the business travel market in the Western world, yet no one really seems to focus on it! The market is ripe to grab and disrupt with Comtravo's automation. Comtravo has been growing rapidly over the last 12 months and and today with the closure of an 8,5m€ Series A the company will be in the position to expand internationally. We are excited about what is yet to come. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/6m2x3HJIh5RxSzdwRPGtBM/ba33fc424925f45ad7e7502aeb08ade3/image_301.png) ### Our Hypothesis Comtravo's business model is the perfect example of data network effects. The human-machine hybrid allows for the generation of data, which in return fuels it's machine which gets better and better with every client - until we reach a level of limited to no human interaction. We believe these types business models will have a significant share in venture returns over the next years. With the busy chatter about AI startups in the last 18 months, we looked into various approaches to use technology in a business sense. We believe using technologies in a defined vertical, where structured data is available, can create rapid value and allow startups to catch up with the established incumbents. On a unit economy basis, parity can be reached early. This is why we believe in Comtravo's approach especially. We believe business travel will thrive, despite an ever growing pool of remote communication tools, decentralized and virtual organisations. Asia's market numbers see even more rapid growth than the EU and US. We are thrilled to be working with the team over the next years. If your company's business travel is broken, try Comtravo. If this is excites you, Comtravo is [hiring](https://jobs.lever.co/comtravo) for various positions in Berlin.

articles.title: Creandum backs Bokio in €3.1m seed round
articles.excerpt: Automating bookkeeping for small businesses, free of charge
articles.text: ### Creandum backs Bokio in €3.1m seed round _"I love doing my bookkeeping" - said no small business owner ever._ Anyone that has run a business knows that bookkeeping is a tedious and backward-looking task. It can take hours to go through receipts, verify payroll, and fill in invoicing details. These are incredibly important parts of running a business, but they're not tasks that create more value for your company. So, it comes with no surprise that small business owners would rather watch paint dry on the wall than do their bookkeeping. In an ideal world, small business owners would go with a solution that: 1. Minimises time spent on bookkeeping. 2. Does not cost an arm and a leg. 3. Is proactive with value-added services. This, however, is a tradeoff that small business owners need to navigate - they could pick two of the three, until now. That's why we are proud to announce that in a €3.1 million Seed round Creandum is backing [[Bokio](https://www.bokio.se)](https://www.bokio.se) - a team that strives to minimise time spent by small business owners on bookkeeping, while helping them to cut costs and focus on value creation. Bokio offers an automated accounting software coupled with seamlessly integrated invoicing and payroll features free of charge. ## Time for a new paradigm There's a massive pool of business owners looking for a new solution. Small businesses make up 96% of all businesses globally, meaning there are hundreds of millions of people doing the same tasks over and over again, every month. The repetitive, somewhat predictable and data rich tasks means it's an area ripe for automation. The timing is right for Bokio for two reasons. First, we have seen huge advancements in the areas of machine learning, and Bokio's solution is the most impressive we've seen. And secondly, we have new regulations in banking (i.e. PSD2) that opens up a new and valuable pool of data that can be leveraged. At the intersection of these two, a new opportunity is born. An opportunity to break the traditional tradeoff in bookkeeping. An opportunity to automate bookkeeping for small business owners without breaking the bank. In fact, we believe that bookkeeping of the future should and will be free for small business owners. While bookkeeping becomes more and more of a transparent layer of a business, a bookkeeping software with up-to-date data can become an increasingly valuable tool that helps to make better business decision on the go, and does no longer serve just the purpose of recording and reporting. Offering a free product helps Bokio to acquire customers and customer data at little-to-no marketing spend - at present 50–100 new customers per day. The aim is to monetize through upselling value-added services such as e.g. credits, insurances, utilities, etc., to companies by turning customers' data into valuable insights and helping them to make better business decisions. Bookkeeping and accounting market is a huge market - around €6 Bn in Sweden alone. And despite accounting differences in various countries, there is a huge international opportunity. ## The bottom line: Backing Bokio intersects a number of themes that we like at Creandum: a huge market in the Fintech vertical, ripe for true disruption, a core service for SMEs to help them in their business. It's all very similar to investments made by the Creandum Funds catering for the SME segment, in iZettle, Tictail, Planday, SYB, Comtravo, Pleo and Tide, and, a perfect application for machine learning. We're very excited about Bokio. Go [check them out](https://www.bokio.se) and start embracing the future of bookkeeping today. _At Creandum, we believe any industry can be disrupted by the right entrepreneur. Check out our [website](http://creandum.com) or follow [Creandum Family](http://medium.com/creandum-family) on Medium to learn more._

articles.title: Level up
articles.author: Carl Fritjofsson
articles.excerpt: The beginning of 2 new lives
articles.text: I had just started to get a hang of this thing called "life". At 36 years of age, I had learned how to tackle the most common obstacles and enemies thrown at me. I was pretty skilled in jumping over gaps and navigating around the _[Goombas](http://mario.wikia.com/wiki/Goomba)_. I often knew what was coming, what to expect, and I rarely had to be nervous. Sure, [my imposter syndrome](https://medium.com/creandum-family/im-a-fraud-my-dealings-with-imposter-syndrome-bbe07091576a) seems to be a constant in life, but I had learned to live with it. Suddenly a few weeks ago it all changed. I reached the next level in life. The same obstacles and enemies remain. But they are joined by new ones, who all of them appear significantly more powerful than anything I've ever seen before. _[Spinys](http://mario.wikia.com/wiki/Spiny)_ and _[Koopa Paratroopas](http://mario.wikia.com/wiki/Koopa_Paratroopa)_ means I have to learn new offense and defense tactics. And I can't even imagine what complex strategy would be needed to defeat the boss at this level. Most likely, this level never really ends and there will be multiple _[Bowsers](http://mario.wikia.com/wiki/Bowser)_ to overthrow over the years. There doesn't appear to be any detailed instruction manual to follow to master this. I read a bunch of books already, but in the playing field I've already discovered most of the theories taught are quickly forgotten. Luckily many untrained people have gone before me and excelled at this level in life, which is the ultimate comfort I have in moments of distress. The old life is still here. Everything hasn't changed. I'm still the same person and the aspirations and values remain. But there a new dimension which has been added on top of the old. Nothing has been lost. More has simply been added. I didn't realize there was room for more, until now... A few weeks ago I leveled up. A new life was born, and my new life began... ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/2VncMF7EcqYYlVh5UvgOP6/86f59c7823c8e1d0b2fa43c6c80d5546/image_299.jpg) ...and things will never be the same again. <iframe src="https://cdn.embedly.com/widgets/media.html?src=https%3A%2F%2Fgiphy.com%2Fembed%2FgjdS9VFkMHzva%2Ftwitter%2Fiframe&url=https%3A%2F%2Fgiphy.com%2Fgifs%2Fwtf-mario-super-gjdS9VFkMHzva&image=https%3A%2F%2Fmedia.giphy.com%2Fmedia%2FgjdS9VFkMHzva%2Fgiphy.gif&key=a19fcc184b9711e1b4764040d3dc5c07&type=text%2Fhtml&schema=giphy" title="" height="380" width="435"></iframe>
