Digital healthcare solutions show strong results Digital health is making breakthroughs within all sorts of fields, and [doctors are endorsing](https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-019-02873-1) the solutions. Diabetes was one of the first areas to gain traction, as the right digitally supported behavioural interventions can significantly reduce and even cure diabetes type 2 (if you are interested in how - check out [Virta Health](https://www.virtahealth.com/research)). While menopause cannot be compared to diabetes there are still [studies showing how lifestyle choices](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5558404/) might delay or decrease symptoms. We are convinced that there is more

articles.title: Creandum backs unitQ
articles.author: Carl Fritjofsson
articles.excerpt: Quality is the only way to win
articles.text: History tells the tale of many classic battles such as the battle of Waterloo between the British and French. In modern days, and with fewer human casualties there are some other well-remembered battles. Hipchat vs Slack, Tidal vs Spotify, and GoToMeeting vs Zoom are a few examples. We all know who won each one of them. So what's the common denominator between the winner? The answer is quality! This is obviously a somewhat a simplification of things, but in a competitive market over the longterm, quality is the only true differentiator for a business. Product quality is what makes companies or . As investors and entrepreneurs, at [Creandum](http://creandum.com), we're very aware of the importance of quality. This is why we are exceptionally happy today to tell the world about [unitQ](http://unitq.com) - a company we've been working with for some time. ### Quality is obvious but difficult. Building a great product that works well and that customers love is a difficult task. Christian and Niklas knew this very well already before founding unitQ. Back in the days of 2007, they built a consumer app called [Skout](https://www.crunchbase.com/organization/skout) from the ground up. They got an impressive amount of users, raised some from a16z, and finally sold the business in 2016. During this journey, they spent a lot of time finding, reporting and fixing bugs. A key insight they gained was to listen very attentively to your end-users. This sounds super cliché, but first of all, it is true, and secondly, this is more difficult than you may imagine. What Christian and Niklas spent endless hours on was manually reading through reviews and what people were saying about Skout online, and then trying to relay relevant insights back into product and engineering. ![The unitQ Founders - Christian, David, & Niklas.](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/9sl3n4bJSQ1FCqzJ2szWY/b5280ba119afe5481fbaf86abfc8ba8e/image_216.jpg) After they sold their company in 2016, Christian and Niklas not only understood the fundamental importance of quality for products, but they also had learned a lot of techniques to improve quality efficiently. That's when they realized that they needed to share this knowledge with other people, and that's why they founded unitQ. Whilst quality monitoring has existed for a long time, extracting meaningful human data around quality, experience and engagement has never been possible in the past. But unitQ's unique NLP engine enables them to extract relevant data from unstructured human information. This gives any product-centric organization a way to automate continuous product quality monitoring across platforms, devices, and languages, and seamlessly integrate the output of such monitoring into the product roadmap. The company has operated in stealth while working with a range of top global consumer apps, and today we're super proud to announce that unitQ has secured an $11m Series A led by Google's AI-focused venture fund [Gradient Ventures](https://www.gradient.com/). We couldn't be more proud of Creandum having the opportunity of being the company's first backer some time ago already, and we're looking forward to continuing to work with [David](https://www.linkedin.com/in/deklov/), [Nicklas](https://www.linkedin.com/in/nlindstrom/), and [Christian](https://www.linkedin.com/in/cwiklund/) as they scale this business while helping companies win through improved quality. <iframe src="https://cdn.embedly.com/widgets/media.html?src=https%3A%2F%2Fgiphy.com%2Fembed%2F3oKHWbFpuUaRkZNDuo%2Ftwitter%2Fiframe&display_name=Giphy&url=https%3A%2F%2Fgiphy.com%2Fgifs%2Fspongebob-spongebob-squarepants-episode-9-3oKHWbFpuUaRkZNDuo&image=https%3A%2F%2Fmedia.giphy.com%2Fmedia%2F3oKHWbFpuUaRkZNDuo%2Fgiphy.gif&key=a19fcc184b9711e1b4764040d3dc5c07&type=text%2Fhtml&schema=giphy" title="" height="326" width="435"></iframe>

articles.title: Mavenoid: Fighting for our Right to Repair
articles.author: Staffan Helgesson
articles.text: _Co-authored by [Beata Klein](https://blog.creandum.com/@beata_66804)_ _**As we are forced to throw away more broken tech products than ever before, intelligent software has the power to unite companies and consumers with the ultimate goal of increased product longevity. We explore how Creandum-backed Mavenoid and its AI/ML software is a key facilitator in the Right to Repair movement.**_ When AI hits the headlines, it's often for reasons that are surprising, impressive, or alarming. The impressive side includes stories such as when [AlphaGo beat world-title-winning Go player Lee Sedol](https://deepmind.com/alphago-korea) in 2016 or when Google demonstrated its Assistant [casually calling a hair salon and booking an appointment](https://www.youtube.com/watch?time_continue=13&amp=&v=wqhxVwXI6q8&amp=&feature=emb_logo). Certain other stories carry a darker tone, from the emergence of [Deepfake videos](https://edition.cnn.com/interactive/2019/01/business/pentagons-race-against-deepfakes/), putting our ability to tell fiction from reality into question, to the doomsday prophecies emanating from a coalition of influencers across both [tech](https://www.vanityfair.com/news/2017/03/elon-musk-billion-dollar-crusade-to-stop-ai-space-x) and [philosoph](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2016/jun/12/nick-bostrom-artificial-intelligence-machine)y, AI often seems grandiose at it's best and scary at its worst. What you won't hear so much about, are the applications of AI and Machine Learning that appear innocuous yet are incredibly powerful; the ways in which, every day, AI/ML is enabling people and businesses to work more efficiently and boost their sustainability. That's exactly what Creandum-backed [Mavenoid](https://www.mavenoid.com/en/) is doing. ## A 21st-century solution Mavenoid is a virtual agent that delivers technical support to customers, enabling them to troubleshoot issues and solve common problems with their technology products themselves - without having to contact human support teams. Headquartered in Stockholm, Mavenoid was founded by two engineers who formerly worked for [Palantir](https://www.palantir.com/), a California based software company. The Company's technology is built on several years of research conducted in close collaboration with the Swedish Armed Forces, who used it to help mechanics repair tanks and terrain vehicles in the field. ## Not your everyday chatbot The solution that Mavenoid provides is far from your typical chatbot. In fact, this is a good juncture to sort out the terminology so that we're all on the same page. Let's start by breaking down the difference between AI / ML. Artificial Intelligence is an overarching concept to create intelligent machines which have the ability to simulate human thinking and behaviour. Machine Learning on the other hand, is an application or subset of AI that allows machines to learn from data without being programmed explicitly. Or, to keep it simple: ML is written in Python, AI is written in PowerPoint . Returning to the subject of chatbots it is a common misconception that all chatbots learn. A substantial number are quite shallow, with a few predefined questions and answers, or naturally fit into a simple decision tree. We have all seen or [experienced hilarious (and sometimes terrifying)](https://www.businessnewsdaily.com/10450-funniest-chatbot-fails.html) examples of "dumb" chatbots. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/46NV27dV7CRyU3dBA027Sj/3f53fd42e154ca9b5c0372bc6b7055bf/image_214.jpg) Unlike generic chatbots, Mavenoid's Machine Learning capabilities mean that it can handle the entire range of support requests: from installation and usage to more complicated troubleshooting. With their solution companies can help their customers repair and maintain their products safely, with step-by-step instructions. In this way, Mavenoid is not just helping consumers to bypass troublesome support processes; it's actually empowering people and businesses to solve complicated technical problems, with the ultimate goal of enabling them to use their electronic product for longer. Mavenoid is driving sustainability at a time when we are figuratively drowning in technical waste. ## Throwaway society The problem of technical waste is real. In the UK alone, [fewer than one in ten people attempt to repair items that have broken](https://news.sky.com/story/we-throw-away-millions-of-items-that-could-be-repaired-11544441). Similarly, consumers increasingly have to deal with ‘[planned obsolescence](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/shortcuts/2015/mar/03/has-planned-obsolesence-had-its-day-design)'. For decades, manufacturers have built goods with a view to them breaking after a certain period of time. They are also increasingly making [devices impossible to repair](https://www.techspot.com/article/1548-unrepairable-tech-devices/). This simply leaves consumers with little choice but to throw broken devices away and buy replacements. The environmental implications of this are serious. According to the United Nations, the world produces as much as [50 million tonnes of electronic and electrical waste (e-waste) a year.](https://www.unenvironment.org/news-and-stories/press-release/un-report-time-seize-opportunity-tackle-challenge-e-waste) To put that number into perspective, this waste weighs more than all of the commercial airliners ever made. Not only is this e-waste heavy, but it is also valuable, estimated to be worth over $62.5 billion annually (more than the GDP of most countries). Worst of all, only 20% of this heavy, valuable e-waste is formally recycled! ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/nMix1mvjt2LJDeLt4Ipi8/c15bae45f993dad4af48a676f2cc5fc5/image_215.png) ## Empowering sustainability But the tide is changing. [Important regulatory moves are afoot across the EU and the US](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronics_right_to_repair), which should make it easier for consumers and businesses to repair their own electrical and

articles.title: Creandum backs Twaice
articles.author: Peter Specht
articles.excerpt: The new standard for battery analytics
articles.text: # Backing Twaice - the new standard for battery analytics We're thrilled to announce that Creandum is leading the 11m€ Series A funding round of Munich-based tech company TWAICE. It's our belief that the company's predictive analytics software is tackling some of the biggest challenges encountered along the lifecycle of a mega booming market - batteries. It's common knowledge that a battery's performance declines throughout its life. But in light of today's electrification trend, it becomes even more vital to tackle and optimise lifetime, reliability and costs. Batteries underpin so many elements of modern industry - powering everything from electric cars, industrial vehicles, to energy storages or power tools and other devices. When they don't function effectively, they can increase operational costs while putting business continuity or customer happiness at risk. As businesses are increasing reliance upon battery-powered devices, it's more critical than ever to address this problem. The biggest challenge is that it's been incredibly difficult to get reliable insight into a battery's performance. Predicting a battery's state of health over its lifetime and remaining useful lifetime accurately is often an unsolved challenge. This has led to costly overstacking of battery capacity on the part of manufacturers, plus suboptimal maintenance and reuse schedules on the part of operators. Thanks to TWAICE, however, this is set to change. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/6Z83ndRqNeRuocNEuI8omS/cf84b42d9d394360233fe066561f6eeb/image_212.jpg) ## Introducing the digital twin TWAICE's innovative battery analytics software uses an intelligent ‘digital twin': a virtual simulation of the real battery. By using live field data in combination with physical and data-driven battery models, TWAICE can accurately determine the condition of the real battery - down to the cell level - and predict performance going forward. It's vital in product development but more than that opens up new opportunities such as predictive maintenance and warranty extension. ## Delivering value across the lifecycle ### Development Historically, the limited insight available into battery performance has forced manufacturers to significantly overstack them, in order to fulfil warranty requirements. Also testing today is laborious and costly, increasing the time it takes to get products to market. Through TWAICE's software testing time can be reduced, while the insight into performance is more sophisticated. This decreases both time to market and cost per unit. ### Operations TWAICE helps companies (e.g. automotive OEMs, fleet managers, energy storage companies) to bear high service costs, insurance costs or deal with warranty risks. Through their predictive maintenance solution, they can determine the exact health of the batteries they run. Operational failures can in real time be detected and prevented, lifetime increased and total costs reduced. More concrete, think of an electric vehicle fleet with batteries representing assets worth millions of $, preventing failure and increasing the lifetime through predictive maintenance represents significant $ savings. ### Second life TWAICE value goes beyond the first life of a battery. Imagine selling a battery to a new owner (e.g. pre-used vehicle) or for second life (e.g. energy storage) while the accurate state of health of the battery is often a black box. A battery that has been monitored/analysed with TWAICE solution, however, gives the full insights and enables defining a reliable residual value. It's like a car with full service history, those selling it on can offer a clear picture of its remaining capabilities, in order to maximise its residual value. ## A market at an inflection point ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/5kmqDsnKYnRJQP3SZ55EAI/0a1c43c1f91c278ec7a61ce060c9a84a/image_213.jpg) Now is the time. The underlying battery market is at an inflection point, and expected to grow between 8–10 times its size over the next 10 years. Rarely do we see such a mega-market trend and momentum. Electrification is happening, and it's a top priority for the mobility and the energy sectors. Next to the battery itself, the software stack around it will be the profiteer. It's already a bn$+ market to address today, which is growing multifold in the next years . Customer demand for the product is strong and growing organically, something we love to see in markets and companies. **An outstanding team in the battery field globally** What's more, TWAICE is a remarkable group of people. When we first met the founders Dr. Stephan Rohr and Michael Baumann about a year ago, we were instantly impressed by them and their clear ambition to build a global category-defining company in the battery analytics space. The two had spent four years of research at the Technical University of Munich, before they founded the company in 2018. In just under two years, TWAICE has executed at the highest speed and grown from a university research project into the top battery analytics software, attracting a diverse and global customer base. They've put together one of the strongest teams you'll find in the battery field, who all bring with them deep expertise in this area. Needless to say, we're very excited to support TWAICE in its journey, alongside our friends from Cherry, Speedinvest & UVC. And you could be too - TWAICE is currently looking for great people to[ join the team](https://twaice.com/career/) in Munich. Come along for the ride!

articles.title: Taking HR a step ahead
articles.author: Peter Specht
articles.excerpt: Factorial’s people data platform
articles.text: # Taking HR a step ahead - Factorial's people data platform _Today we're thrilled to share the €15m Series A round of [Factorial](https://factorialhr.com/). One of the largest A rounds ever in Spain. As an early partner (Creandum led the seed round), we're excited to continue the journey with the fantastic team that Jordi, Bernat and Pau have built. The A-round was led by US-based[ CRV](https://www.crv.com/) to further accelerate international expansion._ The HR market for SMEs is undergoing a large transition, from manual work to digitisation and partly automation. While the vast majority of SMEs are still using spreadsheets, word, paper & co., the tech-savvy ones have been starting to use different single software tools for specific core HR needs or already adopted the first generation of HR suites. That said, in the tech world it's easy to forget how incredibly manual this still is for so many companies out there. Processes that are repeated by people over and over. ### Becoming the backbone for SME's most important asset: people The challenge in HR solutions has been the right balance between feature breadth ("ticking the HR feature boxes") vs. product depth. Yet, with increasing market sophistication, we believe that SME's HR needs are more and more moving to what we see in enterprise, all-in-one suites with access to vertical depth if needed. With the caveat that high ease of use is even more important for the SME segment. To get this combination right we believe the winning HR plays need to a) transform HR software into an even more powerful platform moving more towards data-driven people insights; b) combine an all-in-one suite with best of breed options, stepping up the game for easy integration and becoming the true backbone. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/aVNFce87Vh8d1Vvq4RC9l/e511e8456887f76e44902f96cb39d825/image_210.jpg) Factorial is already making this happen and becoming a true people data platform. It's the central point of processes and insights, but more than that it enables to do better business decisions related to people. We're excited about the power and potential of this and how it will make the daily job of people managers even easier and better. ### Factorial - a stellar case of user love ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/2zGuRH2OYWe8h3FUZFmJD1/4ce16a132babc4661f0525d492707d85/image_211.jpg) When we met the Factorial team for the first time nearly 2 years ago, we were already super impressed by their product-centric thinking and love for every detail of UI/UX and prioritisation on what really matters for HR. Rarely did I come out so excited from a product demo. Ease of use has been a north star for the team from day one and continues to be so today. While many SME products lose this appeal over time when adding more features, it's fair to say that Factorial has built a product and user experience that is second to none in the HR space in Europe. Today this is reflected by super high NPS, strong engagement and very low churn from thousands of users. More than that, the word is out on the street among HR managers and most of Factorial's rapid growth is organic. While Factorial's people data platform is already serving businesses in over 40 countries, with the new funding round, the company will focus on further international expansion and "spreading the love" across the globe. We're looking forward to continuing to support Jordi, Bernat, Pau and team on their journey to build a defining company in the HR space. Want to be part of this rocket ship? Factorial is hiring, [check here](https://careers.factorialhr.com/). _Since many years Creandum has been backing solutions helping SME's to operate efficiently across several verticals and functions: Fintech (Pleo, Bokio, Tide, Billie, iZettle), Travel (Comtravo), HR/Staffing (Syft, Planday, Factorial). The largest part of adoption in SMEs is still upcoming and we continue to be strong believers of this trend._

articles.title: Jonathan Teklu joins Creandum as Venture Partner
articles.author: Simon Schmincke
articles.text: For the past decade, Jonathan Teklu has been a cornerstone of the German Startup ecosystem and one of the most prolific angel investors globally. Today, we are excited to announce that he has decided to join Creandum as Venture Partner. Jonathan is one of Germany's most distinguished angel investors, and with more than 50 portfolio companies across Europe and the US, he has built a broad network among fellow angels, entrepreneurs, and investors. Jonathan first gained entrepreneurial experience at Spreadshirt and StudiVZ - two of the first success stories of the German startup landscape. After Jonathan sold his online media company Global Leads Group, where he served as co-founder & CEO, to Holtzbrinck Digital, he co-founded the investment firm Springstar. As Managing Partner at Springstar in Berlin, he gained further operational experience in helping Airbnb start their international operations, after investing in the company. Today, Jonathan spends his time between supporting entrepreneurs within his angel investments, advising TheCollective to expand globally and developing real estate projects. Over the last nine years, Jonathan has focussed on building a broad portfolio of investments which include companies like Airbnb, Amorelie, Choco, Comtravo, DiaMonTech, One Football, Peat, Trade Republic, TheCollective, Uber and Zeitgold. The German with Ethiopian roots was elected as a Global Shaper by the World Economic Forum in 2012 and built the Berlin Hub as the founding curator. In 2016 Jonathan was featured on Forbes magazine's 30 under 30 list. We had the opportunity to work alongside Jonathan on four of his investments so far, like Comtravo and Honest Food Company, which was acquired by Delivery Hero, and we were incredibly impressed by his fast and insightful grasp of market opportunities, his risk-taking mentality, his engagement with entrepreneurs and his global mindset. As Venture Partner, Jonathan will work closely with Creandum's existing portfolio companies on scaling internationally as well as supporting the investment advisory team as a part-time member on partnering with companies of tomorrow. The whole team at Creandum is incredibly proud to be working with Jonathan over the upcoming years. Jonathan will be based out of Creandum's new Berlin office. Jonathan, we are looking forward to spending time with you. Read more on [Handelsblatt](https://www.handelsblatt.com/unternehmen/mittelstand/risikokapitalgeber-start-up-investor-creandum-macht-einen-32-jaehrigen-zum-partner/25784538.html?ticket=ST-2668766-GGVFtdTKnSffSPgBF6Y4-ap3) or [Gruenderszene](https://www.gruenderszene.de/business/jonathan-teklu-creandum?interstitial_click) (in German).

articles.title: Creandum promotes Simon Schmincke to General Partner
articles.author: Staffan Helgesson
articles.text: While we spend a lot of our time looking for the companies of tomorrow and partnering with the most ambitious founders, perhaps our most important investments are the ones we make in our team as we continue on our mission to make Creandum the premier European early-stage venture capital firm. **That's why we are very excited to announce the promotion of Simon Schmincke to General Partner.** When I got to know Simon in 2014 over dinner at his favourite Berlin Mitte restaurant (that over time became one of my favourites too), he had been in the venture capital industry for a couple of years. Before he switched to the investment side, Simon had acquired great operating and entrepreneurial experiences building three companies for Rocket Internet, such as launching Hello Fresh in the US and managing Foodpanda in Southeast Asia. In addition to being very insightful about the venture industry, I also vividly remember how excited Simon was about N26 where he had just led the seed round. This burning excitement and deep industry knowledge for a young company, its product and its founders hooked me. It's exactly the spirit you need to become a successful partner to the founders you're backing. We got to know each other over a longer period of time and in 2016, we finally became colleagues. Without hesitation, Simon and his family (thank you Caspar and Olivia!) moved to Stockholm to spend one year with the Creandum team in the dark and cold north. Over the last four years, Simon has become an integral part of the Creandum team and a strong leader in our international expansion. He has not only built our physical presence in Berlin, he is also responsible for many of our key new hires (such as [Jonathan](https://blog.creandum.com/jonathan-teklu-joins-creandum-as-venture-partner-671a102a9829), [Peter](https://blog.creandum.com/creandum-promotes-peter-specht-cbb11f21362e), [Ines, Julian and Anne](https://blog.creandum.com/creandum-expands-in-berlin-a3f3b3b9365)) and has increased the awareness of our brand in Germany. We also benefit a lot from his background as a developer. But most importantly, Simon has become a major force in the German startup ecosystem and has led some of Creandum's most important investments in the fintech, e-gaming and SaaS industries including [Taxfix](https://blog.creandum.com/backing-taxfix-the-tax-accountant-for-everyone-303b1a13ef76), [Billie](https://blog.creandum.com/billie-solving-the-sme-financing-gap-through-technology-5aa14f156358), [Tide](https://blog.creandum.com/better-business-banking-creandum-invests-in-tide-dbb661c33eb2), [RFRSH](https://blog.creandum.com/creandum-invests-in-rfrsh-6d5df134514e), and [Comtravo](https://blog.creandum.com/an-ai-for-business-travel-comtravo-closes-series-a-8d3e06165cc2). His strong personality and competence has hugely contributed to the improvement and development of our firm, making our processes smoother and constantly challenging our way of thinking. The number of discussions we have had around product vs process, execution vs design, decision-making and how to build companies have been challenging, rewarding, and lots of fun. So today, we are beyond excited to announce that Simon is promoted to General Partner at Creandum. With this move, Simon is joining the leadership of our firm as we continue to partner with the best and most ambitious entrepreneurs across Europe. As General Partner, he will work closely together with all of us to continue our mission of building the premier early-stage venture capital firm in Europe. He will continue to be based in our (newly built!) Berlin office and will work with us all to expand our team in Germany and beyond. Simon, we are looking forward to continuing the journey with you! ![100% dedication from day 0. Simon in our Berlin office before the furniture, the team and office dog arrived.](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/3v5VkTrICl3KYFMyXLCEsK/b1148436c0a2df4753fc1dac4b9d7232/image_209.jpg) Hear more from Simon in his latest [podcast with Finance Forward](https://financefwd.com/de/podcast-creandum/) (in German).

articles.title: Can I fundraise in COVID times?
articles.author: Peter Specht
articles.excerpt: The “New” Fundraising Matrix
articles.text: COVID-19 is the global black swan event in 2020 causing a lot of uncertainty in the startup funding market. Rounds have slowed down for several reasons such as heightened economic uncertainty, reduced business for companies causing depressed revenues, the inability of funds and entrepreneurs to meet in person, and the increased focus of VCs on their existing portfolio companies. Questions such as "can I raise currently?," and "how will COVID impact fundraising?" have been ubiquitous when talking to early stage founders in the past few weeks. In an attempt to respond to those questions and illustrate the current fundraising market, I've created the below matrix to classify companies that are raising in this new environment. To keep it simple, the x-axis classifies companies from "solid" to "very strong" with reference to metrics (growth, retention, unit economics etc.) and opportunity (need, market size, team etc). Intentionally, I left out a fourth x-axis column of "bad" as I don't expect bad opportunities to get funded in either the current or the past environment. The y-axis refers to the impact of COVID-19 on growth and has been segmented into bad (negative growth, e.g. travel startups), neutral (same or reduced growth, but still growing) and positive (significantly accelerated growth, e.g. digital health, remote collaboration, communication etc. - think of Zoom Video). In a nutshell, I assert that new allocations of capital are being and will continue to primarily be allocated to the rockets, racers and stars. The "best" companies will continue to be sought after, yet _simply_ being "strong" or "solid" will often not be enough to raise externally anymore. The bar has been raised. ## The new reality of the crisis: a taxonomy ### Positive: COVID beneficiaries Rocket: A star before the crisis and currently receiving a massive tailwind from Corona. Revenue/users have grown like crazy in the past weeks, the outlook is very strong and inbound is on fire. It's what every VC is looking for. Rounds for rockets will soar. Racer: Increased product-market fit (PMF) and accelerated growth suddenly make the racer "hot". While the Racer was on the radar for many VCs beforehand, it suddenly became a high priority. Lucky Shot: In the past only existed on the edge of most VCs' fields of vision, but are now in a more fortunate position. Yet as capital concentrates on the best segments, the lucky shot's ability to raise its' next round will remain uncertain. ### Neutral / limited negative impacted Star: While the coronavirus spread might have slowed down, the Star's growth, the fundamental opportunity and the business are still outstanding. Funds recognise this and Stars will continue to be sought after. However, while valuations for Stars were at peak levels prior to Corona, they'll be slightly lower today (-10–15%) impacted by decelerated growth and the general uncertainty on development until the next funding round. Milky Way: One out of many. Slowed-downed momentum and a gloomier investor sentiment make it more challenging to raise, round size and valuation will be impacted (-20% and more). Ghost: Hard to get attention and ghosts will be avoided by investors. While there was a solid chance for the ghost pre-COVID, it almost diminished. ### Bad: very negative impacted Boomerang: They'll come back. They used to be stars before the crisis, but the global lockdown hit the company's segment in particular. While revenue slumped in the short term, the opportunity is there and the Boomerangs will return. Wait for the bounce-back or raise from existing investors, who might be eager to increase ownership. Shark: Strong history but at risk of extinction. Hopefully, existing investors on board have high conviction and continue to keep sharks alive. An external fundraise will be challenging. Zombie: Won't be able to raise these days, both externally or internally. Also prior to COVID, it would have been challenging to attract external capital. ## Pointers on improving fundraising chances The fundraising environment has switched wholesale from being a seller's market to a buyer's market with the balance of power recently being more to the investors' side. Except for rockets and the most popular racers and stars, which will continue to be a seller's market. A couple of pointers that can help improve your fundraising chances: - Previous physical meeting: During current travel restrictions, some investors struggle to get to conviction without meeting teams in person. Having met in the past increases likelihood. Make sure to ping VCs that you've met in person in the past. - Strengthen personal relationships (also virtually): it's common practice that VCs and entrepreneurs get to know each other even before a fundraising process ("have a coffee") and try to build relationships. This becomes even more important today. When communication is limited to video and messages it takes more time to build up trust and a personal connection. Find ways to do this virtually (update mails, video catch-ups). - Be realistic: Investors appetite for outsized rounds and valuations has decreased (unless you are a rocket or racer). If you are overly ambitious in your funding size goals it can backfire and VCs might decline. You don't want to return a couple of weeks later saying that you are raising less. The hurdle to make a VC reconsider within a couple of weeks is much higher than convincing them the first time. It is better to be humble from the start and if you have multiple term-sheets you can then optimise and negotiate on round size and valuation. For general fundraising tactics, I've written another post a few months back on[ how to raise your next round](https://blog.creandum.com/how-to-raise-your-next-funding-round-7e6bd2e027e2). _If you are a rocket_ _, racer_ _or star_ _, I'd love to hear from you. Do ping me via mail (email handle is my first name) or twitter (@[ specht.p](https://twitter.com/specht_p)). & Stay safe and heal

articles.title: Beyond the Uterus
articles.excerpt: The Next Wave of Femtech
articles.text: _Co-authored by [Sanna Westman](https://blog.creandum.com/@sanna_3506)_ During its relatively short life-span, the term **"Femtech"** has created a lot of noise. Famously coined in 2016 by Clue founder Ida Tin the term has sparked some controversy. While some [argue that it is a sexist category](https://qz.com/1586815/why-femtech-is-a-sexist-category/), others welcome [that investments in female health](https://www.theguardian.com/business/2019/jun/06/femtech-startups-womens-health-investors) are finally in the spotlight. But perhaps it is not a dichotomy, perhaps Femtech has been (and still is) an excellent greenhouse for startups who do not only shed light on important societal issues but actually work proactively to decrease them. At Creandum, we strongly believe the Femtech journey is still in its adolescence and ahead of us, there is a mature, more encompassing, version - a Femtech beyond the uterus. ## Why Femtech needs a renaissance Let's face it - the term Femtech today is limited - on average it is only 7.3 cm long, 4.5 cm broad, and 3.0 cm thick. The heavy focus on the female uterus demonstrates how small the Femtech landscape is today. Of course, the solutions targeting female health issues come in many different shapes and forms; [pelvic floor trainers](https://www.elvie.com/), [cooling bracelets for hot flashes](https://www.gracecooling.com/), or [tracking apps for ovulation](https://helloclue.com/) and while important in their niche, the focus is still mostly on the female mid-region. ![To be noted: Many of the companies (e.g. Clue, Natural Cycles, and Inne) are transitioning into later stages too](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/4tb0fXO4CAkwMnwNpHWnau/2f8c8e1dc137da52601f35e5bf3f6cff/image_205.jpg) Unsurprisingly though, sexual well-being and reproductive health are not the only issues women face in their day-to-day lives. Take driving for example: Although, in general, females are considered safer drivers, women are [47% more likely to be seriously injured](https://crashstats.nhtsa.dot.gov/Api/Public/ViewPublication/811766) during a car crash. Some say this is simply due to the female body being more "fragile", but surely a smarter designed car should be able to account for this. Electronics, such as [smartphones or earpods](https://www.independent.co.uk/life-style/women/apple-iphone-xs-max-new-too-big-size-women-sexist-feminist-a8537171.html), are made using the "standard US man" as a reference - not great news for women either. In the medical space, several diseases we know very little about affect women to a larger extent than men; women are [3x more likely to get migraine](https://medlineplus.gov/migraine.html#cat_79), and [75% of all autoimmune patients are women](https://www.aarda.org/who-we-help/patients/women-and-autoimmunity/), just to name a few examples. Even the drugs we eat are [mostly tested on male mice](https://www.theguardian.com/science/2019/may/31/sexist-research-means-drugs-more-tailored-to-men-says-scientist) as female rodents are presumed to be more variable, in part due to oestrous cyclicity. At the same time, these drugs then go out to the market being used by - you guessed right - human females with oestrous cyclicity. ## The next wave of Femtech As the Femtech space is maturing, we are looking at the female body and mind with a more holistic approach, including areas that were not top of mind when the space was mostly about periods. Infant nutrition, egg freezing, and menopause health are all parts of solving a dire need for women who want to live life on their own terms. Transitioning along this path, what are some other solutions we might come across? The intersection between the needs highlighted by Femtech and a broader set of issues, such as flaws within design and medicine (as mentioned before), really spark our interest. We think Femtech is beginning to evolve into a different shape and form. ![ = A growing new wave of Femtech](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/3XQwuBWPT00Jh1vczmRvUl/6ad2eb8efa1fa4a20e5370dbc7cfe522/image_206.jpg) For this new wave of Femtech there will be plenty of innovation happening. Firstly, on the structural level to set biases from the past straight (which in itself will be a breeding ground for very big companies). Secondly, on the experience level where there will be another set of companies who make less profound changes but instead create significantly better products for all, thanks to their deep understanding of _everybody's_ needs - not only men's (hint from [Pauliina Martikainen](https://www.linkedin.com/in/pauliina-martikainen/?originalSubdomain=fi) to the company [Oura](https://ouraring.com/) which seems to have a little way left to [embrace this perspective](https://sifted.eu/articles/femtech-healthtech-mentech/)). While there is still a lot of white space for innovation to happen, we are already seeing some concrete examples of companies who might not label themselves as Femtech but are a part of this wave, such as: - [Kardia](https://www.alivecor.com/) is a solution developed by AliveCor which lets users take a medical EKG at all times. As of today, they have recorded 60 Million EKGs worldwide. They are not only letting patients take the health journey into their own hands but they are also contributing to broadening cardiovascular data for women - [an area today skewed towards men](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/30939754). - [Organise](https://www.organise.org.uk/), the social network that helps employees source better working conditions, pay, and more flexibility around commitments such as caring and childcare. Obviously not a company only marketed towards females, but where a large portion of the users benefiting from the solution will be women. - Another social network, [Chief](https://www.chief.com/), which just recently [raised $15 million](https://techcrunch.com/2020/05/21/chief-the-leadership-network-for-women-raises-15-million-in-funding/) in funding. They are tackling some of the mo

articles.title: The future of work is here
articles.excerpt: But something is missing
articles.text: ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/3doxyhIhCLycmjShvCK5hX/2647559e45024b88070b2fe2a970f998/image_201.jpg) Early March, I wrote the message above to my team on Slack. Since then, more and more companies have [announced that they will continue to allow people to work from home](https://www.forbes.com/sites/jackkelly/2020/05/24/the-work-from-home-revolution-is-quickly-gaining-momentum/#76fc1a5d1848). It's inevitable: remote working is here to stay. Period. Whether it will be a hybrid or a 100% model, time will tell. But certainly, very few companies will be left working 100% on site. However, to adapt to today's new normal of remote working and turn it into a fully-established work concept, the human race now faces a massive structural change. I'm not surprised to see an ocean of tools popping up, aimed at facilitating and improving this shift to remote working. They cover the whole gamut of tech, from chat services and voice tools, to virtual whiteboards and collaboration tools. All useful, but are they really giving us what we need? ## The benefits of the physical office Don't get me wrong: remote working is fantastic in many ways and I personally appreciate it a lot. Yet, I feel we're missing something. Let's take a moment to think about what the physical office provides when it's working at its best. - **The mindset shift**. Changing locations between home and the office helps your mind to shift focus, from "relax mode" to "work mode". The ritual of the commute - no matter how short - essentially helps your brain to prepare for the act of working. What's more, it also works in reverse, physically leaving work helps us to mentally leave work behind, at least in part. Like it or not, but rest is needed. - **Informal mentoring and coaching**. The office space allows for informal chats and small questions in between meetings. These short exchanges between team members are important to build an environment of trust, safety and transparency, but in the world of remote working, they're typically not important enough to call for a virtual meeting. - **Appreciation, friendship, networking and inclusiveness**. Those who've met lifelong friends and invaluable mentors in the workplace know that the constant stream of office communication, both verbal and non-verbal, builds rapport amongst employees. "_I don't care how much you know, until I know how much you care"_ is very true. Regardless of how professional we are, human beings have a need to feel appreciated, to experience belonging and be part of the group and not solely work on a transactional basis. Physical presence also makes networks more visible, enabling a better understanding how to get work done. - **Mental health reality check.** The standard answer for "how are you?" is "good". Hard to tell if that's true when you only see someone for 30 minutes per week on a Zoom call. Easier to tell if you see your colleagues every day, all (work)day long (unless empathy is an alien concept to you). No one is feeling 100% good, 100% of the time. But that's harder to see or voice from behind a screen - **Serendipity - the chance meetings**. How many problems have not been solved following a chat around the coffee machine? Or new initiatives being spurred from randomly bumping into someone in the hall? That unexpected encounter can bring about a valuable lead, an introduction, or the spark for the next project. Perhaps it's because I'm mainly raised in the land of the 3 o'clock _Fika_ (Many Swedish companies still have a communal coffee break at either 10 am or 3 pm), but I'm a firm believer that a few informal chats in between meetings create just as much value as all the workshops, webinars and pulse surveys you care to schedule in. Unfortunately, very few of the remote tools I've seen so far fully address the above and instead aim directly at facilitating communication or direct collaboration. ## The struggle is real... [There](https://toggl.com/out-of-office-remote-company-culture/) is more to building a successful team and company than hardcore collaboration and work-related communication. Strong relationships are a prerequisites for successful collaboration. Some companies overcome this by being very diligent in creating processes and adhering to them (some good advice here). However, for many companies it remains a big challenge, and leads to many [employees feeling left ou](https://hbr.org/2017/11/a-study-of-1100-employees-found-that-remote-workers-feel-shunned-and-left-out)t. In fact, the majority of struggles remote workers are facing are rather mental/social than communication aspect. This challenge is likely even bigger for companies with a hybrid work model, which I personally believe will be the most common set-up going forward. ![Top struggles of remote workers: Communication is only one of the main struggles - topics related to psychological needs accounts for an even larger share](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/3NceyMEKgy7yNcTz6KD03R/d7d9556cd947ba30980906243fbfab7a/image_202.png) ## We're still humans after all I would love to see more tech solutions being designed to help companies foster a sound working environment and a strong culture, regardless of office set-up. Not only will this help people to feel better, but ultimately, it will enable the company to do better work. Think of it as Maslow's hierarchy of needs: ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/5r5HTJWTVTXmP0i9lsK2hT/a3afe4b6b17e6ecbba16f3b7de4b93e0/image_203.png) **Basic Needs - physiological and safety needs**: The home office provides us the warm shelter we need to feel comfortable (as long as we have decent wifi!). We've also got food and water covered; but the tricky part that remains is the "rest" element: in theory you could take a nap anytime, but few do. In reality, a lot of home workers [struggle to mentally logging off](https://www.visualcapitalist.com/how-people-and-companies-feel-about-working-remotely/) from work because they are in fact constantl

articles.title: Disrupting the productivity stack
articles.author: Peter Specht
articles.excerpt: Why we backed Amie
articles.text: # Disrupting the productivity stack - why we backed Amie Remember the old days when you used to manage your day structure in a completely analogue way? Today Google, Apple and many standalone apps tried to mirror the offline experience for all the different tasks - in many different tools: One app for your calendar, a separate one for to-do lists, and a third one for note-taking etc. Comprehensive tools individually, but with too much friction from switching in between apps and inefficiencies in their workflows (think how many clicks you need to open a Zoom call from your calendar). Despite many tools out there, the market still lacks the next generation of calendar + task management. ### The smallest unit: Everything is a to-do. ![Insight from Amie's initial pitch: everything is a to-do](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/1TcdQoTSZP7AyxjQKePjv4/2fa5aa24215ecf96cea53a016bb1c10d/image_199.png) A couple of insights and beliefs have been instrumental for our excitement and hypothesis for Amie ([amie.so](http://amie.so/)): - **Everything is a to-do**: When you think about your productive day, it's fair to say that if you break your time spent down to the micro level, everything is a to-do. And every to-do is a unit of time, the time we need to spend on accomplishing it. - **To-dos need to be scheduled:** If you look at the research, the probability that a task will be completed is much greater if you assign the task to a specific time and day than if it is only on a list. If you look at habits today, many people already block time for to-dos in their calendars. The challenge is to manage to get your long list of tasks into your schedule in an easy way. - **Calendar is the right entry point:** There are different entry points to productivity, such as email, notes, to-dos and calendar. We believe calendar, actually **the fusion of calendar & to-do** is the right entry point for creating a super app in the productivity space. - **UX, UX, UX:** a) Workflows need to feel intuitive and be seamless across devices b) an application needs to be super fast (people want to feel speed while being productive, think Superhuman) c) an app that people will love needs to have super high standards of design and ease of use. **Amie - the joyful productivity app.** Amie is building a productivity software that combines calendar and to-dos in one place in a seamless and efficient way. It's designed to "work like you think" and provide fast and natural experience across all devices, be it with a few taps on your smartphone (tap, tap, ta-da) or efficient shortcuts on your desktop. The experience is aimed to be intuitive and with a joyful touch. Some sneak peak on the product below + you can find more on amie.so ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/3lv67A87RAUC87fZvbisqh/5c7351a2668657999e412c9258f5f604/image_200.png) **The youngest entrepreneur Creandum backed** When I met Dennis the first time, you could instantly feel his 120% (or probably 200%) passion, dedication, and entrepreneurial DNA. He just came back from a hideout in a quiet place in Cape Town, where he isolated for a few months to develop his idea, to start building the prototype and to come up with a larger vision for Amie. Spending more time with Dennis, we were very impressed by his product and user-centric thinking, his level of execution and thoughtfulness around building up a progressive company with high focus on team culture and employee incentivization at heart. Prior to Amie, Dennis was a product manager @ N26 and has an engineering background (and comes with an obsession for design). 23 years old, he's also the youngest founder we ever backed. Interesting side note: previously, the youngest founder Creandum had invested in was Daniel Ek (Spotify) who was 25 at the time Creandum co-led his seed round. We're extremely excited to announce that Creandum is leading Amie's pre-seed round, to further fuel the development and growth (and to secure a spot high up on the product's waitlist ). Also we're happy to have several amazing angels from N26, Spotify, Sennder, Chime, Dubsmash & more on board in this round. If you want to be part of this journey A) Amie is hiring (in particular engineering and design roles - [check it out here](https://amie.so/#work-with-us)) B) Secure your early spot on [the waitlist](https://amie.so/#get-amie) and make sure to invite your friends.

articles.title: Creandum backs Meditopia
articles.author: Carl Fritjofsson
articles.excerpt: Bringing mindfulness across the world
articles.text: The past era of consumer internet provided users with an endless ability to connect with others with social media at the core of this. These platforms create immense value for its users, but as 3.8B people seek social validation from each other we create a very externally focused life centered around comparison to others which can be very destructive. As much as this is the fault of technology, we firmly believe the same can offer a remedy. A new breed of consumer internet companies are right now being created which rather than looking outside towards others help users focus on themselves to understand their own mind, find inner peace, and discover the true nature of their own consciousness. ## Meet Meditopia. We got to know [Meditopia](http://meditopia.com) in 2018 when 3 guys out of Istanbul, Turkey explained to us there was a global demand for mindfulness and mental training. I had already personally followed the mindfulness market closely, due to in 2014 I got lucky enough to invest in [Calm.com](http://calm.com) via [Jason Calacanis](https://calacanis.com/) AngelList syndicate. But Meditopia explained to us how this market required careful cultural adaptation to serve different cultures and countries. That's why from the beginning, Meditopia has had localization at the core of their product development. Today 14M users users across 75 countries use Meditopia to access culturally localized relaxation practices using meditation and breathing exercises, multi-day mindfulness challenges, sleep stories, and much more. Compared to other mindfulness products, Meditopia offers a _deeper_ experience around personal transformation, which caters to users who want to explore what's beyond entry-level relaxation, and Meditopia is already the number one mindfulness product in markets like Brazil, Turkey, Japan, Russia, Latam, and more. ![Discover happiness from within using [Meditopia](http://meditopia.com).](https://miro.medium.com/1*ymCQqNgtVUq47ASkMsqz0A.png) It's been an incredible privilege to follow the Meditopia team for the past two years and it's fair to say that this is one of the most capital-efficient run companies we've ever seen. In today's uncertain economy, seeing founders who understand and manage their unit economics to the depth this team does, while also enjoying hockey stick growth, is true bliss. Furthermore, every time we've interacted with [Fatih](https://www.linkedin.com/in/fatih-mustafa-%C3%A7elebi-b0bb38100/), [Berk](https://www.linkedin.com/in/berk-yilmaz-09252338/), and [Ali](https://www.linkedin.com/in/alimuratceylan/) they have over-delivered against what they promised which further strengthens our excitement for the team. Hence, we couldn't be more excited today to announce that together with our friends from [Highland Europe](https://www.highlandeurope.com/), Creandum is leading Meditopia's $15m Series A round. Training your mind is becoming as essential as training your physical body, and we believe Meditopia will be one of the most important products in the world in making that happen. <iframe src="https://cdn.embedly.com/widgets/media.html?src=https%3A%2F%2Fgiphy.com%2Fembed%2FH7kfFDvD9HSYGRbvid%2Ftwitter%2Fiframe&display_name=Giphy&url=https%3A%2F%2Fgiphy.com%2Fgifs%2Fmoodman-meditation-zen-meditate-H7kfFDvD9HSYGRbvid&image=https%3A%2F%2Fmedia2.giphy.com%2Fmedia%2Fv1.Y2lkPTc5MGI3NjExMzg2MWZkMTVmY2Q4MzMxMTU0ZTVjNWZjNWQ5MDI1ZWFmNGFjMTU3NCZjdD1n%2FH7kfFDvD9HSYGRbvid%2Fgiphy.gif&key=a19fcc184b9711e1b4764040d3dc5c07&type=text%2Fhtml&schema=giphy" title="" height="288" width="435"></iframe>

articles.title: A Small Sign of Progress on Gender Diversity in Tech
articles.author: Carl Fritjofsson
articles.text: Two years ago [Creandum](http://creandum.com) started to actively measure gender diversity inside the funds' portfolio, on the premise that what gets measured gets done. We have ever since then publicly reported our **Creandum Gender Diversity Index** ([2018](https://hackernoon.com/diversity-inside-european-vc-more-work-needed-c545353b7e4c) + [2019](https://blog.creandum.com/diversity-inside-european-vc-2-0-limited-progress-made-f89479fe3738)). Here are the results for 2020, and although the balance is still male-dominated we do see some signs of progress. ## A reminder of why diversity matters. If anyone is still questioning why we care about this, it's simply because of performance. We aspire to make the Creandum funds' portfolio as successful as it possibly can be, and diversity plays a key role in that. There are countless studies on the topic and as an example, [BCG and MassChallenge](https://www.bcg.com/publications/2018/why-women-owned-startups-are-better-bet.aspx) found that companies with a woman on the founding team delivered twice as much revenue per dollar invested than those companies run solely by men. Equally important, a lack of diversity limits the problems that the ecosystem solves for. Founders address problems that concern them directly, and talent gravitates towards companies whose products excite them. Although the impact of diversity on a company's performance and problem-solving skills seems to be common knowledge in the tech scene, the problem remains entrenched, as numerous reports, such as [Slush's recent "Entrepreneurship refined" whitepaper](https://www.slush.org/entrepreneurship-redefined/) points out. However, through the eyes of the Creandum funds' portfolio, there's a silver lining on the horizon. ## Methodology. Our Creandum Diversity Index is focusing specifically on gender. The impact of gender on startups is the most researched axis of diversity, and that data remains insufficient on most others. When we started this initiative two years ago, we agreed on rather doubling down our efforts on this specific topic, instead of covering the entire range with less vigour. Each year, we send a poll to the portfolio company CEOs measuring the number of women across 3 dimensions in their respective organizations: 1. across the whole organization 2. on the management team 3. on the board In addition to this, for the first time, we also added a 4th data point related to compensation and the pay gap between the genders. In total, this year we surveyed 54 portfolio companies of which 51 responded. ## The results. ### 1. Whole Organisation: 40 % (+4 %) This year, the Creandum funds' active portfolio employee count more than doubled (!) to a total number of 7728. Almost 40% of those are female, lifting the percentage up by 4 points compared to last year. Even more compelling: Comparing to the [change from 2018 to 2019](https://blog.creandum.com/diversity-inside-european-vc-2-0-limited-progress-made-f89479fe3738), the increase quadrupled! Overall we think this is a great trend. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/3i48QX62TEJkXElx8Tn6Iv/d481a25419ffb8ee0d291fce00551a50/image_191.png) Looking deeper at the firms we already measured in 2019, 23 of them increased their female/male ratio while only 6 reversed it. ![2010 to 2020 year-over-year change in female-to-male ratio, arranged by headcount.](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/2I4BdTWIkkHE7hTM7clhrJ/3c5ade1b1099756d75cbd3b739ccc38e/image_192.jpg) Out of the 51 portfolio companies in this study, 20% have hired an equal amount or even more women than men. Nevertheless, only half of the funds' portfolio companies have managed to fill one-third of their jobs with women. And sadly, almost 25% of the portfolio companies have staffed less than a quarter of their positions with women. Focusing on the twelve new early-stage companies that joined us within the past year, sadly, the average amount of females in those firms is only close to 30%, 10 points below the average across the portfolio. This low number is heavily connected to our data insight, that the bigger a company gets in terms of headcount, the more it's focused on gender equality across the entire company. While ventures with less than 100 employees count only 33% of females on average, companies with more than 100 employees reach an average of 40%. ![Distribution of men and women (in %) across the funds' portfolio arranged by headcount.](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/3vggde7NE57BqBM0ygqQ8b/5e3845e51821b1ef7047d9e1be4dc54b/image_193.jpg) Comparing the different industries we invest in, it's striking to see that digital health companies score way above the average, with each around 60% females. No matter if offline or online, healthcare seems to be predominantly a female-led industry. ### 2. Women in Management: 31% (+8%) On average, there are 31% of females in management positions across the portfolio. Again, comparing it to last year's increase, the number quadrupled, from a 2 % increase to 8 %! This is also a strong sign of progress, although we still see less than 1 out of 3 female leaders in the Creandum funds' portfolio. ![Total % of women in management positions across the portfolio companies.](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/7icZonJK44rrJVtXMGkyBx/5204687017017af604f66ef3539eb19b/image_194.png) Almost half of the fund's portfolio companies (48%) have at least a quarter of their management team made up of women, 22% have a third. And 8% of the fund's portfolio has more than half women in management. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/7eW2LwMEGnuZQ5egMet9Dl/8f2abfe4f96dfaae2620c6935c55c7dc/image_195.png) This is one of the most important metrics, as women in management serve as role models and heavily influence the total amount of women in the company. The data demonstrates that if the management team is at least 33% female, on average, organizations have a much higher likelihood of creating gender balance across the wider team. Even when o

articles.title: Introducing Creandum’s Diversity Knowledge Bank
articles.author: Carl Fritjofsson
articles.text: [The strongest companies we see have founders who can challenge one another](https://blog.creandum.com/10-years-later-getting-to-know-spotify-before-series-a-2279e7e54be0), but to do so requires different perspectives. In short, **diversity drives better decision-making, which in turn builds better companies**. There's a great wave of female and under-represented founders emerging, but still, they constitute just a small proportion. The same goes for engineers and, unfortunately, also venture capital firms. [Data from our annual diversity index](https://blog.creandum.com/a-small-sign-of-progress-on-gender-diversity-in-tech-915c85ac9221) indicate that there is progress across the gender dimension, but the trend is moving slowly. The reason is simply that this is a multifaceted, complex topic with no quick solutions, nor silver bullets. As a VC with a global platform backing a range of different industries, **at [Creandum](http://creandum.com) we're well aware of our responsibility and power to help drive the diversity agenda in the tech industry**. We are already pushing the subject in the board room, with the hope that by making diversity a topic of continuous discussion and monitoring, we see change happen. But we've also learned many times that companies feel a bit helpless. ## Introducing Creandum's Diversity Knowledge Bank In order to provide our companies and the tech ecosystem at large with some practical resources, **we have collected best practices, tools, and general thoughts on how to promote and foster diversity and inclusion in their businesses.** These are all documented in [Creandum's Diversity Knowledge Bank](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/u/3/d/1M45fB1cJwLQJa8M6jwXHIaQts6iLXqwWaf57wqGTnHU/edit#gid=1022305167). This knowledge bank is meant to be used by anyone leading, working, or investing in technology companies. It's an action-driven resource bank to help any kind of tech company or VC tackle common diversity challenges such as reducing bias, implementing a diverse hiring strategy, or measuring inclusion. The list is divided into different categories: - **Hiring:** An extensive list of best practices in strategic talent sourcing, including a collection of great tools, resources, and recruitment companies. - **Organizational Management:** Best practices and tool recommendations to properly implement diversity strategies in your organization such as how to manage unconscious bias, create a code of conduct, or track diversity metrics. - **Communities:** A long list of relevant communities and organizations to partner with, sponsor, or use for talent sourcing. - **Diversity in VCs:** This list includes tips to increase diversity in the deal flow process, as well as secure more inclusive post-investment strategies. On top of that comes a list of companies and initiatives for VCs to partner with. The **[Creandum Diversity Knowledge Bank](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1M45fB1cJwLQJa8M6jwXHIaQts6iLXqwWaf57wqGTnHU/edit#gid=1022305167)** has been designed to move on from the theory and warm words to something more tangible and hopefully equip tech companies, as well as venture capital firms with the practical skills and tools required to build a more diverse tech scene. ## A living resource This knowledge bank is not an exhaustive list and there's still a lot of room for improvement, including the addition of more content and categories. **It's intended to be a living resource for founders and VCs to continue to add to as they create and discover new answers to the issue of diversity.** Naturally, we don't believe a spreadsheet with URLs is the solution to our industry's diversity challenges, but we see this as one of many initiatives we can provide to help push this topic forward. We hope [Creandum's Diversity Knowledge Bank](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1M45fB1cJwLQJa8M6jwXHIaQts6iLXqwWaf57wqGTnHU/edit#gid=1022305167) gives companies a head start in becoming more diverse and inclusive, and fosters our industry's collective understanding of how we can bring about continuous, positive change. Technology has managed to solve some of the world's biggest problems, and it won't stop here. We're convinced that, together, we can begin to look at diversity in a new light and make our industry more inclusive, but we all need to roll up our sleeves and work long-term on this. **There's more to be done!** We are constantly looking for more content to add to this knowledge bank. For submissions, please send an email to [diversity@creandum.com](mailto:diversity@creandum.com). <iframe src="https://cdn.embedly.com/widgets/media.html?src=https%3A%2F%2Fgiphy.com%2Fembed%2FkHZ3KNTkHzg9VzqtQ2%2Ftwitter%2Fiframe&display_name=Giphy&url=https%3A%2F%2Fgiphy.com%2Fgifs%2FIntoAction-kHZ3KNTkHzg9VzqtQ2&image=https%3A%2F%2Fmedia3.giphy.com%2Fmedia%2FkHZ3KNTkHzg9VzqtQ2%2Fgiphy.gif&key=a19fcc184b9711e1b4764040d3dc5c07&type=text%2Fhtml&schema=giphy" title="" height="435" width="435"></iframe>

articles.title: Creandum backs Swan
articles.author: Simon Schmincke
articles.excerpt: Banking as a service without the regulatory hustle
articles.text: It is extremely difficult and expensive for non-fintech companies to include financial products as part of their value chain. While banking infrastructure layers have been around for years, working with these is still costly, tedious and requires months of work to overcome regulatory hurdles. As a consequence, embedded financial services have been limited to companies that could dedicate vast resources to these projects. This is the reason why banking products tremendously lacked innovation. Introducing [Swan](https://www.swan.io/) -providing banking infrastructure and compliance as a service, so that every tech company can offer financial products in minutes, rather than months. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/7qzYciZgMxVcQVZT5TloDu/60b1b78bba28d7f282b9a6b0ea2a70ec/image_188.jpg) ### The status quo - Digitisation of basic financial services as a product The first generation of payment fintechs have made a quantum leap in digitalisation, customer experience and price, while remaining very close to the incumbent banks in terms of value proposition. With such simple banking products, today's consumers are used to handling multiple accounts at the same time, and basic banking services are increasingly being commoditised. Nevertheless, it's the same companies (banks) offering the same products (accounts, cards and lending) just in a much simpler, cleaner and often cheaper way. ### The future - Making basic financial services a feature _**Our hypothesis:** We believe that the commoditisation of financial services has just started and that in the future, financial services, rather than being offered as a standalone product, will become features of larger-value propositions, embedded in applications' existing user interfaces._ We believe that every tech company should be able to offer financial services without needing to rush to become a fintech. This means that companies will continue to focus on their core offering, using the regulatory shield, technology and security of specialised providers like Swan. ### Swan - Full service and offering, without the hustle. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/4nyN0GqzJ3q7sMny3vMqLx/fca97467f14e40d53724afea24055b09/image_189.jpg) Swan offers the first fully productised Banking as a service solution, accesible on the go via an API. For their customers, that means - **Regulation**: Swan puts down their regulatory framework, so that partners don't need to be approved by the regulator - **Banking operations**: A client interface handling customer support and requests, money and transaction management, issuing of physical and virtual cards, .. - **Security**: Customer authentication, fraud detection, KYC and KYB, .. **...all through their own APIs. No service, no manual interactions, no project management required - done in minutes.** ### The benefits - More value for customers, more revenue for companies The use cases for tech companies are vast and include: - Enabling users of a SaaS business to distribute payments directly from the software; - Offering marketplaces the chance to hold money directly on the platform; and - Enabling platforms to offer joint accounts, split costs equally or even start loyalty card programs. Offering such services can be transformational and increase engagement, loyalty and retention for smaller and medium-sized businesses. It enables a company to capture incremental revenues (e.g. cross-sell without extra acquisition), creates additional value for the end-customers (through new use cases) and thereby ultimately allows it to compete with larger platforms that, up until now, were only able to offer such services because they had access to endless resources to implement them. ### A founding team with a history of payment expertise It's rare that you meet someone with as much payment expertise as [Nicolas](https://www.linkedin.com/in/nicolasbenady/), who worked in payment for more than 13 years and co-founded two successful payment startups, _[Limonetik](https://www.limonetik.com/)_ and _[Antelop](https://www.antelop-solutions.com/)_. It's even rarer that a [Nicolas](https://www.linkedin.com/in/nicolas-saison-7501563b/) partners up with a second Nicolas, who, later on in the process, turned out to be a previous apprentice of the former during his time at Limonetik, and subsequently gained more payment experience working at _[Payboost](https://www.payboost.com/)._ Adding the technical expertise of [Mathieu](https://www.linkedin.com/in/matbreton/), who worked as a lead developer at [Xebia](https://xebia.com/) and is a co-founder of [JS-Republic](http://www.js-republic.com/), to the payment expertise of the Nicolases made us ultimately fall in love with the team. We are super excited to work with them on transforming the financial services landscape, and there's a chance for you to work with them, too. SWAN is hiring in Paris and the EU. Read more about it in [English](https://techcrunch.com/2020/09/15/bank-as-a-service-startup-swan-helps-other-companies-issue-cards-accounts-and-ibans/) and in [German](https://financefwd.com/de/swan-funding/).

articles.title: Transitioning To a Distributed Organization
articles.author: Carl Fritjofsson
articles.text: Let's face it, distributed teams...or remote...or virtual...whatever you want to call them, are here to stay. C19 kicked us all in the butt and there's no turning back. Some companies were lucky and had already adapted to either a fully distributed setup or a hybrid one, but right now, across the board, companies are trying to wrap their heads around how to transition into this new world, where the team and work primarily have an online presence, and physical, face-to-face engagement is much rarer. Naturally, the [Creandum funds](http://creandum.com)' [portfolio](http://creandum.com/portfolio) is going through the same thing, and recently we held a joint discussion with 20+ founders, in which we all shared our learnings and experiences, and exchanged best practices relating to this. The following is a summary of this discussion, which we think many companies will be able to benefit from. ## Think online-first. No matter if you're operating 100% or partially distributed, or even if there is only a handful of team members who work from home, you have to think online-first. **Software is your office**, **not the physical building some of you might be sitting in** or where the physical post is mailed to. Inclusivity is the key to building a strong company culture, no matter the location. Utilize the advantages of the always-on internet to overcome geographical or time-related distances. A few virtual office tips to pass on to your team: - Transparency is important: Encourage conversations in open channels, so anyone can follow them and stay on top of everything that is going on. - Similarly, discourage private messages (unless it's really private). - In a virtual meeting, require individual participation even for those in the physical office - meaning everyone should log in with their own camera instead of sitting in one room with several people behind one camera - it creates an unnecessary distance to team members who are not in the office. ## Document everything. In a remote setting, likely working across different time zones, **asynchronous communication is the norm**. To overcome this challenge, documentation is essential and you need to assign new importance to the written word. All knowledge, processes, workflows, as well as discussions and decisions, should be put on (virtual) paper, no matter if kept in Favro, Google Docs, Notion, Airtable, GitHub - you name it. Discourage internal email communication as that creates silos. Instead, default to documenting everything in open destinations that anyone can access through a URL. Further, video/audio-record all important meetings, and transcribe them, so people can skim the content quickly if they couldn't attend. There are many tools out there to help automate this. The tacit knowledge this is generated in meetings, but then oftentimes lost, can be one of your organization's most valuable assets. ## The all-hands game show host. As a leader, you know how essential it is to bring the right energy into a meeting, but **transmitting this energy virtually is _much_ harder**. This is especially critical for the all-hands meetings where the core purpose is to rally your troops. Hence, you need to dial-up your enthusiasm by 3x to ensure the energy transcends the cameras. If you're the leader of the meeting, think of yourself as a game show host. Disregard your self-respect for the moment, get the humor out, and play the game. Engage the audience and have different teams present the topics they are working on. People pay more attention when there is a frequent change of speaker, so use different people to present and create natural sections that start and end within a meeting. In addition, make sure to invite more-junior team members to present, in order to ensure that a larger share of the organization feels ownership for the meeting. If the meeting is long, consider activating the participants by doing physical exercises such as warm-ups, collective breathing, etc. ## Foster non-work-related communication. Naturally, most of the communicating at work with co-workers is about the work which needs to be done. However, building social bonds and **knowing the human being behind your colleague's role is key to building trust** and eventually efficiencies within teams. Hence, you need to proactively encourage your team to spend part of their work hours to socializing. Organize and randomize buddy 1–1s to get to know each other. Use dedicated products, like [Donut](https://www.donut.com/), that facilitate this kind of social communication. One tactic is also to schedule meetings to start 15 min earlier than planned and use that extra time to specifically talk about completely non-work-related things. This is a perfect opportunity to build trust by, for example, centring the conversation around an emotional question like "When was the last time you cried?", or "What is your fondest memory from your childhood?". The playbook for distributed teams is in constant development, and we'll continue to share more learnings from the Creandum funds' portfolio. We're learning more every day that goes by. Do you have any further tips and ideas to upgrade distributed work? [Ping us!](https://www.creandum.com/contact/) <iframe src="https://cdn.embedly.com/widgets/media.html?src=https%3A%2F%2Fgiphy.com%2Fembed%2FZBQhoZC0nqknSviPqT%2Ftwitter%2Fiframe&display_name=Giphy&url=https%3A%2F%2Fgiphy.com%2Fgifs%2Floading-virtual-hug-ZBQhoZC0nqknSviPqT&image=https%3A%2F%2Fmedia1.giphy.com%2Fmedia%2FZBQhoZC0nqknSviPqT%2Fgiphy.gif%3Fcid%3D790b76118e6d9732018c3420d0e2dff288ed102eef09383f%26rid%3Dgiphy.gif%26ct%3Dg&key=a19fcc184b9711e1b4764040d3dc5c07&type=text%2Fhtml&schema=giphy" title="" height="454" width="435"></iframe>

articles.title: Leo Nilsson joins Creandum
articles.author: Johan Brenner
articles.text: An essential part of Creandum's DNA is to back ambitious entrepreneurs who are building great products that users love (Spotify, KRY, Vivino, Kahoot, Depop, Amie— the list goes on). Today, we are very excited to welcome one of those entrepreneurs from our own #Creandumfamily to join our investment advisory team: iZettle's former CPO **[Leo Nilsson](https://www.creandum.com/team/leo-nilsson)** will start **** as our secon**d Entrepreneur-In-Residenc**e **(EIR**). We met Leo in 2013, [two years after we participated in iZettle's Series A round](https://blog.creandum.com/the-izettle-story-with-cofounder-magnus-nilsson-19e4761143). Since then, we've been following his impressive journey to become the company's CPO. His strong product management background will not only add a new perspective to our teams' discussions but also, even more importantly, a new superpower to contribute to the success of [the funds' portfolio companies](https://www.creandum.com/portfolio/). As Leo is currently transitioning out of his role as CPO at iZettle, we had a brief talk on his product development experience, his biggest learnings, and what he is up for next: **_1. You spent almost a decade at iZettle, one of Europe's most successful Fintech_ companies _— tell us about your career within the company._** _Working for seven years at iZettle felt like joining a new business seven years in a row. The company grew from 45 people to 900+ during my time there. I started as a Growth Product Manager, launching new markets, including Brazil, Mexico, Netherlands and France. It was a quick way to get to know the market, the customers, their user behavior, the product itself and also the different teams at iZettle, as pretty much every function was involved in a new market launch._ _After a few years, iZettle made a strategic decision to focus more on expanding the proposition in existing markets, notably by adding more software capabilities and financial services to support small businesses on their journey. I started by overseeing our main products, Payments and Point of Sale, and building a small team of product managers around those._ _In 2016, I joined the leadership team as Chief Product Officer (CPO). The new role meant going from a strict focus on the end-user and the product to always thinking about our vision and strategic goals, bringing in and developing the right people, and how to operationally hit our targets through scaling, portfolio and organizational management_. _It was definitely a humbling experience. When I left, we had roughly 30 independent product teams across growth, core products and platform - not counting the many product teams iZettle is now interacting with across PayPal._ _**2. What are the biggest learnings you took from that time about product development in a young and fast-growing company?**_ _I learned a ton - especially from the many mistakes we made. In the context of how product development relates to total business success, here are my three biggest learnings:_ _**1. Develop end-to-end thinking for product success.**_ _Building a successful product truly requires you to think about the entire business and demands that you make tradeoffs between speed, value, and quality all the time.
