articles.title: Leap – the social learning platform for the over 55s
articles.author: Fredrik Cassel
articles.text: At Creandum, we like to keep our network of entrepreneurs close to us. Hence, we couldn't be more excited to announce the backing of one of those talented founders that we even had the pleasure to be working closely with for a few months: [Caroline Ingeborn](https://www.linkedin.com/feed/), former CEO of Toca Boca and ex-[Entrepreneur-In-Residence at Creandum](https://blog.creandum.com/caroline-ingeborn-joins-creandum-as-entrepreneur-in-residence-a399384b550e) building **[Leap](https://leap.so/)**, a social learning platform for the over 55s. Innovation is usually associated with youth and young people as this demographic is perceived as more open, experiential and creative, whereas their older-looking colleagues are more likely to be viewed as stable and conservative. Hence, we're seeing a lot of momentum on new digital services targeted to teenagers and adolescents as most entrepreneurs and company-builders aim towards those young people, to pick up their latest innovations. But what about the older people, the largest and fastest-growing segment of our society? ### An untapped market Maybe it's just a sign of my own inevitable ageing, but this segment has become increasingly interesting to me. It is a generation of people with considerable time, energy and spending power that have smartphones at their fingertips. Still, they are often not only seen as ‘obsolete' or ‘over-the-hill' they have also been largely overlooked by tech developers in the past. Until now. ### Enter Leap Leap is a social learning platform targeting the over 55s to power meaningful experiences. It is built around two central assumptions: meaningful connections happen when people meet in small groups – and are strengthened further when those small groups are united over shared interests. Users connect over both audio and video, in groups of between five and ten. The platform offers conversations and classes hosted by so-called ‘Leap Leaders' (experts recruited from the target audience) with especially strong initial traction among people interested in writing and creativity as can be observed in the current beta version. ![Leap, the social learning platform for the elderly.](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/7LanpowkT3nJlmZZCp5HBF/0ef510a95dceca10ccb3ba76438fd4f2/image_113.png) ‘Clubhouse for the elderly' might be your initial thought now – but it's rather the opposite. Think of deep, close relationships that are usually built offline around shared interests over time. Leap's mission is to enable its users to build meaningful connections between people who share interests. While the beta version enables mainly synchronous conversations, the future also points towards asynchronous options of interaction and education. To find the sweet spot, the team is working very closely with the first users. ![Some of the first classes on the Leap platform.](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/6eR3EKjj8HBTlFGLSdEOGh/ac55720be27786ab7a17a7b1865e0ccf/image_114.png) Finding the best product-market fit is a balancing act between sensitive listening to the users, a data-focused approach and a strong inherent product vision. A delicate task but who could do it better than a team that combines an intrinsic conviction to build the best product out there with a determined goal in mind to find the solution for those elderlies eager to continue to learn, grow and connect? ### A diverse duo of serial entrepreneurs Leap is founded by Swedish entrepreneur Caroline Ingeborn, former CEO of Toca Boca and Creandum's former Entrepreneur-in-Residence, and [Vishal Kapur](https://www.linkedin.com/in/vishalkapur4/), former CTO and co-founder of Screenhero. Caroline's skillset includes strong experience in building a consumer brand ([Toca Boca](https://tocaboca.com/)) paired with an aggressive, boundary-pushing mentality that she inherited from her time in investment banking. Vishal on the other hand represents the ideal counterpart to her: A very reflected, thoughtful tech engineer with deep sector competence in both consumer-focused video and audio tools, whose last company was acquired by Slack. The two met through the [South Park Commons](https://www.southparkcommons.com/) community and bring together profound product building experience and curiosity for a demographic they are not part of. Caroline and Vishal allowed themselves to take time to get to know each other and how they work as a team, first in an informal way, bouncing ideas, before they realised how strong the mutual energy was between them and around this cause. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/1CBRdrh5ZEkcsObnMM0lKk/5f14d080fd4909491692bfec6065533c/image_115.jpg) This diverse founding team convinced us with their determination and unique experiences to build a product that will be truly engaging. Having worked alongside Caroline when she was Entrepreneur-in-Residence at Creandum, it's a pleasure to back her and Vishal on this exciting journey. _Are you above 55 and looking to learn something new while connecting with like-minded individuals? Get on Leap's waitlist and be among the first users: [https://leap.so/](https://leap.so/)._

articles.title: YuLife
articles.author: Carl Fritjofsson
articles.excerpt: The Unfair Advantage of Strong Company Culture
articles.text: More or less every company Creandum speaks to claims culture is important for them. Company culture is an entrepreneurial meme that everyone subscribes to but very few actually master. But when your company is named [‘the best startup to work for in London in 2021'](https://www.heytempo.com/london-top-startups-to-work-for-in-2021/) you must be doing something right. On top of that, [when you raise a $70M Series B round by some of the best European funds](https://techcrunch.com/2021/07/14/yulife-nabs-70m-at-a-346m-valuation-for-its-gamified-wellness-oriented-approach-to-life-insurance/), you're definitely on the right track: Enter [YuLife](https://yulife.com/), the lifestyle insurance company providing life insurance, wellbeing, and rewards in one simple app. To get under the skin of what sets Yulife apart from other companies, we wanted to share how the founders [[Sam](https://www.linkedin.com/in/samfromson/)my](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sammy-rubin-4493a7/) and Sam have been able to establish such a phenomenal, culture-driven company. Even before the pandemic imposed a challenge to the well-being of employees globally, dealing with stress, anxiety, uncertainty and social isolation, and the new hybrid work models adding an additional layer of complexity to employer-employee relationships, Yulife integrated company culture in the core of their business to attract and retain the best talent to set the base for a hyper-growth company. ### Values drive performance. For companies that grow at an explosive pace, performance metrics are usually at the top of mind for the founders. While this definitely also holds true for Sam(my), they consider their values, upon which their company culture is built, as even more important than performance. They kick off every new week with an all-hands meeting placing a topic related to the company values at the centre stage of these meetings. They do this without mentioning performance-related KPIs, which are covered in a separate meeting later during the week. By bringing values into the start of every week the organization is intentionally reminded about its overarching importance. ### More than just a cute brand: Living the mission. Yulife truly puts wellbeing at the heart of everything they do. Yulife's group life insurance protects lives and rewards living, much like the way they look after their own people. Employees feel at home and refer to colleagues as their _Yulife Family_ and they benefit from, yes you guessed it, a more than decent insurance coverage. At YuLife, employees are encouraged to follow and deeply care about the company's mission to turn financial services into a force for good and not just take their job as a means to earn a living, but to actually live their best life while working. While a drive for good performance is taken for granted, Yulife encourages its employees to contribute an active part to the company's culture, have fun while being at work, establish strong social ties with their coworkers and live up to the shared values. Because everyone in the organization is anchored to the values, they are able to go beyond fun ping pong and beer nights and rather build deep meaningful relationships across their team members. ![The Yulife Team.](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/16pwBuCisdinUjlOwDKtiZ/7cdc2b256dda653aebe52d9a40b5498c/image_110.jpg) ### Hire with culture on top of your mind. In the past 24 months, [since Creandum invested in YuLife](https://blog.creandum.com/insurance-with-a-heart-announcing-creandums-backing-of-yulife-4cd96ef02567), the team has ~4x'ed in size. As they have shown, there is no need to slow down the hiring decisions, as long as you keep the company culture top of mind in the hiring process. Every candidate is assessed against if they are additive to the company culture. Since all existing employees are so deeply indoctrinated into the culture, Yulife is able to distribute candidate evaluation to the broader team which allows them to keep a fast pace, while the founders still are involved in the majority of all hires. ### Relentlessly reinforce target behaviours. YuLife's onboarding process starts before the employees first day at work. Every new hire receives ten (10!) books delivered to their doorstep before their first day. Those books include a mix of startup basics (such as [Measure what matters](https://www.amazon.com/Measure-What-Matters-Google-Foundation/dp/0525536221)), inspirational books (such as [Delivering Happiness](https://www.amazon.com/Delivering-Happiness-Profits-Passion-Purpose/dp/0446576220), [The hard things about hard things](https://www.amazon.com/Hard-Thing-About-Things-Building/dp/0062273205)), and books with a particular perspective on Yulife's product which centres around the tough topic of death (such as [Overcoming fear of death](https://www.amazon.com/Overcoming-Fear-Death-Through-Systems/dp/B06XXHLQSL/ref=sr_1_3?dchild=1&keywords=Overcoming+fear+of+death&qid=1626205348&s=books&sr=1-3) and [When breath becomes air](https://www.amazon.com/When-Breath-Becomes-Paul-Kalanithi/dp/081298840X/ref=sr_1_1?dchild=1&keywords=When+breath+becomes+air&qid=1626205372&sr=8-1)). Once new hires join, they get to meet many different team members across the business and talk about what it means to work at YuLife, be part of the community and the culture. As the learning of a culture is a continuous process not limited to the first few days, in order to maintain the culture throughout the employee's tenure, the founders talk about their values continuously. On top of that, Yulife keeps a powerful behaviour-shaping tool at their disposal to reinforce desired behaviour: recognition. They use their all-hands meetings to deliberately express gratitude, highlight personal & team wins, and give time to individual team members to present themselves to the rest of the company, revealing something unexpected about their background and personality. ### Better tracking leads to better decisions. What

articles.title: Factorial
articles.author: Peter Specht
articles.excerpt: Using Spain’s largest Series B to continue redefining HR for SMBs
articles.text: Every funding round presents a moment to consider the journey so far - but as [Factorial](https://factorialhr.com/) raises its $80m Series B, the largest in Spanish history, it seems right to celebrate the core reason that Jordi, Bernat, Pau, Cesar and team got here: Product. In a world where incumbent HR suites have become intimidating and clunky through feature sprawl, Factorial takes a laser sharp focus on what SMB users really use and need, with a delightful experience. Wile adding more features Factorial has never compromised on ease of use + UX and created a product second to none. [Just last year](https://blog.creandum.com/taking-hr-a-step-ahead-factorials-people-data-platform-969b6878f7c2), we put it this way: _"The challenge in HR solutions has been the right balance between feature breadth ("ticking the HR feature boxes") vs. product depth. Yet, with increasing market sophistication, we believe that SMEs' HR needs are moving more and more toward what we see in enterprise. That means all-in-one suites with access to vertical depth if needed - with the caveat that high ease of use is even more important."_ The opportunity in the HR market today is massive, in particular enabling SMEs to move to strategic HR. Factorial is making the journey beyond typical HR software by focusing on insights relating to everything around people within an organisation. There's no more valuable resource, and we see that having the right insights is more crucial than ever. In 2021, where teams have moved to more remote / hybrid setups and classical HR processes have been challenged, you need a powerful platform to serve your employees best. In this Series B, Factorial has raised a round of funding that nearly matches the largest _exits_ of the Spanish startup ecosystem. This is a threshold moment for Spanish startups, marking new maturity for the region. More to come. But most importantly, Series B helps the best companies floor the accelerator. We're excited to continue to back Factorial and participate significantly in this round led by Tiger Global. Together with them and our other co-investors, we look forward to support the team on their journey to build an extraordinary Spanish, European and global success story.

articles.title: Coming out of stealth: Vay — the world’s leading teledrive mobility company
articles.author: Simon Schmincke
articles.text: It's rare that we announce a new portfolio company nearly three years after the Creandum Funds invested - but for this unique company it was definitely worth waiting: Here comes [Vay](https://vay.io/), a Berlin-headquartered deep tech company with groundbreaking technology in the field of autonomous driving. Vay will be the first company operating a certified driverless commercial mobility service on public streets in Europe as soon as next year. And while some of you might have seen cars driving through Berlin with strange-looking hardware attached and no human touching the steering wheel - this is only the beginning of an exciting journey of a new form of transportation. Let's take a step back and look at the current world of transport. Approximately 1.3 million people die each year as a result of road traffic crashes - and these accidents are the leading cause of road injuries and death among children and young adults aged 5–29. The main cause behind most accidents? Human imperfection leading to speeding, intoxication, distraction, and fatigue. Now imagine a world where all those factors are removed. ### Enter Vay - Safer than traditional driving Vay's fleet is already operating with safety drivers across the streets of Berlin. But from next year, Vay will be able to completely take out the safety driver from its vehicles - and have the cars controlled 100% by ‘teledrivers'. What does that mean? Vay's drivers will be sitting in an office in central Berlin, driving the cars remotely. ![A driver in the Vay Telestation driving the car remotely.](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/1TLmjjfs8iIOJpfCFNBVEp/9c9b09968f71dcc8a6d7e6f8aaead9cc/image_104.png) Vay's system is engineered to the highest and latest automotive safety and security standards (ISO26262, ISO21434). In addition, when compared with traditional driving, Vay's teledrivers will have augmented skills, including 360-degree blindspot-free vision and supervision for fatigue or distractions. Safety is at the core of Vay. ### The team - a collection of the most relevant experience you can think of One of our key assets at Creandum is our presence in San Francisco. Not only does this allow us an overview of what's going on across the pond, but it also brings us closer to a global pool of the most interesting and talented founders. Just a few months into our San Francisco office, in 2018, Peter was introduced to a fellow German, based in Silicon Valley: [Thomas von der Ohe](https://www.linkedin.com/in/thomas-von-der-ohe/). We built a relationship with Thomas over the following month, and Simon and Peter ultimately decided to partner up with the team for their Series A. ![Vay co-founders Fabrizio Scelsi, Thomas von der Ohe and Bogdan Djukic.](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/6kgESiRuuiXUhBxDMiKMYA/321e757b9cbbd84e6ffd2ccbd1e718f9/image_105.png) Together with co-founders [Fabrizio Scelsi](https://www.linkedin.com/in/fabrizioscelsi/), and [Bogdan Djukic](https://www.linkedin.com/in/bogdandjukic/), it was clear he was on to something new. Together with the rest of their team, they unite experience from some of the world's leading automotive companies: Tesla, Google, Waymo, Zoox, Skype, Byton, Argo, Amazon, Uber as well as Audi, BMW, Daimler - you name it. Intrigued by this combined experience, we stayed close to the team and followed their progress with keen eyes. The majority of the team is in Berlin to settle ground in Europe while the other part works out of Portland, Oregon. ### No half-measures The Creandum funds backed Vay's $30m Series A round back in 2019, together with a range of fellow European VCs such as Atomico, LaFamiglia, System.One, Visionaries Club, Signals as well as stellar business angels Patrick Pichette (Partner at Inovia Capital, chairman of the board at Twitter, former global CFO at Google), Cristina Stenbeck (Board member of Spotify, chairman of the board at Zalando), Qasar Younis (co-founder and CEO of Applied Intuition, former COO and Partner of Y Combinator), and Formula 1 champion [Nico Rosberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nico_Rosberg). ![The Vay car fleet is already driving remotely around Berlin with safety drivers, but as of next year, those drivers will be removed from the car.](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/4zD2KVQEi39ratG8IbAlHI/2c142ee1b17bee0581f49dfa6d63df2c/image_106.jpg) Three years later, Thomas and his team continue to impress us and we look forward to accompanying the company in its next steps, establishing ‘TeleDriving' as a new path to an autonomous future.

articles.title: Creandum welcomes “Built for Mars” Peter Ramsey as Entrepreneur-in-Residence
articles.author: Simon Schmincke
articles.text: Over the course of the past 18 years, [Creandum](https://www.creandum.com/) has become the natural home for outstanding product founders. [Spotify](https://www.spotify.com/de/), [iZettle](https://www.zettle.com/de), [Vivino](https://www.vivino.com/DE/de), [Klarna](https://www.klarna.com/), [Cornershop](https://cornershopapp.com/en/), [Trade Republic](https://traderepublic.com/de-de), [Taxfix](https://taxfix.de/) - you name it, it's part of our core mission to help the most ambitious global entrepreneurs deliver the products the world needs next. Our Entrepreneur-in-Residence programme is designed to double down on that mission and provide all founders in the [Creandum Funds' portfolio](https://www.creandum.com/portfolio/) with world-leading expertise. So, we are delighted to announce our latest team member: [Peter Ramsey](https://www.creandum.com/team/peter-ramsey), best known as the author behind ["Built for Mars"](https://builtformars.com/). Put simply: Peter is the best UX expert in Europe today. Despite being based on the beautiful, vibrant south coast of England, his business sees him working shoulder to shoulder with the most progressive tech companies in the world, including Google, Klarna, and Notion. _"Building great UX is a mixture of art, personal preference and understanding human behaviour. It's not a set of fixed rules to follow, but rather a process of creatively solving new problems."_ When he is not analyzing websites and digital tools, you can find him "understanding human behaviour" of his 6-month old daughter or exploring ambitious plans that involve British farms (and potentially metric tons of insects. Ask him about it one day.) We sat down with him to learn more about his path to become Europe's most active UX consultant at the age of 28, his core tips for great UX and his future plans: _**1. You ran a proptech company for six years and [sold it to one of the worlds largest private equity firms in 2018](https://www.insidermedia.com/news/national/barbon-completes-movem-acquisition). Today, you're one of the most well-known UX experts and more than 250.000 people read your "Built for Mars" Blog. How did you become a UX expert? Tell us about your story.**_ _The short version of the story is that at Movem, I was a product-led founder. That was the part of the job I truly loved, and so I was self-taught (out of necessity) to build a better product._ _When we were struggling with sales, instead of hiring more people to hammer the phones, I obsessed over reducing churn._ _After the acquisition, friends started asking me to help them with their products. Then friends of friends, and after a few years of ad-hoc consulting I set up Built for Mars. Now it's all I do, and it's great._ _**2. How important was the role of UX in your company Movem and what are the biggest lessons you took from that time about UX?**_ _The user experience is important to every start-up, I think it's just the definition that people struggle with. UX doesn't just mean pixels on a screen, but how something feels. It's the cross-section of human psychology and ‘stuff' - and humans are surprisingly irrational._ _For example, people are outraged when physical bank branches close down, as that's something that they believe they value. Yet when you actually have to visit one, you're frustrated that you couldn't solve it online. Banks can somewhat alleviate this by having great UX within their app._ _**3. What do you think is the "secret sauce" to really good UX?**_ _As a product grows - in both features and staff - it gets more difficult to maintain a high standard of UX. If I had to pick one factor, it's having a product manager / designer who really cares._ _And not just a corporation tweeting that they care, but actually investing their resources in making the experience better, regardless of if it directly impacts their EBITDA._ ![Peter's office in his garden on the southern coast of England.](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/25xHCw8MVgiv4a5WXJ314l/8296b69ef974fb0f993f485b358823eb/image_103.jpg) _**4. What are the key UX tips you would give to any early-stage company that is just starting its product development?**_ _Most people don't properly account for the incremental cost of adding features. Teams get excited, and claim that "in just 1 week we can build this cool feature" - what they fail to understand is that it's never just a week._ _The complexity that you've added to your product increases the time required for testing and it likely makes building an intuitive UX harder._ _**6. How do you think being part of Creandum will benefit your professional development?**_ _I'm here to learn as much as I can. One day (could be months, could be decades), I want to swing for the fences with another product. But the timing and opportunity needs to be right._ _In the meantime, I've been gifted an opportunity to learn from not just one of the best VCs in the game, but portfolio companies that clearly ‘get it'._ _Creandum is thrilled to have Peter join us and share his UX wisdom with our investment advisory team and the funds' portfolio companies. Any ideas or UX-related questions? [Ping him](mailto:peter.ramsey@creandum.com)!_

articles.title: 15 Years of Fintech at Creandum
articles.author: Simon Schmincke
articles.excerpt: What's next?
articles.text: Fintech is done, right? What more can happen in a sector that has seen such immense innovation and growth, and has attracted so many incredibly talented entrepreneurs in recent years? Strangely enough, this is one of the most asked questions people want to discuss on panels and podcasts when it comes to the sector. Admittedly, a lot has happened. Yet every year we see completely new business models, digitisation of more analogue functions and technology progression which enables version two or three of something that we thought was great and digital already. Time to have a look back, understand what we focused on so far, and look forward to where we see opportunities going forward. We also want to take a look back at the Fintech [portfolio](https://www.creandum.com/portfolio/), double click on some of the beliefs that drove us to select those teams and dare to look into the future. To date, the Creandum fintech portfolio companies have raised over $6.5bn. Five of those startups have become unicorns: [Klarna](https://klarna.com), [Pleo](https://www.pleo.io/de), [iZettle](https://izettle.com), [Trade Republic](https://traderepublic.com) and [Pipe](https://pipe.com). Aside from those unicorns, Creandum's next crop of rising stars includes German [Taxfix](https://taxfix.de/) and [Billie](https://www.billie.io/en), British [Tide](https://www.tide.co/) and [YuLife](https://yulife.com/). ## Part 1: Looking back ![_Creandum's Fintech Portfolio_](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/5yn7fDBvooUS4peVtqKtbo/021cca892921d2168231bc5fff7ea3c1/image_102.jpg) When looking at the Creandum funds' fintech portfolio, it becomes clear that our focus ranges from consumer-facing businesses to SME, Infrastructure and Insurtech. But where Creandum's portfolio outside Fintech is strong in consumer offerings (Spotify, Depop, Kahoot, Small Giant Games and others) - in Fintech we have predominantly eyed startups in B2B. Our hypothesis a couple of years back centered around the observation that product offerings for enterprise customers would be disrupted by players who understand go to market, consumerization of UI and UX and often product lead growth. This is something we monitored especially in fintech. Players like [Billie](https://billie.io) and [Abacum](https://abacum.com) understood this trend and took existing product offerings to the next level, focussing on a new market segment. In Insurtech we have had a conviction that using modern technology will allow insurance companies to redefine how to do underwriting and assess risk, as well as enhancing the customer experience and how they engage with users. This allowed us to partner with innovative insurance models like Yulife and Laka. We are also carefully following macro shifts in the world and how that sparks demand for new insurance coverages, which is why we joined forces with SafetyWing and their ambition to bring health benefits to the remote workforce. While the beginnings of Klarna and iZettle were coined by the unbundling of services, today we see an expansion in product offering across many players. Initially highly verticalized, Pleo (offering spending solutions for employees) has now expanded into AP / AR solutions as well. Where Tide started as a checking account, today the company is providing Credit, Invoicing and Employee Cards. That ultimately leads to the discussion of whether some of the companies compete with each other. While our hypothesis remains that a concentrated effort on a verticalized product has the advantage over a horizontal player, adding new features for your core customers works well for some players. ### Consumer **[Argent](https://www.argent.xyz/)** - The simple & secure gateway to the decentralised web. **[Taxfix](https://taxfix.de/)** - Making tax declarations easy. **[Trade Republic](https://traderepublic.com/en-de)** - The mobile-only and commission-free broker. ### SME **[Billie](https://techcrunch.com/2019/07/16/billie/)** - Revolutionising SME Financing **[Bokio](https://www.bokio.co.)** - Free automated accounting for SMEs **[iZettle](https://izettle.com)** - Mobile payments and point-of-sale solutions **[Pipe](https://pipe.com)** - Instant access to your annual cash flow **[Pleo](https://www.pleo.io/de)** - Combining expenses with smart, beautiful software **[Tide](https://www.tide.co/)** - The business banking service you deserve ### Infrastructure **[Abacum](https://www.abacum.io/)** - Financial planning for mid-market companies **[lemon.markets](https://www.lemon.markets)** - Trading equities through an API **[Swan](https://www.swan.io/)** - The Banking-as-a-Service platform that allows any company to become a Fintech ### Insurance **[Klarna](https://klarna.com)** - Committed to making online shopping easy and hassle-free **[Laka](https://laka.co/de)** - Laka is an insurance company that is powered by the community **[Safety Wing](https://safetywing.com/)** - Providing cross-border benefits for remote employees **[Yulife](https://yulife.com/)** - A life insurance company built for modern business ## Part 2: What's next and where are we spending time? Fintech will remain one of the core activity areas here at Creandum. Both because we remain extremely bullish on the opportunities and because we keep meeting teams who push the bar of what's possible in their respective sub-industries. On top of that, traditional incumbents still hold the majority of market share with outdated products and processes: there are plenty of opportunities for future fintech entrepreneurs to disrupt the status quo. Here's where we see the most potential. **Payments: Enabling companies to orchestrate getting paid** Both offline and online, who to pay, when, where and how - we continue to get excited about how companies can automate and orchestrate payment flows more intelligently. With the challenges of small margins, companies need to demonstrate enough value to either participate in the transaction in a meaningful way or accumulate large

articles.title: Under The Hood of Diversity: 2021 Creandum Diversity Index
articles.author: Carl Fritjofsson
articles.text: We have said it before but it bears repeating: **diverse teams drive better decision-making and build better companies**, and [the data shows it's true](https://www.bcg.com/publications/2018/why-women-owned-startups-are-better-bet.aspx). Diversity is good business, and is why it's a priority for us every day. That's why we're increasing the diversity of our team. It's why we examine diversity in every investment the fund pursues. It's why we helped launch [Included.vc](https://included.vc/). But it's not enough. There's still work to do. Every day. We are listening closely to how our peers are making a difference and sharing that knowledge (check out the [Creandum Diversity & Inclusion Knowledge Bank](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1M45fB1cJwLQJa8M6jwXHIaQts6iLXqwWaf57wqGTnHU/edit#gid=1022305167) for a full library.) To everyone, we say: Keep going. Keep accelerating. Keep examining your unconscious biases. We will get there together. And as part of our work along this we want to present the Creandum Diversity Index 2021. ### Methodology Our Creandum Diversity Index is focusing specifically on gender. The impact of gender on startups is the most researched axis of diversity, and that data remains insufficient on most others. When we started this initiative, we agreed on doubling down our efforts on this specific topic, instead of covering the entire range with less vigour. Each year, we send a poll to the portfolio company CEOs measuring the number of women across 3 dimensions in their respective organizations: 1. across the whole organization 2. on the management team 3. on the board In addition to this, last year we also added a 4th data point related to compensation and the pay gap between the genders. We use our Diversity Index to put light on the topic of gender diversity with each of the fund's portfolio companies. By looking at an individual company's diversity data in comparison to our broader portfolio helps facilitate the conversation and drive the initiative forward. The reports from [2018](https://hackernoon.com/diversity-inside-european-vc-more-work-needed-c545353b7e4c), [2019](https://blog.creandum.com/diversity-inside-european-vc-2-0-limited-progress-made-f89479fe3738) and [2020](https://blog.creandum.com/a-small-sign-of-progress-on-gender-diversity-in-tech-915c85ac9221) can be found in the respective links. In total, for this year we surveyed 59 portfolio companies of which 52 responded. ### Women across all organisations: 45% (+4%) ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/2uS8GrqnOEFtlD05QP0TT1/602ff0581eea2d0e9d23bf9d0f775073/image_94.jpg) Across the portfolio, we can see an improvement to 44,5% women among all employees. Assuming 50% is the desirable level, we are close to this key breakthrough. Interestingly, this is the same increase as last year - which means we might just cross that boundary in 2022. The average is brought up by a handful of cases with 65% or more women in the team. But at the same time, the number of companies with more than 50% women declined by 5% to 15%. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/2vb7XXMrqY2nDCLDLhZgPp/4c0859f81874c780abbeabc2dc45823d/image_95.jpg) Although we again have many examples that have improved gender balance, these trend toward the younger companies in the portfolio. Elsewhere, it feels like just as many hired more male employees (hence the cloud of dots in the left bottom corner.) But there are encouraging signs that the older businesses start increasing their share of women as time goes on. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/2S7AOObNCwX5J6zCNHdXJs/6b60349ec0da40e99fa8d0ab1a1837cf/image_96.jpg) We see a similar picture if we look at the relative amount of women for different types of companies by size: the larger the companies are, the closer we get to 50% However early employees are often more important and benefit more from success. The effects of this shouldn't be underestimated and we must work harder on getting it right in this aspect. ### Women in Management: 28% (-3%). ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/3lXY10Su8GrvYJC9lRmYm6/355ab1e5ec05eb9cd21e3c02202f5c7e/image_97.jpg) After a great leap last year, we see women in management levels worsen in 2021. It's hard to speculate about the causes, although [many have commented](https://www.bbc.com/worklife/article/20201021-why-this-recession-disproportionately-affects-women) on how the pandemic has affected the fate of women disproportionately to men. The effects of this may be greater as they continue to further life stages that may include more responsibilities. Thankfully, the trend still puts us 6% ahead of 2019, so we are hopeful for progress next year. We also see that companies who have women in leadership positions are by far better at recruiting women and having a more balanced organization overall, making this number specifically important for our companies to improve. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/47wbh1Yr5vIyERQz0OiZUg/4c58d88671f5d6d2b58966ccd4a45dfa/image_98.jpg) At the same time, we now see half of the portfolio have more than 25% women in management and the proportion with less than 1% is clearly shrinking. The majority of businesses are at least heading the right direction. As with last year, we find a relationship between women in management team and the overall share of female employees. If there are more than 50% women in management roles, there is an average of 54% female employees. ### Board Members 13% (+3%). ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/6r0lyMBt43RKEsOsDtMRwQ/9089a2cf7c83add1e4cc46f64e3a23e6/image_99.jpg) Boards are notoriously imbalanced for gender, and are on perhaps the longest timeline for how quickly they are changing. The good news is, we have seen a leap this year of 3%, versus just half a percent in previous years. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/3Q0YClPKPpKUcmWYQk4EjU/14b6108ee8cd6cc991c51c4f2edd5d18/image_100.jpg) The number of companies with more than 50% women board members is also on the

articles.title: Creandum backs Vue Storefront
articles.text: # Creandum x Vue Storefront _Today, Creandum is leading [Vue Storefront](https://vuestorefront.io)'s Series A round. To mark the occasion, we interviewed co-founder Patrick Friday about how the business started, why Headless ecommerce matters and what make the company tick._ As with many great startups, Vue Storefront was born out of frustration. Working in an ecommerce agency, Patrick Friday was finding again and again that brands were driven to despair by slow, inflexible front end storefronts. Some were struggling along with compromised front end experiences provided by their back end software, but the biggest were commissioning fully custom built storefronts. And yet, the promise of [headless ecommerce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Headless_commerce) was that each part of the equation could be independently as great as possible, to give maximum speed, flexibility and choice. Something had to be done. Patrick asked his colleague Filip Rakowski to look at implementing a new approach to front ends. The investigation started with React, but very quickly moved to the Vue.js platform and the project tripled in speed. They now had a new way of building storefronts on Vue. Vue Storefront was born and launched as open source. Uptake skyrocketed right away. — ## Seed Patrick explains: "It has grown organically in the most amazing way. We never spent money on marketing, no money on advertising. Instead, the clear limiting factor became that the business was part of a single agency, when the appetite existed across the whole industry." In 2019, the decision was made to spin out the business. Bart Roszkowski joined as the third co-founder and brought much experience from three previous exits and VC backed startups. After raising a seed round from two strong local investors, Smok Ventures and Movens Capital, then joining Y-Combinator, the focus very quickly became how the team could complement its open source success with an equally powerful proposition for enterprise. But this would need more resources. Luckily, Vue Storefront was on Creandum's radar and the team were in touch about a potential Series A. Creandum Partner Peter Specht explains what he saw in the business: "We'd been looking at Headless e-commerce for a while and it's clearly a large trend that's here to stay. While a lot of development has happened on the backend, the front end has been overlooked. Vue Storefront was very well positioned to capture value and develop a new standard. It stood out by being developer-focused, open source, agnostic and flexible on top of ANY backend." This changed the game for the Vue Storefront team. They were building up to their YC demo day but didn't even have a deck yet. The conversation with angels and investors accelerated development of the next financial plan and more. Demo Day took a back seat to the accelerating growth of the business. — - ## Breadth and depth Vue Storefront puts much of its focus into choosing which aspects of the product have breadth, and which have depth. Patrick again: "We very quickly realised most products are often only aimed at enterprise, midmarket or very small businesses but we don't need to choose in that way. We give so much out of the box that many see the benefits immediately and want to test it. But we equally know that the depth of our flexibility is a massive winner for enterprise." For enterprises looking to put a head on their headless options, this flexibility means they aren't tied into a single vendor and they have all the advantages of the existing custom solutions they might have had before. Crucially though, they gain this without having to start from scratch. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/2MoviUkKNty616e98XE5EW/4a5c2278f2be6e2fff78b9c117005ff5/image_91.jpg) Vue Storefront had discovered that the vast majority of online brands over $25M in revenue had a custom front end. This was a massive opportunity to replace and upgrade, without those brands having to leave their existing back end of Magento, SAP or anything else. "We told enterprises Vue Storefront is the last front end you will ever need. You might be happy with your backend, CMS, payments today - but inevitably platforms and possibilities develop year on year. With Vue Storefront, you have the flexibility to replace every other component and keep your front end experience the same." The clear journey for the business after Series A is increasing this advantage through breadth of integrations. The second facet of this is automating more and more of the setup process so that the sophistication of enterprise onboarding becomes even easier and available to more brands. Patrick says "our mission is to make this kind of technology accessible for everyone." Again, this is a key part of what impressed Creandum about the opportunity - Specht explains: "What's so exciting here is how Vue Storefront can address all parts of the market from relatively low down SMB level through midsize to the largest retailers out there." Vue Storefront wants to become a starting point for education among the community. This includes initiatives like the MACH Alliance - a group of agencies and tools promoting the best of breed open tools for the enterprise tech ecosystem. It stands for Microservices-based, API-first, Cloud-native SaaS and Headless and Vue Storefront was invited to be one of the first members. Elsewhere, its first conference attracted 1800 attendees across two days, thanks to its breadth of partners across different CMS, backends and other systems. This was a karmic bet that educating the industry will pay dividends for all. But it's also the benefit of being a serious and active member of a thriving open source community. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/6iFNegl2YBU8WFW0hbHtj8/ae207226d2b08000a72d4258d6461af0/image_92.jpg) — - ## Product When it comes to product, the approach is clear: be as customer-centric as possible. articles.title: Denmark in 2021: The B2B (SaaS) capital of Europe
articles.text: It's easy to talk about "the Nordics" as one entity - but just as Smörrebröd is not the same as Knäckebröd and Suomi sounds nothing like Norsk, there are major differences in the startup ecosystems. And Creandum has enjoyed a front-row seat as the different countries' startups developed in their distinct directions. Take Sweden, which became [the Fintech hub](https://sifted.eu/articles/juni-sweden/?utm_source=Sifted&utm_campaign=39940a04d7-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2021_10_14_01_14&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_3d44334990-39940a04d7-192905642) of the cold north with unicorns like [Trustly](https://www.trustly.net/us), [Tink](https://tink.com/), [(i)Zettle](https://www.zettle.com/se), and [Klarna](https://www.klarna.com/se/) (yes, we are particularly proud of those last two). Or Finland, [the gaming capital](https://www.pocketgamer.biz/special-report/71415/finlands-transformation-from-start-up-capital-to-mobile-heavyweights/) that has influenced everyone under 30 with games such as Angry Birds and Clash of Clans, alongside hot new startups like [Skunkworks](https://www.skunkworksgames.com/) getting us hooked on merging tools. Today, we want to focus on Denmark, where we are seeing a new verticalized ecosystem emerge: The B2B(SaaS) ecosystem of Denmark (...and, spoiler alert: we might tell the winter saga of Norway and Iceland at a later point.) ## Watching for waves When looking at the maturity of ecosystems we like to think in waves. For those of you who are new to this concept: since most entrepreneurs and early employees have an innate "urge to build", you usually see a 2nd wave of businesses following successful exits. Once these are a hit and this trickles down again, the ecosystem enters its 3rd wave (the grandchildren of the 1st, if you like). So where are the Nordics in these terms? Norway and Iceland are currently on their first wave but starting to become interesting. The former already has some impressive exits (Kahoot!) and exciting companies across varying stages including [Cognite](https://www.cognite.com/en/), [Xenata](https://www.xeneta.com/), and [Dune Analytics](https://dune.xyz/home). These successes trigger the transition to the 2nd wave. In the more mature markets, Sweden hosts a couple of impressive unicorns and we currently see its third wave of founders. It has not only produced a lot of unicorns in fintech but about one fifth of total funding in the region goes into new fintech startups. Denmark and Finland are not far behind. Their Unicorns have a combined value of $61.1bn and in Denmark, the clear majority appear in the B2B space. Knowing this area well, we anticipate exciting stuff but also an accelerating trickle-down effect. Look out Sweden— Denmark is heading right into its 3rd wave! But how did Denmark get here? ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/5IwkVUkz2xltw44Iuhqjft/e558815bf851d1b4671ce825d7b795b4/image_88.png) ## The battle of Enterprise SaaS: US vs Denmark 2014 was a good year for the Danes - they were crowned number 1 at the [European Badminton Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_European_Badminton_Championships) and hosted the [Eurovision Song Contest](https://www.ebu.ch/news/2013/09/copenhagen-named-host-city-of-20). But it also saw [Zendesk](https://www.zendesk.com/), the Copenhagen-founded customer service, and sales CRM go public at over 1 BUSD valuation. This provided the country's biggest tech exit and gilded the nation. However, some think it came at a price. Just months after [Morten Primdahl](https://twitter.com/primdahl), [Alexander Aghassipour](https://twitter.com/aghassipour), and [Mikkel Svane](https://twitter.com/mikkelsvane) started building the software in Svane's loft, attracting over 1,000 trial customers, investors started to flock. They offered to invest - but only if the company moved to the US. They were not the only Danish founders "encouraged" to relocate in this way. On one hand, this demand may have delayed the trickle-down effects of a Denmark-based "Zendesk mafia" (which instead established in the US and supported companies like [OneLogin](https://www.onelogin.com/) and [ChartMogul](https://chartmogul.com/)). But on the flip side, the company may well not have gotten where it is today without that move. In parallel, we saw many Danish now-Unicorns go through the same relocation: [Unity](https://unity.com/), [Sitecore](https://www.sitecore.com/), [Tradeshift](https://tradeshift.com/), and [Chainanalysis](https://www.chainalysis.com/). These moves created a wave of influence that has benefited the Danish B2B ecosystem immensely. **So what were the three key benefits of this compromise?** 1. Danes now have a network of successful B2B founders 2. It has instilled "B2B confidence" in entrepreneurs building in Denmark 3. It has created a new breed of commercial talent in Denmark As is often the case when an ecosystem is created, you need a few successful entrepreneurs as the starting point. They partly work as role models, but they also come with new hands-on knowledge and understanding of how to run a category-defining business, or set up offices and win in the US. Not only are they fundamental in bringing money back and angel investing - they are also instrumental in spreading know-how. Indeed, not all B2B founders in Denmark have had the chance for a 1-on-1 with [Mikkel Svane](https://twitter.com/mikkelsvane). But they have had the chance to see him succeed. Seeing someone like you take a big step creates a model to do the same, and not be deterred by "common knowledge" that B2B companies are best built elsewhere. ![Strong individuals in the Danish tech ecosystem](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/7BpfNK32WPO3ugO8BtlNmz/a8fbd6e6a8f03b26982718ca39e9f5cb/image_89.jpg) Lastly, setting high standards and building globally recognized companies means that the greenhouse for talent has flourished. It seems like the cross-pollination between the US and Denmark has created a new breed of commercial and product talent that doe

articles.title: Welcome Iris, Creandum’s new Associate
articles.author: Simon Schmincke
articles.text: We're truly delighted to welcome Iris Hendriks as Creandum's latest Associate. In the last year, Iris has gone from our internship programme to full Associate, spending time in both EU offices and fast becoming a great member of the team. Her career has already taken her from the Netherlands to Canada, to Switzerland to Belgium and beyond, covering two Masters degrees in Management (with one cum laude with honours) and an internship at Bain & Company. In between her degrees, she also ran the Erasmus Consultancy Project, helping Dutch companies expand into Indonesia as a full time board member, and consulted with PureDrops, a Swiss NGO focused on providing access to clean drinking water in Uganda. Somewhere in the mix of all this, she found the time to become an enthusiastic cook (and eater, ask her for her Google Map of great eating spots) and remains a true "Dutchie", cycling around Berlin and trying to infiltrate the office with native treats and game nights. She's already throwing herself into a range of interesting challenges and investment analysis with our team. Welcome Iris! _We're hiring Associates in Sweden and London, so you could be next. [Check out all our open positions here.](https://creandum.recruitee.com)_

articles.title: Creandum x Billie — an interview about B2B Buy Now Pay Later
articles.author: Simon Schmincke
articles.text: _Buy Now Pay Later provides a fundamental quality of improvement for consumers - but in B2B, it can create a crucial opportunity for the cashflow-strained merchant. Providing a real time experience, similar to the one we are used to for consumers, is only possible because the team at Billie has created a next generation approach to risk-scoring and SME data._ _After the team's recent news of a [partnership with Klarna](https://www.altfi.com/article/8467_klarna-backs-berlins-b2b-buy-now-pay-later-leader-billie-in-100m-round) and [raising its latest funding](https://techcrunch.com/2021/10/25/billie-a-buy-now-pay-later-specialist-for-the-b2b-market-raises-100m-on-a-640m-valuation/), we wanted to talk in more detail about the thinking behind these moves and what makes the company tick._ **Simon: Today you announced your next financing milestones: an impressive $100m funding round and a $200m re-financing line: Looking into the future, where do you expect this industry to head to and what's in it for Billie?** **Matthias:** We see B2B payments at a turning point, much as B2C payments were a decade ago. B2B is still lagging behind in ease of use, seamless integrations and the user experience of consumer tech. We strongly believe that all of those things have to come to the B2B world. Old technology, complex processes, and paper-based transactions need to be a thing of the past. At the same time, B2B transactions can be a lot more complex: requiring multiple stakeholders, larger basket sizes, complex invoice requirements and ERP exports. The counterparty, a business entity, is more complex and heterogeneous than a typical consumer. However, B2B payments will start to resemble B2C payments. While in today's world the business buyer needs to jump through many hoops to make a transaction happen, buyers will be center stage tomorrow. Complexity will be managed and processes be automated. At Billie, we see ourselves driving this change, being the category defining market leader and providing the deep technological solutions B2B transactions and payments need to empower merchants worldwide. Thus, we will put even more emphasis on building features and products for our existing and future customers making their B2B payments frictionless while at the same time increasing our efforts for international expansion. **Simon Schmincke: Billie recently announced a very intimate partnership with Klarna - can you elaborate how that came to place and what it means for both teams?** **Matthias Knecht**: We have known Sebastian and the Klarna team for a few years now and have always been huge fans. Klarna's way of empowering consumers and supporting them in all their payment needs has transformed B2C commerce forever - and created a self-reinforcing flywheel for its own growth. We have created a similar flywheel for the business user here at Billie. The synergies are obvious: While Klarna is focusing on B2C, Billie covers B2B. Most merchants actually serve both private consumers and business customers and therefore need specific solutions for each. Thus, this team-up made perfect sense. With Billie's B2B payment methods, Klarna can provide the first holistic BNPL solution on the market, removing the complexity of multiple integrations and securing a strong competitive advantage. This partnership dramatically and instantly increases Billie's reach to tens of thousands of Klarna merchants. **Simon: BNPL seems to be the flavour of the year in Fintech - why do you think it is so en vogue right now?** **Matthias:** The essence of BNPL is not new - businesses and consumers have paid on 30, 60 or 90 day net terms for a long time. However, over the last decade technology has made it possible to offer BNPL at unprecedented scale for online and offline purchases. Through major advancements in areas like payment processing, scoring technology, fraud prevention, real-time identification and more, consumers can now pay whenever and however they want. Payments today feel as easy and fun as using any other app on your smartphone. All the complexity, the plumbing, the risk assessment, the identity verification is hidden in the background. These new payment rails are challenging old, traditional systems like the credit card schemes which have existed since the 1950s. Consumers, especially the younger generation, feel that the user friendliness and transparency of modern BNPL payment methods better suit their needs. But in B2B payments, the transformational changes have been slower to take shape. Modern BNPL technology for B2B payments is still in its infancy and so they are still dominated by clunky, old, often paper-based processes. It's another area where business buyers do not enjoy the same level of convenience and automation that all of us enjoy as private consumers. A fully automated, conversion-optimized B2B BNPL payment method with a fun and slick user interface is missing. Most B2B merchants today are forced to try building it themselves or not offer BNPL to their business customers at all. At Billie, we are solving this challenge and helping business buyers enjoy the same level of freedom of when and how to pay as we know it from B2C commerce. **Simon: What are people getting wrong when they enter the BNPL industry?** **Matthias:** Some of the most overlooked aspects of the BNPL playbook are two factors that can make or break your profitability as a BNPL provider: risk and refinancing. At Billie, we have trained our risk models and limit engines for years and have been able to consistently achieve some of the lowest default rates in the industry. Fraud risk is an especially key risk category in e-commerce which needs careful management and constant model recalibration. To detect the patterns and attack vectors one needs a lot of data to train and backtest the models. Our systems are running different categories of machine learning models on AWS which allow for the highest checkout acceptance rates while keeping default r

articles.title: Nine Angel Voices - The Story Behind
articles.text: During summer [I posted a question on Twitter](https://twitter.com/axeliaklein/status/1408325175884468233?s=20) asking to highlight female angel investors in Europe. It created a solid list of names. But at that point, I also realized I wanted to go beyond the names on a list and paint a wider picture. [This](https://www.craft.do/s/VS5UPV8g5J2ufF) is an attempt to fulfil that mission. I have asked nine European angel investors about: their story, what got them into investing, their investment rationale behind companies they have backed, their advice to those who want to start angel investing - and more! These truly are nine amazing women and it makes me proud to be a small part of an ecosystem including these individuals. Big thanks to [Yenny](https://twitter.com/YennyCheung), [Yvonne](https://twitter.com/YvonneBajela), [Deepali](https://twitter.com/deepalinangia), [Namrata](https://twitter.com/doc_namrata), [Bérénice](https://twitter.com/BMagistretti), [Janneke](https://twitter.com/jannekeniessen), [Lian](https://twitter.com/LianMichelson), [Jane](https://twitter.com/JaneWalerud), and [Helena](https://twitter.com/htorras), who gave me some of their valuable time. Hopefully, it will inspire more women to start angel investing! [Link to portraits here ](https://www.craft.do/s/VS5UPV8g5J2ufF)** I hope you will enjoy reading it as much as I have enjoyed creating it! _Co-authored together with [Lorenz Raml](https://www.linkedin.com/in/lorenz-raml/) and [Harneet Dhaliwal](https://www.linkedin.com/in/harneetdhaliwal/)_

articles.title: Building Creandum: the team for 2022 and beyond
articles.author: Johan Brenner
articles.text: # Building Creandum: strengthening the team for 2022 and beyond One of a VC's most important investments is in their own team. Every member brings their own story of growth, reaching new benchmarks and expanding their reach and maturity over time. We've had a lot of great results in our Creandum funds - but we're equally pleased to see our team thrive alongside them. Meanwhile, the European startup scene has never been more powerful or competitive, and never has there been this much talent and opportunity in the market. This is the next step to level up our team across multiple functions and seize the opportunity in today's evolving VC market. _(...and before we get started, let me remind you: [we are hiring](https://creandum.com/jobs/). Could you be our next team investment?)_ ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/5S7rkazCnceDFEN2H84nFH/24593e6644879c554b856e8feb03e35e/image_85.jpg) ## Carl Fritjofsson becomes General Partner Carl joined us in 2011 from his own startup, and like many other Associates, left to join portfolio company Wrapp as cofounder. After a stint at 500 Startups in San Francisco, he rejoined in 2016 as a Venture Partner, graduating to full time Partner in 2018. Carl is a tremendous asset to Creandum. He has been instrumental in building our Silicon Valley office and excelled in investments including Cornershop, recently sold to Uber for $3.5Bn. He shows boundless and fearless energy, generating superior dealflow across multiple regions, while driving efforts in areas like Diversity + Inclusion. And he does this as a core part of the team despite being miles (and timezones) away from our offices in Stockholm, Berlin and London. In short, we believe that Carl can carry Creandum's flag and help lead the team's development for many years to come. We are honoured to welcome Carl as Creandum's latest General Partner. [Read the full post here.](https://blog.creandum.com/carl-fritjofsson-creandums-latest-general-partner-6b12aeec6805) ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/1TJDTiU2uUQ1EXFvmHnXs5/08e43ab4c65906f2459654644c927638/image_86.jpg) ## Beata Klein is promoted to Investment Manager Creandum usually has a straightforward timeline to its Associate programme: 24 months working with the team and portfolio to learn our trade. But as one of our Associates put it just recently: ["There are no rules when it comes to a career in venture capital."](https://blog.creandum.com/making-sense-of-one-year-in-vc-1298b5757e95) In Beata's case, we're inclined to agree. She's ready for the next level and we're enormously proud to promote her to become Creandum's latest Investment Manager. She brings very relevant experience -running her own startup in Asia and graduating from the Kinnevik group, renowned for uncovering some of the best new and entrepreneurial talent. Once on board at Creandum, she immediately over-delivered on the two most important areas: analytical and process power. Since then, she has proactively taken on firm leadership responsibilities - recruiting and thinking about the firm's future at every stage. Investment Manager was the natural next step. [Get to know Beata better with a full interview here.](https://blog.creandum.com/beata-klein-creandums-new-investment-manager-294016204270) ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/5NzEHNw2TF7gD2Hurae9Nm/3c07d1358f3c28a5e6e7e0ce92f991ed/image_87.jpg) ## Michelle Coventry joins as Head of Talent In the early startup years, where we focus, talent is the number one investment for teams. It's an area where you can never be doing enough. That's why it has always been one of our main priorities in assisting portfolio companies and one of the most rewarding ways to collaborate with founders. But the market is only getting more competitive. Michelle joins from Five AI and Kindred Capital, having helped build foundational teams at Depop, Appearhere and supported Betfair, TransferWise and Farfetch. With 25 years experience, she brings a maturity to the area of Talent that goes beyond the simple and tactical, instead planning for the ultimate cultural fit for the years ahead. ### A busy year, who's next? In 2021 alone, this builds on the return of [Sabina as Partner, Gemma as our latest Principal](https://techcrunch.com/2021/05/18/creandum-boosts-team-with-new-partner-sabina-wizander-and-new-principal-gemma-bloemen/), [not one](https://blog.creandum.com/welcome-to-the-team-max-4efaf3fb903e) but two Maximilians, [Iris as our latest Associate](https://blog.creandum.com/welcome-iris-creandums-new-associate-fa781422b2), [Lisa as Executive Assistant](https://blog.creandum.com/welcome-to-berlin-lisa-de4a8357de75) and our Entrepreneurs-in-Residence, including [Peter Ramsey](https://blog.creandum.com/creandum-welcomes-built-for-mars-peter-ramsey-as-entrepreneur-in-residence-9f9feeebfca). And indeed, we're still hiring. If you think you could make a difference in our team, check out [our open roles here](https://creandum.com/jobs). If you know someone from a diverse and overlooked community with a passion for VC, you can recommend they [apply to Included VC's 2022 Fellowship here](https://2fhwxuu9b7l.typeform.com/to/YvwaVnYu%20%E2%80%9C). 2021 has been a meaningful year for the team, our portfolio and our business - but we're sure there's much more to come.

She's ready for the next level and we're enormously proud to promote her to become Creandum's latest Investment Manager. She brings very relevant experience - running her own startup in Asia and graduating from the Kinnevik group, renowned for uncovering some of the best new and entrepreneurial talent. Once on board at Creandum, she immediately over-delivered on the two most important areas: analytical and process power. Since then, she has proactively taken on firm leadership responsibilities - recruiting and thinking about the firm's future at every stage. Investment Manager was the natural next step. At this great moment, we wanted to take a minute together and reveal a bit more about Beata and how she got here. ### The advantages of different founders Given her own founder experience, much of Beata's focus is on the earliest entrepreneurs. She has a front row seat to the innovation and enthusiasm coming from second and third wave founders in Europe. "Seeing this new breed of EU individuals emerge and perform better than those out of the US is incredibly compelling. There's a different take on scaling for European founders - you're born in one geography knowing you will inevitably have to scale instead of thriving locally in the US. This means the best founders must always have thought about the next step to escape the gravity of their local market." She has seen how that forward-looking perspective trickles down to areas like product and team, generating founders who are thinking in advance about the next step, the next vision for where they are going. Although she founded a B2C company herself, her investment history is clearly weighted toward B2B. "The trends of B2C are trickling down into B2B and the companies we are seeing there today are very far from the old enterprise software of the world. It's very product-led, it has beautiful UX and UI. These look like consumer products. But crucially: there's so much left to digitalise that hasn't even got close yet in B2B. It's just getting started." Within this, she highlights the opportunity to do more with data inside organisations. Every business sits on enormous volumes of information, including breadcrumb trails about their behaviour that can provide valuable insights. ### Today's funding environment Anyone who has spent a little time with Beata quickly recognises she's fearless. So, in the current startup ecosystem, where valuations are rocketing and deals are flying through, what does she think of this brave new world? "Ultimately, you either play in the market that exists or you don't - and risk only participating in second rate companies that others don't want to follow. You have to be conscious: will this funding propel the company or start to become a hindrance?" As a founder herself, she finds it natural to argue that cash in the bank can create a certain confidence and security that actually _serves_ execution. "It lets you be more forward-looking and long term in mindset." "Yes the valuations are crazy and maybe not every pre-seed is worth $50M. But on the other hand, if the money is spent wisely it helps you hire the best talent and get where you are going faster." They used to say the average time for a startup to reach Unicorn status was 8 years. Nobody would be surprised to hear that time has maybe halved. Could greater funding be driving this progress? Beata returns to the idea of conviction in founders. "It comes back to how big you think the companies can become. If you're aiming for 1 billion outcome you need to think differently to 10 billion outcome. That's where the judgement comes in." Throughout our discussion of this area, one thing is clear: we live in a time where it's really up to investors to put their money where their mouth is. If they believe a founder can get a business to a certain level, and they want the ownership that matters, the old rules of pricing may need a rethink. ### What makes the best VC? In many careers, the focus is on having all the answers. Beata says VC is more about offering the best questions. "VC is like being the dumbest person in the room asking the most clever questions. It's not about trying to outsmart founders, but having the humility and understanding that you only possess a fraction of what they know. So instead, you try and help them tell the story. She also talks about how exercises in reflection have helped her grow in the role. "I'll often pick an idea and try to internalise it by putting it out on Twitter to others." Indeed, if you haven't been paying attention to Beata's Twitter threads over the last year, are you even _on_ VC Twitter? The aim of all of this is that when she sits down with an entrepreneur, she always leaves them with some piece of advice, recommendation or introduction that they can go away and apply to their work. What's her recent key advice to founders? "The main thing is I encourage all founders to get a mentor group around them of other founders. As VCs you have maybe 5–10 people you discuss with on a daily basis, you share ideas, your thoughts on a space, you build an understanding of what others are doing. As a founder you also have some competition with peers but you can either select a group of them or people not within the same space or stage. 5–10 people you speak to regularly and trust." Even in startups, it takes a village. So what's next? "Staffan said so many times early on that VC is a long term game and I'm really starting to understand how true that is now. I want to make sure I'm a valuable part of the ecosystem in this long game." I think I speak for everyone at Creandum when I say we all hope the same for Beata. And we look forward to supporting her as she gets there.

articles.title: Creandum’s new General Partner
articles.author: Johan Brenner
articles.excerpt: Carl Fritjofsson is now General Partner
articles.text: # Carl Fritjofsson: Creandum's latest General Partner After 18 years, much of our thinking about Creandum is toward the future. How do you establish a firm that can continue to thrive not just in the years ahead, but for decades? The answer is always generational. When we think about our GPs, the way we talk about this role is "holding the keys" to Creandum. And it's really the right metaphor for the responsibility that we give to our strongest members. Creandum is an important home for our portfolio, investors and partners. That brings us to Carl. Carl joined us in 2011 from his own startup, and like many other Associates, left to join portfolio company Wrapp as cofounder. After a stint at 500 Startups in San Francisco, he rejoined in 2016 as a Venture Partner, graduating to full time Partner in 2018. Carl is a tremendous asset to Creandum. He has been instrumental in building our Silicon Valley office and excelled in investments including Cornershop, recently sold to Uber for $3.5Bn. He shows boundless and fearless energy, generating superior dealflow across multiple regions, while driving efforts in areas like Diversity + Inclusion. And he does this as a core part of the team despite being miles (and timezones) away from our offices in Stockholm, Berlin and London. In short, we believe that Carl can carry Creandum's flag and help lead the team's development for many years to come. We are honoured to welcome Carl as Creandum's latest General Partner. He has been a part of the Creandum family for many years which makes this next step a natural evolution. Here's what he had to say about this experience: "I've now been part of the Creandum family for over 10 years, both as a team member in various roles as well as a portfolio founder. I have witnessed this firm's evolution from a regional Nordic player into pan-European, and how we've raised the bar of excellence on how to do VC across every dimension possible. During that time I've also experienced a similar journey myself. It feels like I have grown up together with Creandum in a beautiful harmony, and I couldn't be more excited to continue to build on that journey for many years to come." Carl is also a great partner for our entrepreneurs. He never gets tired of helping high and low and he's a big contributor in the boardroom when he needs to be. Which is why our founders have things to say like this: "Carl has inspired us to think big and continues to offer guidance and insight on a regular basis. One of things at YuLife that we look for in our investors is a shared sense of values and purpose. In Carl and the whole Creandum family we have found true partners in realising our vision. — Sammy, Co-founder and CEO at YuLife "Carl has had an active role with us throughout the Cornershop journey. Especially during our Series B fundraising he played an instrumental role supporting us with storyline, material as well as process. It's been a true joy to have Carl on our side. — Oskar, Co-founder & CEO at Cornershop In short, we believe that Carl is a person that can carry Creandum's flag and help lead the team's development for many years to come. And we know this is important to him. We'll give him the last word here: "Innovation is what makes us human. Our ability to exponentially transform and evolve the world we live in is what separates us from all other animals. And today, entrepreneurship is the most powerful tool to change the world around us. This is why what we do here is important. This is why I believe entrepreneurs are the real heroes of society. This is why I feel this is the best job in the world and I do it with a smile on my face every day." _This is part of a round of team updates at Creandum - [get the full picture here](https://blog.creandum.com/building-creandum-the-team-for-2022-and-beyond-884e168745bd)._

articles.title: Creandum goes London
articles.text: > "What happened down in the dungeons between you and Professor Quirrell is a complete secret, so, naturally the whole school knows." We are not comparing the social dynamics of VC to that of a wizarding boarding school (or are we!?) - but to some of you, the announcement we are now about to make will not come as a surprise. Regardless of your level of insight we are super excited to (finally) **officially** tell you that we at Creandum have leveled up and now have 12 feet on the ground in the UK! ## How it started, How it's going ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/1rr56PvlwfPFvS71wRnNq1/80c2e381402d5f3fb67c8f2e0b1cd54a/image_82.png) Two decades ago when Creandum was the new kid on the block we had the long-term ambition to build a globally leading firm. Looking back, perhaps we at least had a fraction of the drive (and positive naivety) that seems to be a common denominator amongst [the founders in our portfolio](https://www.creandum.com/portfolio/). Since that time we have taken steady steps, with regular intervals, to build the Creandum footprint across the European continent (and beyond). Creandum started making investments outside the Nordics in 2012. One year later we put [Johan Brenner](https://twitter.com/johanbrenner) **** on the ground in SF to build our office and presence there. Not only did we want to help portfolio companies make it in the US but we also wanted to make sure we had our ears to the ground and understood both the European and US investment landscape. In 2016 [Simon Schmincke](https://twitter.com/simonschmincke) opened the Berlin office and with great success managed to make DACH one of our most important regions. So does that mean we are now betting on the UK to become one of our most important regions? Well no, not really... ## ...Because it already is ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/2XtCxvFWt4zLJXAK3r7FmP/4af929230038dc525aefc7a81363e2fb/image_83.png) Just as VCs take bets on entrepreneurs, entrepreneurs do the same with VCs. We are thankful that [Simon](https://twitter.com/simonbeckerman), [Maria](https://twitter.com/MRaga_Depop), and all others in the Depop team dared to take a bet on us (via Fredrik) and become their partners and Creandum's first UK-headquartered investment. Not to mention for letting us follow their journey to becoming the leading Gen Z vintage marketplace in the UK and US - and [all the way to exit](https://blog.creandum.com/depop-organically-opening-the-hearts-and-wardrobes-of-gen-z-2c08d1783841). "Fredrik is one of the best investors on the EU tech scene. His support has been invaluable, not only financially but morally too. I truly valued his guidance as he helped get Depop to where it is today." - Maria Raga (Depop) We are also proud backers of Argent, where we felt an instant connection on how we consider product and the weight we put into making a great UX/UI experience. We are very excited that they let us join in the early days of their fantastic journey. Great things ahead! "Having built and sold one business with Creandum (Peak Labs), I knew they were the best partner from the earliest stages to help build ambitious product and culture." - Itamar Lesuisse (Argent) And there's more to be announced soon - we can't wait to tell you about the latest pre-seed / seed team that has chosen us and are now rocket-ship-fuelled-up. "What we really appriciated was that they had respect for that you haven't figured out all things at an early stage, plus their experience in taking companies from seed and beyond very successfully" - Stealth founder As you can hear, we have been excited about the UK for a long time, and this is why it has become the second-largest market for our last two funds (beside Sweden), and also one of the fastest-growing. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/7tLMGmf1jkXMAOKZBQgQ6e/d34a6c13a28fd1fbd67a7bab103bb566/image_84.jpg) ## We are (not) on a plane (or on a boat)... ...Or on Zoom for that matter. Having spent time on airports and planes Zooming into board meetings and founder calls, we ultimately asked ourselves: Why all this going back and forth? If the UK already is one of our core markets we should pay the respect to the ecosystems and founders that it deserves and make sure we are just a Boris-bike ride away. With the Monzo mafia, the Revolut mafia, the Depop mafia, Deliveroo mafia (and many more!), we feel the UK is more exciting than ever. And with more tech talent roaming the streets of London, Manchester, Oxford, Cambridge, Nottingham (the list goes on!) than ever before, we felt we couldn't stand a day longer only being blurry Zoom faces. ## Calling UK founders, operators, and investors! We* are extremely excited to take this next step in the history of Creandum. And although geographies change, investment focus is still the same as it has always been; being the first or one of the first institutional investors on the cap-table (i.e. pre-seed to Series A), of the most ambitious founders. We look forward to continuing to focus on the most important problems facing the planet and are excited about all aspects of consumer and software innovation that will play the part in the solution.
