articles.excerpt: Meet the Fellows
articles.text: We've been talking for years about the need for greater diversity and inclusion in VC - but if there's one thing we know, it's that no single organisation can change things alone. That's why we were delighted to speak with Nikita Thakrar and our friends at Notion from the earliest stages of Included VC. What nobody anticipated was just how the Fellowship would output a thriving community of talented individuals to fertilise the VC world. The number of those that have now graduated into positions in VC and related industries is testament to the fellowship's success. And yet, it also feels like just the start. As these cohorts progress through their careers, there's no doubt their presence and progress will lay the foundations for more and more to follow in their tracks. To celebrate the success of the fellowship so far, we wanted to highlight the journey of a few of the individuals that have taken place so far. Without further ado, let me hand over the stage to some recent Fellows to talk about their experiences with the fellowship and what they have been doing since. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/2ARq5mbVF03ZeXQjMjIoPR/207e7aacc9e07f3cc624f3427a6aa54f/image_81.jpg) _(Left to right)_ **[Munashe Dema](https://www.linkedin.com/in/munashe-dema/)**, **now at M12, [Swathi Damodharan](https://www.linkedin.com/in/swathi-dhamodaran/), Now at Blume Ventures, [Kadi-Ingrid Lilles](https://www.linkedin.com/in/kadiingrid/) Now at Silicon Allee** ### How did you get here - what led you to the moment in your career where this was the next step? **Swathi:** I graduated over the pandemic and was at a very early point in my career so it was something I had envisioned as a post-MBA career path.I enjoyed my job in tech and engineering but was always looking for ways to accelerate the timeline. I wanted to find a way to balance the depth of technology with the breadth of VC. **Kadi-Ingrid:** My career had been continuously building up to the shift towards the venture capital industry. I had been focusing on supporting startups and founders from the earliest of stages. Co-founding Estonia's first social enterprise incubator and interning at an early-stage VC firm in the Bay Area. Working on supporting and developing the Estonian startup ecosystem on a governmental level. A few years of working as an operator at early stage B2B SaaS platform startups in Berlin. I embarked on a bit of a professional soul-searching which led me to a realization VC would be the best course. **Munashe:** I had worked in hypergrowth UK startups such as Bulb Energy and LAMB, where I learned a multitude of skills, found deeply enriching, and which certified my desire to work in the startup ecosystem. However, I always felt I had an even deeper hunger to continue learning more and explore new startups, which could simply not be satiated by one startup. Through speaking to one of the founders at LAMB about their YC journey and startup financing generally, I realized venture capital may be the best path to satiate this hunger. I began my VC journey firstly by sending hundreds of unsolicited emails to VC firms globally, then many LinkedIn messages, and a multitude of internship applications. Quickly in the process, I did realize the venture industry operates as a closed network and I would need a different solution to break this barrier and at the same time, a friend familiar with the program sent me a link to Included VC. ### Why VC? Why is this the part of the ecosystem for you vs being in a startup or other directions? **Swathi:** What I was able to conclude with discussions was that **timing** is the most important piece of the puzzle. So when I reflected upon what I wanted to achieve over the next set of years, I realised that I value exposure across a broad range of verticals more than the depth of working in a startup. Meeting interesting people every day and being able to zoom in and out of different problem statements was very exciting for me. The Indian startup ecosystem is at an exciting point and I wanted to be able to be in an immersive environment where I can observe that. **Kadi-Ingrid:** For me, work in venture capital offers a unique mix of impact paired with continuous learning and development. This comes from being exposed to cutting-edge innovation, new business models, and inspirational founders as well as the drive to find and back the best startups, and provide meaningful value and support to the startups in one's portfolio and network. **Munashe:** VC offered me the opportunity to work with a range of talented entrepreneurs and learn about myriad interesting industries, whilst remaining at the forefront of technological advancements. Compared to asset management, I felt a VC career would provide a less structured path and exponential growth, unimpeded by the bounds of a corporate structure. At Blue Future Partners, I was given the space to turn my idea of an Africa-focused VC fund of funds into a product. Above all, the motivation for a career in venture capital stems from my desire to have a major positive impact on society through my work. Based on the impact I saw from VC-backed companies have on human life over the past 25 years, I felt a career in VC would give me the best opportunity to empower many communities and positively impact many lives. ### What was the most surprising aspect of the programme? What did you not expect? **Swathi:** It was without a doubt how helpful and tightly-knit the community of fellows became. While I did hear a lot about it, I had never been a part of one before to fully internalize it. I think it emerges from sharing so many commonalities in terms of aspirations and interests but also experiencing the many different versions of it from each Fellow. Between the 50 of us, we came from different countries, backgrounds, were at different points in life and that made it extremely refreshing. Applying for VC jobs can be a taxing process and I think being able to support each

articles.title: Populating the Metaverse — an Overview of the Early 2022 Landscape
articles.text: _by [Sabina Wizander](https://twitter.com/SabinaWizander) and [Beata Klein](https://twitter.com/axeliaklein)_ _This is part 1 of a 2 post series, you can find the second piece, about **securing** the metaverse here._ Because the marginal cost of copying something was zero, the Internet started as a place that removed the scarcity of the real world. Access became the keyword. Communication, information, trade, distribution - it all became significantly easier to dip into resources previously hard to attain. It also created a Web where aggregation (or centralization) was key, and companies such as [Zoom](https://zoom.us/), [Google](https://www.google.com/), [Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/), and [TikTok](https://www.tiktok.com/) flourished. They all made it worthwhile to spend much of your time online. We are now in the early innings of **a shift that is reclaiming scarcity**. Blockchain **increases** the marginal cost of digital assets and this decentralized ownership has created a third WWW shift, where our resources are transferring online much as our time has. With this combination of time and resources spent online, the idea of the Metaverse is getting closer and closer. **Inspired by our investment in [Scapin](https://www.scapin.app/)', this two-part series will discuss how we see the development of the Metaverse.** **The first piece will focus on the resources required to build a compelling Metaverse platform (spending time).** **The second piece will focus on the economic aspects of that platform (spending resources), with some inevitable overlap.** ## Virtual world ≠ Metaverse Virtual worlds and spaces have successfully existed for decades - we don't have to go far to find examples such as [Habbo (Hotel)](https://www.habbo.com/), [Second Life](https://secondlife.com/), [Fortnite](https://www.epicgames.com/fortnite/en-US/home), [Minecraft](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us), [WoW](https://worldofwarcraft.com/en-gb/). But none of them can be classified as a Metaverse. _"The metaverse is the moment in time where our digital life is worth more to us than our physical life" - [Shaan Puri](https://twitter.com/shaanvp/status/1454151237650112512?lang=en)_ Some adopt the definition of a Metaverse similar to the one given by [Shaan Puri](https://twitter.com/ShaanVP) - that it is a point in time. And others, like [Matthew Ball](https://twitter.com/ballmatthew/), see it as a 3D destination. _"The Metaverse is a massively scaled and interoperable network of real-time rendered 3D virtual worlds which can be experienced synchronously and persistently by an effectively unlimited number of users with an individual sense of presence, and with continuity of data, such as identity, history, entitlements, objects, communications, and payments." - [Matthew Ball](https://twitter.com/ballmatthew/)_ You can likely not create a destination if people don't perceive it as valuable - hence the latter is a possible effect of the former. Another definition is based on [the seven rules of the Metaverse](https://medium.com/meta-verses/the-seven-rules-of-the-metaverse-7d4e06fa864c), of which one states that "there is only one Metaverse". That is why one virtual world can never be called a Metaverse, and why Fortnite isn't a Metaverse but a possible virtual world/destination/node/zone in the Metaverse. ## The Opportunity: Building the Metaverse Since the start of 2021, we have seen a continued interest in building the Metaverse, and when Facebook became "Meta", the concept became mainstream. From then on, many other Web2 players spent an increasing amount of time and other resources to build out their Metaverse capabilities, with recent examples like [TikTok minting NFTs (not very successfully)](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/tiktok-nfts-lil-nas-x-bella-poarch-grimes-1266048/). See more below: ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/3d2Mibx9fE1t3ZpqMdkykK/e9f92c181b113277645ba43a1685d092/image_76.png) However, despite committing significant resources, **the battle between legacy players and startups isn't as unfair as it might seem**. This is because the community around Web3 favors decentralization (for reasons read: [Why Decentralisation Matters](https://onezero.medium.com/why-decentralization-matters-5e3f79f7638e)). With new and exciting initiatives launching every day, it's more about winning hearts and minds of entrepreneurs, developers, and early adopters than ‘just' committing capital. Below, we map out several interesting current initiatives based on five overarching categories we observe in the space. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/2YFtHJ248oqoRFZhi6bvTG/322d1c8b0db6bcf99c2f1a96ee59e251/image_77.png) It's important to keep in mind that while some form of delineation is necessary, the boundaries within Web3 are (and will be) fluent. While this adds additional complexity, it also makes studying it much more interesting and worthwhile. Let's dive deeper into each category and highlight some noteworthy European examples! **Let's start with Destinations,** in essence, virtual spaces in which individuals can explore, create, play, and interact with others online. We are particularly proud to back [Scapin'](https://www.scapin.app/) here, whose social communications platform aims to increase the sense of connection and expression in online conversations. For a long time, all we have had to work with when socialising online is text, images and video. VR came along but didn't hold up to many of its promises. The latest generation of companies are trying to change this by making us even MORE expressive online than in real life. Other interesting players in this space are for example [Uku](https://uku.wtf/), also with strong conversational focus, or [Cosmos](https://cosmos.video/), your virtual node for work. Of course, any kind of interaction presupposes a sense of identity - in the case of Web3, an **Online Identity.** The beauty of Web3 is that one's online identity is completely independent o

articles.title: Leveling up
articles.author: Carl Fritjofsson
articles.excerpt: Introducing Creandum’s DE&I Policy
articles.text: When you [keep](https://blog.creandum.com/diversity-inside-european-vc-2-0-limited-progress-made-f89479fe3738) [saying](https://blog.creandum.com/a-small-sign-of-progress-on-gender-diversity-in-tech-915c85ac9221) [the same](https://blog.creandum.com/introducing-a-hands-on-knowledge-bank-to-drive-diversity-and-inclusion-in-tech-54d00f629677) [thing](https://blog.creandum.com/under-the-hood-of-diversity-2021-creandum-diversity-index-14caa8a6dd4e), there's a risk it loses impact. So let's really take a moment to hit this one home: **Diverse** **businesses** **perform** **better.** But it takes more than rhetoric to bring this change into the world. Just as our language must be explicit, we must lead by example with crystal clear initiatives and targets that show how the whole industry can get there. Historically, that has meant efforts including launching our annual [Diversity Index](https://blog.creandum.com/under-the-hood-of-diversity-2021-creandum-diversity-index-14caa8a6dd4e), leading the effort at [Included VC](https://blog.creandum.com/creandum-x-included-vc-meet-the-fellows-d9d4f3a97d67) and highlighting non-obvious role models in our own visuals and materials. Today, we want to take it one step further by sharing [Creandum's Diversity, Equality and Inclusion Policy](https://www.craft.do/s/u0rQUXoy3ZmoS6) which we have designed to make a difference for ourselves and our portfolio. In short, at Creandum we believe in 3 things: 1. We believe in equal rights for all people regardless of social identity across areas like gender, race, ethnic origin, nationality or sexual orientation. And beyond rights, we also believe in equal opportunities for all. Everyone deserves the same opportunity at Creandum, and it is an equal partnership where the economics of the firm are split according to equal pay for equal work. 2. We believe diverse teams perform better. This is a deliberate repetition as it's worth repeating. Fundamentally as a VC and startup, we operate in the unknown. We try to understand today what tomorrow will look like. Triangulating diverse perspectives is one of the most potent ways to do this. Hence, we believe diversity is not compliance... it's business-critical. 3. We believe in meritocracy. Any investment or people decisions made by the fund are based solely on the conviction and performance of such individuals and companies, and never on diversity traits. Creandum simply aspires to work with the best. But finding the best requires effort. The best come in all shapes and sizes. We have to remind ourselves that in order to find the best, we cannot only look where it feels obvious. ## Initiatives To force us out of biases and push the fund and portfolio to embrace diversity, we have deployed a range of initiatives as part of the policy. The current focus is specifically gender and ethnic origins and aimed at three dimensions of Creandum's activities: ### The Creandum organization - In all hiring processes at Creandum, we commit to building a candidate pipeline which at the final round should include at least 50% of candidates who are of underrepresented gender or ethnic origin. - All mentors are committed to inclusive leadership, which means: - We treat everyone with fairness and respect. - We appreciate everyone's uniqueness. - We do our utmost to provide resources and support for everyone to achieve their full potential. - We use gender-neutral language. - We measure inclusion in our team twice per year. - Creandum employees are encouraged to combine parenthood and work, and the firm understands and supports the practical implications of this with for example flexible work hours. We also believe parenthood should be distributed equally regardless of gender, and hence gives everyone across all our offices up to 9 months of 100% paid parental leave irrespective of local state-funded leave. - At least every 2nd year conduct unconscious bias training across the entire team - When the firm acquires services, such as for example legal, banking, or recruiting, we ask such providers to staff our project with diverse team members across gender and/or ethnic origins. ### Creandum's investment advisory activities - In our internal documentation for every investment recommendation, we include a dedicated section on the topic of what the company is doing and how they're thinking about DE&I. - In our term sheet, we have a specific clause stating the company's commitment to DE&I as well as broader ESG. - When the fund is leading a round, we do our utmost to involve and invite angel investors of diverse backgrounds. - We proactively support and help portfolio companies to improve their DE&I with practical tools and best practices. - For any follow-on investment recommendation, the company must prove progress and actions related to DE&I. - Once a year we survey the entire portfolio on gender diversity across their team and externally publish the results. - Once a year we measure gender distribution in the top end of the deal flow funnel. ### Entrepreneurial ecosystem development - Maintain and promote [Creandum's DE&I Knowledge Bank](https://www.craft.do/s/9yrez4a3nfsPqq) for anyone to use. - For any event hosted by Creandum, ensure participation of all genders and people of different ethnic origins. - In all visual external communications (e.g. website, job descriptions), help build non-obvious role models by highlighting women and people of different ethnic origins. - Whenever invited to speak at an event where diversity is missing, offer up Creandum's seat on stage to females and people of underrepresented ethnic origins. ## Targets Without real goals, a plan is just an ambition. Hence, in addition to the range of initiatives above, we have decided to take this one step further by setting explicit targets for ourselves related to DE&I. Our 3 targets are ambitious to us, and they span across what we believe are the most important and measurable areas, and they come with different time hori
