articles.text: _Read more about our latest fund in [Sifted](https://sifted.eu/articles/creandum-vc-500m-fund/), [tech.eu](https://tech.eu/2022/03/01/early-backers-of-unicorns-including-klarna-and-spotify-creandum-unleashes-its-newest-fund-at-500-million), [BusinessInsider](https://www.businessinsider.de/gruenderszene/business/halbe-milliarde-creandum-neuer-fonds/), [DI](https://www.di.se/digital/creandum-stanger-ny-fond-pa-nara-5-miljarder-oppnar-for-kryptoinvesteringar/), [faz.net](https://www.faz.net/aktuell/finanzen/creandum-schliesst-500-millionen-dollar-fonds-17841083.html), [FinanceFWD](https://financefwd.com/de/creandum-fonds/), [Tech Funding News](https://techfundingnews.com/stockholm-investor-creandum-that-backs-many-european-unicorns-raises-500m/), [Shifter](https://shifter.no/notis/creandum-med-nytt-fond-pa-500-millioner-dollar/238966), [EU-startups](https://www.eu-startups.com/2022/03/stockholm-based-vc-firm-creandum-closes-new-e448-million-fund-to-back-eu-founders-at-the-earliest-stages/), [Silicon Canals](https://siliconcanals.com/news/startups/swedish-creandum-gets-448m/), [ArcticStartup](https://arcticstartup.com/creandum-has-d500m/), [pymnts](https://www.pymnts.com/news/investment-tracker/2022/creandum-closes-500m-early-stage-investment-fund-for-eu-tech-companies/), [L'Entrepreneur](https://lentrepreneur.co/innovation/b2b/linvestisseur-spotify-creandum-leve-448-millions-deuros-dans-son-sixieme-fonds-de-demarrage-01032022), [KapWatch](https://kapwatch.dk/nyheder/venturefonde/article13783439.ece)_ For nearly twenty years, Creandum has committed to entrepreneurs whose products change the world. We are excited to continue this journey with a new $500m fund: Creandum VI. Heavily oversubscribed and backed by the leading institutions globally, we will continue our work supporting companies across Europe and the US from the earliest stages. ### Continued commitment to the earliest stages Today, 1 in 8 of Creandum's portfolio companies are unicorns - loved by billions worldwide. But that's only half the story. Brands like Spotify, iZettle and Trade Republic have become household names. Yet when we met them it was just Daniel, Jacob, Christian and a vision. The early stage is where we have always been most comfortable. We commit to founders **before** the world catches on, **before** everyone knows, **before it's obvious.** Creandum VI will continue on this path. This **commitment** means patience and relentless support throughout the highs and lows of every entrepreneurial journey. This commitment is what differentiates us from those who think value is created in the short term. Our job is not to know better, but to inspire with the questions that don't come to mind as easily. ### Continued focus on those who build the best products Today, competition across every category of innovation is fierce. But in our experience, founders who focus on building the best products still prevail. Those who dare to think in generational opportunities and solutions will succeed by virtue of their burning passion for product excellence. Time and again, we have witnessed the success, not of those who run the fastest, but of those who never lose track of the problems they aim to solve. Those who care for the details others overlook. Those who focus on the core needs of their customers and create the best experiences. **To those who dare to change the world: You are the entrepreneurs we seek for Creandum VI.** ### Continued trust from the most renowned global institutions Each Creandum fund over the last fifteen years now holds valuations between 6x and 13x. With Creandum VI, we are extremely excited to add some of the most renowned universities, endowments, foundations, and institutions globally to the circle of partners who put trust in us. In addition, we welcome back every single LP from every single Creandum fund since the beginning of our journey. **To our partners: thank you for your continued and new support.** ### Continued change within the firm As a firm, we have also continued our work in diversity, equity, and inclusion by updating [our Diversity Index](https://blog.creandum.com/tagged/diversity) on proportions of diversity within our team and our portfolio. We have introduced a [new DE&I policy](https://blog.creandum.com/leveling-up-introducing-creandums-de-i-policy-3d85ff83914e) with clear targets and commitments. The subject has been close to our hearts - and we are proud to have now publicly committed to positive change. Finally, Creandum today is a truly international venture firm. We once started in Stockholm - the true roots in our company culture and product DNA. The addition of the San Francisco office helped us shape our understanding of true global products and offer network support between the two continents. Berlin paved the way to become the leading early stage venture fund in Europe. With the addition of our London Office at the end of last year, Creandum today operates close to the entrepreneurs in four of the most vibrating startup ecosystems globally. A lot of things continue with Creandum VI - in and around the firm. Yet, looking back at almost 20 years of early stage investing, seeing the state of the European Ecosystem today, and working with a fund that enables us to help shape the digital world like never before: **we could not be more excited, to back the companies of tomorrow, like it was day one here at Creandum.**

articles.title: Creandum + Product + Ellen (our new associate)
articles.text: I know I speak for the whole team when I say we are very excited to welcome our new Associate in Stockholm, [Ellen Lee](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ellenleelbs/). She joins our growing array of product expertise at Creandum, including [Built For Mars](https://builtformars.com) creator and globally renowned UX expert, Peter Ramsey, and our Designer-in-Residence, [Felix Haas](https://www.felixhaas.io). With our Nordic heritage, we are spoiled by great design. And we've had the privilege to back fantastic product-obsessed teams at Spotify, Kry, [iZettle](https://www.zettle.com/de), [Vivino](https://www.vivino.com/DE/de), [Klarna](https://www.klarna.com/), [Cornershop](https://cornershopapp.com/en/), [Trade Republic](https://traderepublic.com/de-de) and [Taxfix](https://taxfix.de/), to name a few. Ellen comes with the hard-to-beat combination of **business student** gone **self-taught developer** gone **product manager**. Having graduated from London Business School with a Masters degree in Management, she started her career at Arla Foods on commercial strategy and consumer product innovation. Curious about technology and passionate about building valuable products, she decided coding was a key skill and trained to become a software developer. This led to a fascination for tech products and from there, a move into product management. Most recently, she led one of Anyfin's product teams in Stockholm, where she focused on product development and managed teams of designers, developers and data analysts. In her own words: "I'm always excited about turning ideas from paper to tangible products. To me, this means tuning into users' needs, and going above and beyond to create solutions that bring value to consumers and businesses. It takes team effort and the right balance between user and business objectives to deliver a roaring product success. " "I'm thrilled to transition into the venture capital space and work with inspiring entrepreneurs and product enthusiasts, scouting out powerful products with stellar user experience!" Originally from Taiwan, Ellen has been a citizen of the world for the last few years and we are so very happy to welcome her to the Creandum team.

articles.title: “Show us the money”
articles.excerpt: And other inspiring thoughts from 5 female founders
articles.text: 1% of venture capital, 12% of senior investors and 19% of C-suite. This is women's share of the tech industry. No one can say that gender equality "has gone too far". It hasn't gone far enough and it's not moving fast enough. There is massive untapped potential for **the whole industry** if we can become better at using all of the talent pool. And with the war for talent increasing, and Gen Z becoming a main source of talent, this is no longer something that you need to feel good. It's business critical. They say: "If you can see it you can be it". I also believe **"if you can see it you can hire it/fund it**"**. Role models play an important part for everyone.** I had the luxury of speaking to these five role-models, founders and business leaders on their motivation, experiences and what needs to change. ### [Jennifer Phan](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jenniferphn/), Founder and CEO [Passionfroot](https://www.passionfroot.xyz/) **On founding a company:** "The fascination of using technology to solve problems and make a big impact. I think starting a company is a way to create a world which I hope to see." ![Jennifer Phan, Photo: Passionfroot](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/2WCiMY3BJoFELBRWXAli3X/fe6af6e637134f465c87f969d214e2c0/image_72.jpg) **On (the additional) challenges being a female founder:** "Building a company and raising funding is obviously difficult for everyone, but due to the lack of equality in tech, female founders usually face unconscious bias, lack of role models and mentors, weaker networks and fighting for their legitimacy." ### [Michelle Kennedy](https://www.linkedin.com/in/michellekennedy2/), founder and CEO, [Peanut](https://www.peanut-app.io/) **On what is needed to empower more women to found companies:** "Honestly, women do start businesses. But, we have to level the playing field here in terms of access to networks and access to finance." " What we don't need is mentorship, specific programs or accelerators for women-led businesses (which pit us against one another). What we need is equal access, and funding. We simply need funding - show us the money!" **On (the additional) challenges being a female founder:** "The challenge here is unconscious bias. It's real, and it's there. It's there in so many ways - if you can only be what you can see, and you can only see men building fast growth companies, raising funding, you wonder whether it's for you." "Similarly if you're in venture, and your pipeline looks like you, there is a comfort and familiarity there - a security in investing in a founder who went to the same school, or has a similar profile. Given the majority of those in venture are still men, it's self-perpetuating that more men are funded." ![Michelle Kennedy, Photo: Peanut](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/5Gs8X7hg3cZ4OBjdX3QaOT/adfde997d1335a6b58e338fc3cbedd8d/image_73.jpg) ### [Aiga Senftleben](https://www.linkedin.com/in/aiga-senftleben-38762459/), Co-Founder and General Counsel at [Billie](https://www.billie.io/?utm_source=google&utm_medium=cpc&matchtype=e&utm_term=billie&gclid=Cj0KCQiAmpyRBhC-ARIsABs2EApI2ROEGnFxOd4176uLeiYrOo5tdHEqu8O_XhA_baj3WTVfMcA756caAodeEALw_wcB) **On whether female founders have certain strengths that male founders normally don't:** "Female CEOs certainly attract female talent to a company - and in times of the "War on Talent" - this is surely a super power" ![Aiga Senftleben, Photo: Billie](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/6XBN8DuNyOdcd4D5VmtlG1/d1f56049bfd3110ac0843769a6090571/image_74.jpg) **On (the additional) challenges being a female founder:** "I see additional challenges in the personal lives of women: when I left my job to start Billie, people would ask why I had left a secure and well-paid job in order to start a new company. The fact that I was pregnant when founding Billie got even more people questioning me. I think it is easy to be discouraged by these comments" ### [Charlotte Pallua](https://www.linkedin.com/in/pallua/), [Estelle Merle](https://www.linkedin.com/in/estelle-merle-07aaa165/), founders [Topi](https://www.topi.eu/) **On whether female founders have strengths that male founders normally don't:** "(Not to generalise men and women but...) the way we are trying to build topi is being very thoughtful about a few items: having an open and diverse culture, be performance-driven, but not aggressive, have a no face-time culture, have a culture that is based on trust and flexibility. In our second week we jointly defined our core values and working norms and try to live by them every day." "Starting a company is definitely very intense and challenging (and also very fun), but we honestly don't think we face different challenges than men. We have never experienced any adversity - actually quite the contrary, funds were excited about two female founders, in most interviews we hear that candidates say that it's refreshing to work for a female-led company." "There are of course some funny anecdotes, like a big fund addressing us in an email with ‘Gentlemen' or that MDs of a GmbH don't by default in the law get parental leave. But we don't take those things personally." ### [Caroline Ingeborn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/carolineingeborn/), founder and CEO [Leap](https://www.leapchats.com/) **On (the additional) challenges being a female founder:** "I think it's problematic that there are so few female founders out there, especially who have reached unicorn status. Without this sort of female representation, it's harder for women to imagine themselves succeeding. There is also the issue of access to capital. We all have inherent biases, myself included. As the vast majority of capital is still controlled by men, this impacts who gets funded." ![Caroline Ingeborn, Photo: Creandum](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/3IjZQ7CIqaOur7iXPPVszh/bdc8dd207be3e3110e2fac0802221120/image_75.jpg) **On what is needed to empower more women to start companies:** "Start sooner! We need to talk about the fear of failur

articles.title: Creandum welcomes ArK Kapital!
articles.author: Johan Brenner
articles.text: _Read more about ArK Kapital's funding at [Sifted](https://sifted.eu/articles/ark-kapital-financing-startups/), [tech.eu](https://tech.eu/2022/03/29/ark-kapital-raises-eur165-million-to-offer-long-term-alternative-financing-options/) and [DI](https://www.di.se/digital/sa-ska-eqt-och-nordea-veteraner-fa-bolag-att-avsta-riskkapital/)._ While venture capital bends over backwards to win the best founders, it is still much harder for fast-growing startups to secure other forms of financing from traditional banks. The simple reason is they just don't have the data they usually require to feel confident - startups have limited history, near to no profits and are therefore considered far too risky. [ArK Kapital](https://www.arkkapital.com/) is here to change this. By using operational data and applying their own well-trained algorithms, they are able to assess risks in ways that banks simply can't. This is important because there are many situations where equity financing is just not a sensible answer. Many of the most common forms of growth simply don't need an equity approach, with accompanying dilution and other challenges. If it's about CapEx investments or inventory-building, there's nothing wrong with using old-fashioned debt financing. Because they can access operational data, ArK Kapital makes its lending decisions based the fundamentals of the business, not just an outsider's historical perspective or the assets on the balance sheet. This lets them offer something that has never been done before on a broader scale: Long-term growth loans for young companies. On top of having a more accurate picture at underwriting, ArK also has access to real life data during the loan period. This allows them to spot signs of downturn before it happens and suggest solutions with their customers. And furthermore, they provide access to these same kinds of dashboards with their customers, aligning everyone around best in class growth tools that protect the future of the business. **As Henrik Landgren, Co founder of ArK, says:** "The average tech company has 500 million rows of data updated daily. It is used daily to optimize business activities but no one has taken the opportunity to convert this into attractive financing options." There are parallels here with revenue-based financing. But the financing case and underlying risk are completely different. While Pipe.com, Wayflyer and co. focus on short term working capital loans, ArK wants to finance companies over several years until they reach or get closer to profitability. This lets them become a stronger and more valuable business partner that really helps startups to grow the fundamentals of their business faster - not just a stopgap solution. Ultimately, we believe ArK can become much much more than a lending company. By providing precise risk assessment also to other lenders, they will eventually become the finance platform of the future. **A Winning Team** Becoming the global financing platform of the future is going to take a hell of a team and we believe ArK has it. [Oliver](https://www.linkedin.com/in/oliver-hildebrandt-15755415b/?miniProfileUrn=urn%3Ali%3Afs_miniProfile%3AACoAACZYnNMBnCUIe2eYCvFA1XJDENEtmajcKdo), [Axel](https://www.linkedin.com/in/axel-bruzelius-003264/?miniProfileUrn=urn%3Ali%3Afs_miniProfile%3AACoAAAAJmQMBI03tCo6KIdrgwKUi1mHGyMtqj5M), [Henrik](https://www.linkedin.com/in/henriklandgren/?miniProfileUrn=urn%3Ali%3Afs_miniProfile%3AACoAAABPfzEBXu5D3Obb2e0iK2RV7zz_PZpLnHA), and the rest of the ArK team combine company-building in various fintechs, lending at Nordea and data analytics at Spotify and [Motherbrain](https://eqtgroup.com/motherbrain) among others. They're equally able to hire the best - among them [Julia](https://www.linkedin.com/in/julia-ehrhardt-141972/) as CFO and [Elin](https://www.linkedin.com/in/backlnd/) as CTO. To the entire ArK team, welcome to Creandum, and here's to broadening the finance options for the best startups out there!​​ ![From left to right: Henrik (CPTO), Elin (CTO), Axel (COO), Oliver (CEO) and Julia (CFO)](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/VWIuPi5TGHj1qVNoFmlGO/bdb925f0e0523963a8dca84da021c0e9/image_71.jpg)

articles.title: Cognitive noise: something for your UX toolbelt (in 60 seconds)
articles.author: Peter Ramsey
articles.text: Let's talk about **cognitive noise**, and how it can make you a better designer—in 60 seconds or less. Firstly, most drivers are familiar with the concept of **stopping distance**. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/3UNufBM3jERoZ2PSNhGEaR/df4a8016373f9ed11b44583a62534e3b/image_66.jpg) In short: stopping a car isn't all about tyres. You have something called ‘reaction time'. This is however long it takes you to go: "_oh s**t, I need to brake_". Well, there's a similar concept that occurs when using digital products and services: **digestion time**. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/SuRmvgghYZBK2HuozWxb9/9fb0509b88aed12938b0f6573af97e83/image_67.jpg) It takes some time to work out what you're _being asked to do_, before you can then go ahead and do it. For example, you have some onboarding, and then _!WHAM!_, you land on a screen with un-labelled fields, and you need to work out what to do. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/HstCQ7eG3Cv5xEMpv39Jd/e5153a78816e4777a768c3e07db6a4a1/image_68.png) _"Okay, I'm customising something, but what?" -_ **This is your digestion time**. We call it **cognitive noise**, because it's the noise that drowns out the purpose of a page. It's everything that inhibits the user's understanding. Here's the kicker; it's **notoriously hard to measure**. Often, people will conduct user testing, and give the participant some context (for example, while watching a user create a ‘goal' in a dashboard): ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/3AqmiwUIDRl87355YOdcAF/4aa77b4f96fee16352db07a5952bb7bf/image_69.png) But that context bypasses the natural digestion window. **It's like telling someone in their driving test that they're about to perform an emergency brake test**. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/5dPvt2b4nMQNOWvIvTFxE5/36a85be5aa6cdf3d488394dc4a6ff19e/image_70.jpg) Let's recap: - Cognitive noise is how we measure ‘digestion time'. - Digestion time is how long it takes you to realise what you need to do next. - People rarely think about digestion time, and even fewer accurately measure it. **So, what can we (product builders) do to remove noise?** Here are 3 actionable and practical takeaways: - Ensure every action has a **clear label**. - **Add context** wherever possible, even priming the user about contextual leaps that are _about_ to happen. (i.e., _"next, we'll ask for your phone number..."_). - **Remove unnecessary elements** (words, images and features—everything that isn't necessary, is noise). Phew, was that 60 seconds? I think so. _If you want longer UX analysis, just like this, you can see a more detailed breakdown of cognitive noise over at [Built for Mars](https://builtformars.com/case-studies/revolut-junior)._

articles.title: Securing the Metaverse
articles.excerpt: Taking the Wild West Out of Web3 Financials
articles.text: _by [Beata Klein](https://twitter.com/axeliaklein) and [Sabina Wizander](https://twitter.com/SabinaWizander)_ **625 MUSD (or 173,600 Eth + 25.5 million in USDC) stolen.** Being a part of the Web3 financial system today is equal parts exciting and terrifying. This is something the [Axie Infinity](https://axieinfinity.com) community learned the hard way last week with [the Ronin bridge hack](https://roninblockchain.substack.com/p/community-alert-ronin-validators?s=w). Fortunately, the Axie community is a strong one and they will get through this. At the same time, we see equally clever, if not more clever, individuals building for the good in this space. And they are spurred by the chance to add something new, with the potential monetary upside if they are successful. We have previously [written about the Metaverse from the perspective of interface and time](https://blog.creandum.com/populating-the-metaverse-an-overview-of-the-early-2022-landscape-10bd153d0d37). In this piece we want to take you on a journey throughout the resource layer , asking what makes up the basis for trade and ownership in a digital environment, and how we can keep these assets safe. ## Why Web3 and Creators are a Match While Web2 was great in allowing us to instantly distribute information, connect, and communicate at zero marginal cost, it also produced highly centralized structures as a byproduct. It goes without saying that the digital platforms of Web2 became immensely powerful and increasingly set up ‘the rules of the game' in their own interest, e.g. by changing underlying service terms at will, with often dramatic consequences for small and medium-sized creators. Web3 is a direct reaction to these problems, aiming to shift power from network orchestrators back to the initial value creators. **** In Web3 the core idea is that ownership is decentralized and driven by a tightly-knit community that strongly believes in these advantages. It gives power back to the creator and his/hers community both for ownership but also for reward. ## Our Digital Identities We believe that enabling creators (developers, designers, artists etc.) to better take charge of their own content and revenue through digital scarcity will be instrumental in the shift to strengthening our digital identities. Recall the definition we had set for ourselves of the Metaverse, as: "the moment in time where our digital life is worth more to us than our physical life" - [Shaan Puri](https://twitter.com/shaanvp/status/1454151237650112512?lang=en) So when comes the inflection point when our digital identity is worth more than our physical one? A partial answer to that is when our online assets are worth more as status markers than our physical ones. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/fwPmlYgK5lmonOpKVt5PV/797a68e1b39320a1f6af81a84e501d51/image_62.png) If we look at the evolution of valuable assets, it has deviated throughout time. The value a certain asset holds is largely defined by a social agreement between individuals that it could be exchanged for that value. If previously it was the red tie, the expensive watch or the fast car, now we see celebrities such as [Justin Bieber buying his way into the Bored Ape Yacht Club](https://www.highsnobiety.com/p/justin-bieber-bored-ape-nft/) via his 1.3 MUSD purchase of Bored Ape #3001. Or displaying your wallet address in your Twitter profile as a way to show your commitment to Web3. In any case, in order to transition to the Metaverse "point in time", we need assets that people are interested in buying, we need to have a functioning social agreement around value, and we need to have a system that enables trades, safekeeping, and prevent theft. **In this piece we will discuss these requirements from two different perspectives:** 1. **The Web3 Asset Layer;** 2. **Safeguarding and storing Web3 Assets** ## The Web3 Asset Layer For creators, it is an obvious advantage to leverage the power of decentralization. It enables them to monetize by launching tokens or NFTs, giving fans a way to ‘invest' in them while also gaining benefits like early access to premium content. The initial value creator will naturally benefit most from the creations but can also choose to share the further upside with fans by giving ownership rights to token holders. Ownership also incentivizes each community member to drive engagement and improve the overall community. _More companies building out the asset layer are popping up all the time:_ ![European examples are specifically highlighted in the text below.](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/2JNVJaF0hAftK0PWjeTKUo/0238153545873a9d6c44f3f99485c86a/image_63.png) **Asset creation**. This category shows the interaction between creators and Web3 by enabling individuals to create and monetize their content across a variety of verticals such as music ([Anotherblock](https://anotherblock.io/)), sports ([Liquidi Team](https://www.liquidi.team/)), art ([DoinGud](https://doingud.com/)), and many more. **Asset marketplaces.** Once the individual creations have been minted, they can be traded across specialized and general asset marketplaces**,** such as [La Collection](https://lacollection.io/) or [Mintbase](https://www.mintbase.io/)**,** which are supported by a variety of infrastructure tools providing compliance or helping with on-chain custody and distribution. **Social money and community incentives**. [Melon](https://melon.ooo/), for instance, allows creators to launch their DAOs as a way to build a community for their fans and enable them access through holding NFTs of the creator's work. ## Safeguarding and Storing Web3 Assets We started this article by mentioning the recent Ronin Hack. This instance is by no means an event in isolation. Since the start of this year, tokens, stablecoins, and NFTs have been exploited for a [total value of over 1 BUSD](https://cryptosec.info/defi-hacks/). At the same time, Open Sea admits that [more than 80% of the assets created for free on the pl

articles.title: Creandum x Packfleet
articles.excerpt: An interview with Cofounder Tristan Thomas
articles.text: ## A short Q&A with Co-founder, Tristan Thomas ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/5nHm486wpumnYDumnI83dt/a2d8e1a809aabd088a4cdf792df03ba7/image_61.jpg) ### Why has nobody fixed the delivery experience already? Why is it so bad? What we've seen in this market historically is that it's dominated by a small number of large incumbents. They were started decades ago and so have a huge amount of baggage, both technological and bureaucratic, heaped upon them. Until recently, that's been "good enough" but consumer expectations are changing. We live in a world where you can get hot food delivered to your door in 30 minutes or order a cab and track it right to your door, but your parcel deliveries still randomly turn up (or don't!) when you least expect them. Technology gives us an opportunity to change this. By combining deep tech expertise with operational rigour, we believe we can provide a world-class product and service to retailers, both big and small. And if by doing so, we can also provide them with a better alternative than working with companies named after large rivers, then all the better! ### What are the biggest lessons you're bringing from your time at Monzo? The importance of customer focus. For too long this industry has relied on apathy to keep customers, and the products that both retailers and recipients have to use are incredibly outdated. We're spending as much time as we possibly can really understanding what customers want and building a product that solves their problems. It's a market that's eerily similar to the banking market in many ways and we want to be that challenger to the big players in the same way that Monzo was to the big banks. ### Tell us about how you are building the company. How are you thinking about culture, talent etc? Remote vs local working? There are a few things here that are really important to us: transparency, autonomy, empathy and ambition. I believe we can build the best company if we are radically transparent internally, to allow and enable all of our team to build context and make decisions themselves rather than rely on hierarchical decision making. Alongside that, this is a deeply human business - we work with atoms, not just bits, so we need to understand the human element just as much as the tech side. One example of the ways we do this is by encouraging all of our team to do at least one day of deliveries every month, so everyone can understand exactly what it involves - and by extension, build a better product for our delivery team and therefore offer a better service for our customers and their recipients. Today, we run a hybrid local work setup. We have a cool railway arch in South East London that we use as both our office and our warehouse space - having everything and everyone in close physical proximity is incredibly useful for an early stage company as we figure things out. We try to spend approximately 2 days/week in the office together and then work remotely for the rest of the week; but at the core of this is flexibility, so if someone wants to work in the office everyday, that's great. And vice versa, if life gets in the way and you need to go to a doctor's appointment rather than come in, that's also great. In the long term, who knows; we try not to be blindly ideological about this but instead make sensible decisions where we treat everyone like adults! ### Why Creandum? We were incredibly impressed by the team at Creandum. They put in a huge amount of work to understanding us, understanding our business and understanding the market that we operate in. That, combined with their deep expertise in building companies at an early stage like ours, made it an easy decision for us to take and we couldn't be more excited about them joining us on this journey. ## Why we invested - Welcome Packfleet! Next day delivery in the UK is broken. Packfleet is here to create a green, technology-first, customer-centric delivery experience for everyone, and we are proud to support them on this journey. Few people would say their delivery experience delights them. As a consumer you often miss packages, or unexpectedly find them on your doorstep for anyone to find. As a merchant, the signup, pricing, and pickup experience are often at the very least confusing and time consuming, and in the worst case the case of errors and high costs the consumer ultimately pays for. Every ecommerce company we spoke to, large or small, was keen to get a better delivery experience, as this directly translates into higher customer satisfaction and reorder rates. Moreover, many companies and their customers were looking for green delivery options, aware that delivery can be up to 40% of the carbon footprint of an online retailer. Enter Packfleet - a seamless merchant and customer experience, driven by agile and innovative technology built for this day and age, and executed by a deeply committed, highly vetted team of employed drivers in electric vans. From the moment we met Tristan, Hugo and Josh, we were incredibly impressed with their vision of revolutionizing delivery, and their relentless focus on using technology to create a differentiated customer experience as well as create true efficiencies and a seamless green delivery experience. Product is in our DNA at Creandum. We believe Product Conquers All - and it was clear to us that the Packfleet team shared this. We are excited to partner with them and cannot wait to support their journey to bring a superb delivery experience to everyone.

articles.title: Why you’re clueless after shipping product
articles.author: Carl Fritjofsson
articles.excerpt: How Bucket helps
articles.text: ## Why you're clueless after shipping product - and how Bucket helps One of the privileges of working at Creandum is that we get to join founders for their journey, and get to know and collaborate with them through the twists and turns. The impact of this is that, when they are ready to start something new, we know they mean business. And they know Creandum is a partner who will be there when it matters. It's nearly five years since Rasmus and Ron [sold their last company Opbeat to Elastic](https://blog.creandum.com/creandum-backed-opbeat-acquired-by-elastic-a988f53c81f2). Creandum was a proud seed investor of the company, and we saw the founders go on to experience hyperscale as Elastic grew across the world and eventually IPO'd. And here we are again. The same co-founders are now ready for another rodeo, and also this time with Creandum by their side! World, meet [Bucket](http://bucket.co/) - _the feature company_! ## Blindly building product It almost sounds ridiculous when you say it like this, but the fundamental of day to day product development is adding and improving features. Today, software companies assemble engineers, designers and PMs around the scope of "One feature at a time". They spend months scoping, designing, and building a new feature. The end of such work is then celebrated when the team eventually ships said feature, announcing this at a townhall and newsletter. Meanwhile, someone in product analytics is reviewing the big picture and may look at conversion rates, active users, monetization or other "product aggregate" metrics to understand any impact on the product's overall performance. Bucket Co-founder, Rasmus puts it this way: "I don't actually think there's any "hand over" from feature team to product analytics team. Often, the analytics people just aren't in tune with what features are being released. They just report on aggregate numbers." "Sometimes they may do ad-hoc deep dives on a certain feature, but that's flaky and inconsistent. And often, these ad-hoc reports are impossible to compare as they're done by different people, use different definitions and look different." "We want to take the ad-hoc feature analysis and make it a consistent, repeatable, natural extension of the current product development workflow. For anyone to successfully do this, the product has to be treating features as a first-class citizen." The challenge here is that product analytics is an abstract of the entirety of your product. There are many reasons why conversion rates may change. How much of that is tied to the latest feature launch? How many of your users actually used that feature? And how do users who use that feature differ in their behaviour from others who don't? Plain and simple: does the feature have the business impact it was intended to have? You don't really know. You operate in the dark. And maybe even more importantly, why does the team of engineers, designers and PMs celebrate shipping the feature and move on? Why are they not held accountable that the feature delivers the intended results it was designed for? How can the work be done when the feature is shipped, vs when the feature delivers the intended results? How much can they improve the feature post initial release, if they aren't also held accountable for perfecting and optimizing that same feature? Fundamentally: **if you work in _Features_ but think in _Product_, you're always going to have a disconnect** that threatens your ability to understand and improve success clearly. This brings us to [Bucket](http://bucket.co/). ## Building with Bucket Bucket is designed to bring product workflows and decision-making down to the feature level, repairing the void between ownership and tracking. This creates the opportunity for features to live longer in scope, as teams learn where and how to prioritise their efforts for maximum iterative impact. With Bucket, companies no longer celebrate shipping a new feature (which in all honesty is vanity) but rather celebrate feature success. With Bucket you also bring a level of transparency to engineers and PMs. It's no longer about submitting code, but it's in fact about submitting the code that actually has the most optimal and intended impact. This is like turning the light on for product development that has been operating in the dark for so long. Bucket's Rasmus again: "It helps engineering managers prioritize their resources. What should the 500 engineers be working on the next month? New features or fixing existing broken features? Now they finally know." ## Product conquers all This company really hits home for us. At Creandum, we believe True Product Conquers All. If product isn't the answer, you're asking the wrong questions. So when a pair of great founders we already know, who have just spent half a decade picking up scaleup experience at one of the most successful public tech companies tell us feature success is the future of product love, we listen. You should too. Today we're incredibly proud to announce that Creandum has led the pre-seed round into Bucket and we cannot wait to see the magic Rasmus and Ron will create as they redefine modern product {feature} development.

articles.title: The Race to Net Zero in Europe
articles.excerpt: Shining Light on Solar Tech
articles.text: _By [Sabina Wizander](https://twitter.com/sabinawizander) and [Iris Hendriks](https://www.linkedin.com/in/iris-hendriks-216466136)_ _This article attempts to chart the solar Climate Tech startup ecosystem and how it can help us build a carbon-neutral economy. It builds on Speedinvest and Creandum's analysis of [1100+ Climate Tech startups founded in Europe ](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/u/2/d/10mlHmmzLgMyuQKjjL9F_yFPCiAePC1qY/edit#gid=704078740)in the last decade and our overview of the [European Climate Tech startup ecosystem](https://www.speedinvest.com/blog/europe-climate-tech-report)._ ## The importance of solar to reaching net zero The energy sector is one of the largest sources of global emissions, accounting for [almost 75% of all global CO2 emissions](https://ourworldindata.org/emissions-by-sector). Energy fuels our cars, heats our homes, and powers our industries. So it is necessary to decarbonise the sector by increasing the use of renewable energy sources in order to limit the rise in global temperatures to 1.5°C, the goal set by the [Paris Agreement](https://unfccc.int/files/essential_background/convention/application/pdf/english_paris_agreement.pdf). To achieve this, 40% of Europe's total energy consumption should come from renewable sources by 2030. Solar energy has the potential to play a particularly key role, especially as the technology that supports low-cost photovoltaic (PV) systems continues to mature. The efficiency of PV panels is measured in terms of the percentage of the sun's energy that the panel can convert into electricity. By this measure, the efficiency of solar panels has almost doubled in the past 10 years with modern PV modules reaching efficiencies of greater than 20%. Next-generation systems in labs have even reached about 40% efficiency, highlighting [the still unrealized potential of this technology](https://www.ise.fraunhofer.de/content/dam/ise/de/documents/publications/studies/Photovoltaics-Report.pdf). As for cost, the price of solar energy follows Swanson's Law which predicts that the cost will decrease 20% for every doubling of the installed capacity. In practical terms, this has led to the price for solar energy [dropping by 90% between 2010 and 2020](https://speedandscale.com/home/). According to Lazards LCOE (levelized cost of energy) calculation, utility-scale solar energy is already cost-competitive with conventional generation methods such as gas, coal and nuclear ([min $29/kWh vs. min $65/kWh for coal](https://www.lazard.com/perspective/lcoe2020)). And, as described above, technological advancements will probably further push the price down. ## Flipping the foreign policy script on oil and gas dependence Energy dependence on authoritarian governments with poor human rights records is a long-standing problem. The [top three oil producers after the United States](https://www.worldometers.info/oil/oil-production-by-country/) are, in fact, Saudi Arabia, Russia and China. The security issues of this arrangement are clear. A real-world example of this is the fact that the EU is still [heavily reliant on Russian oil and gas](https://www.nytimes.com/2022/03/23/business/olaf-scholz-russia-energy.html), importing 40% of their gas from Russia. These payments then fuel the country's government and fighting forces who are (at time of publication) engaged in a brutal invasion of Ukraine - the horrors of which are only now becoming apparent. At the same time, 45% of the country's federal budget comes from taxes and export tariffs. So, what is currently a vulnerability in Europe could become Russia's Achilles' heel if investments are made that make it easier to turn away from oil, gas and coal. With this in mind, the EU was quick to release the [REPowerEU initiative](https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/fs_22_1513). Its aim is to accelerate achieving Europe's energy independence from Russian fossil fuel imports before 2030, while still keeping retail energy prices in check. Out of the six measures described in the initiative to reduce this dependence, two focused on increasing the amount of renewable energy and one specifically on solar energy. But there is still a long way to go. Since 2019, the EU and UK have [at least doubled their net solar productions](https://www.iea.org/data-and-statistics/charts/net-solar-pv-capacity-additions-2018-2020). But while these growth numbers seem impressive at first sight, we need to put them into perspective. The net solar PV capacity in the EU amounted to about 160GW in 2020. In order to reach the ambitious [goal set out by the European Green Deal](https://ec.europa.eu/info/strategy/priorities-2019-2024/european-green-deal_en) to become the first climate-neutral continent by 2030, this number [needs to increase to 870GW](https://api.solarpowereurope.org/uploads/EU_Market_Outlook_for_Solar_Power_2021_2025_Solar_Power_Europe_d485a0bd2c.pdf). Considering the current average energy output of newly built solar plants in Europe, this would cover 6,745km² - or more than 2.5 times the surface area of Luxemburg. But if certain problems are overcome, then a solar Europe is an achievable goal. ## What are the primary obstacles to widespread adoption of solar tech? The good news is that the bottlenecks in the adoption of social energy are manageable and can be overcome with the development of specific technologies. We see four main constraints to scale installed PV capacity: lack of availability of cheap solar panels, lack of qualified installers, high upfront cost for the installation, and balancing of the energy grid. **Lack of cheap available solar panels:** In the past 20 years, China became the global manufacturing hub for solar panels, currently producing about 80% of global PV systems. Traditionally, the lower personnel cost in China outweighed the shipping costs to Europe. However, [according to the Asia Times](https://asiatimes.com/2022/01/solar-panels-a-portrait-of-china-supply-chain-risks/), a

articles.title: Don’t hire designers too late
articles.author: Felix Haas
articles.text: When you think about hiring your first designer, it's probably already too late. Too often when building a product, there has been the misconception that "design can come later" - and this often results in developers doing the UX themselves and building up usability debt that is costly to unwind. For the right designer, joining an early-stage business can be a tremendous opportunity . Instead of months designing buttons for a corporation, they may transform a startup's entire trajectory, from early customer touchpoints to branding and product. But in truth, 95% of designers don't want to be the first designer at a startup. It can mean sacrificing access to collaborators, mentors, or simply a well-structured environment that allows them to thrive. Having joined startups like Gorillas, Mapify, Arive, and Yababa as the first designer, I wanted to share my key advice on how to hire and attract the right design talent for that position. Let's go! ## Look at products you like One really effective way to source great designers is by looking at products that you love to use and then figuring out who built them. Don't just look at commercially successful products like Airbnb, Uber, or Instagram, but really ask yourself and your friends what tools they use and why they are truly great. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/4xRfqVdHeJ3HPb8AWcs2aW/db616f9f9bb1880c876dcd2edfefd46e/image_57.png) Once you find something cool, start hunting the creators on Product Hunt or Twitter and reach out. Don't be shy when cold-approaching. Most people love hearing from fans and appreciate the kudos. ## Start building relationships today - and be patient You want to start building relationships with designers as early as possible, not just because you are hiring. Once you run out of the designers you know, you're going to need to explore the nearest communities and start expanding that network. Attend events, use LinkedIn, and don't forget venues where designers are known to mingle such as specific cafés, coworking spaces, or creative studios. As with any community, make sure to think about what you can offer to help them first. I know many founders who approach inspiring designers on a regular basis. Even if you are not able to recruit them, invite them for a coffee and get to know their environment. Learn as much as possible about the design community. ![Doing cold approaches on LinkedIn](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/49PnDIMRxejzBx0gN2T1n0/7881eeb5712451b460610d5d56f46891/image_58.png) The more you're invested in and care about design, the more designers will want to work with you. So start integrating design values into your company's culture. ## Twitter as the secret Designer Hub Usually, people always refer to Dribbble and Awwwards when sourcing new design talent - but the truth is, beautiful imagery and nice visuals are not primarily what you should be looking for in a first designer. You want someone who is versatile - a jack of all trades. Someone who is able to think analytically and critique other designers' work. And Twitter is the secret place where designers are exchanging thoughts and giving each other this kind of revealing feedback. You can start following trending designers or simply start interacting with a few through tweets, threads, or direct messages. ![Interacting with designers on Twitter](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/1ymjz8jw4ZupYbVUY3EcYQ/aafb63e907c4f674071fe84dcacd5751/image_59.png) Remember, your first designer will be part of crafting your product strategy, including entire design foundation, so make sure you look at those characteristics when evaluating your candidate. ## Be generous with position and equity Great designers are getting paid a lot and you won't be able to compete on salary. Fortunately, I know a lot of great designers who value ownership and impact over large paychecks. And that's your chance to win. Consider giving your first designer the same amount of equity as your first engineer. Depending on your company's stage you should even be thinking about offering your designer a "co-founder" or "founding designer" position. If that's not an option, an example for a founding designer position with current market expectations in e.g. Berlin would be around 70 to 85k EUR salary with an ESOP package from 0.5 to 1.2%. Sounds like a lot? If they are the right candidate, it will be worth it. If you find someone that is hungry to learn and ready to grow with your startup, you want to be flexible with what you offer. ## Closing thoughts Getting to know the best of the best designers is a process that takes time and you will most likely have to try a lot of different things. Make sure you onboard design talent rather sooner than later in order to avoid the trap of building a product that no one knows how to use. Generally, I am not a big fan of outsourcing design work at the beginning of a company, but a freelance UX/UI designer is still way better than no designer if you have no other choice. A last thought: are you a designer or an agency that works with startups? We know many great founders who'd love to work with you and I am happy to make an introduction. Just get in touch!

articles.title: Do VCs add value?
articles.author: Carl Fritjofsson
articles.excerpt: 4 years later, the answer remains: sometimes
articles.text: # 4 years later, the answer remains: sometimes. VC = smart money. VC = value add. VC = helpful. This is how the VC industry markets itself to founders. But do founders really agree? A few years ago, __ [Henri Deshays](None) (at [Newfund](http://newfundcap.com)), [Owen Reynolds](None) (then at University of Chicago, now [Expon Capital](http://Exponcapital.com)) and I embarked on a project for [Kauffman Fellows](http://kauffmanfellows.org/) where we polled a group of VC and founders to establish if VCs really add value. [The headlines were clear](https://medium.com/hackernoon/do-vcs-really-add-value-founders-say-sometimes-f27bb956eb8c): VCs think they add about 30% more impact than founders do, with similar gaps in perception across most other areas. The startup world evolves fast, and four years later we've now gathered the same team and repeated the research to see what has changed. We received responses from 71 VCs (76% early stage, 13% late stage and 11% multi-stage) and 88 founders (Stage: 96% Early (seed, A), 4% late. 65% EU, 31% US). ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/48ztKD9FV3ItsL2UWSpXUs/bdc274afeebbd9884c188aed618616a8/image_51.png) ## Perceived impact of a VC. Similar to the last survey's results, VCs overestimate their level of impact and helpfulness. Founders rate the average impact of their VCs as a mere 5.2, whereas VCs believe their impact to be rated a decent 7.1 - a 35% difference. We decided to break this impact score down to better understand in which areas founders and VCs perspectives differ. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/46nywPXfATu9vZzqGyH1VM/1a1619060973e29b86e0207cadc08df7/image_52.png) The largest gap in perception comes in recruitment - 69% of VCs think they're making a real difference here when nearly 79% of founders state that VCs don't. Big difference. Similarly, with introductions and marketing, nearly three-quarters of VCs see an important impact, whereas only 44% of founders agree. This is particularly interesting because, in the 4 years since our first study, the conversation about VCs offering operational support has only grown, with funds increasingly adding talent functions and portfolio support roles. Yet the gap in perception is widening. Living up to founders' expectations (or VC promises) is difficult. So what can VCs do to add more value in recruitment? Given that VCs manage multiple portfolio companies and need to spend time on finding new investments, founders can probably not expect every VC to fuel their recruitment funnels. Some can, but most cannot. However, for key executive roles, VCs could go the extra mile by opening up their Rolodex, sharing experiences on how to best work with recruitment agencies, and most importantly jumping on calls with final-round candidates to push them over the finish line. Your investors can be your best cheerleaders. On a positive note, one area both founders and VCs agree that VCs have a significant impact is on follow-on financing. VCs have a natural ability to help founders raise follow-on capital by for example connecting founders with the right people and funds, supporting on preparation materials such as decks and financial plans, and helping craft fundraising strategies. Generally, what is striking about this chart is that some founders note their VCs to be critical across some areas, whereas others deem their impact insignificant. The range is wide. There are different possible explanations for this. One could be the quality of the VC and their relationship with founders. There are many VCs who simply are capital allocators and only call the founders to yell when they get a negative investor update. There is also a massive difference in terms of relationship and network between the top and medium VCs. The ability for the VC to leverage their network for hiring, biz dev, fundraising, etc. can be dramatically different. Another explanation is the natural cycles any founder-investor relationship follows; some periods, VCs roll up their sleeves, communicate daily and help a startup navigate through times of uncertainty. Other times, the company is smooth sailing and might not need or want help from their investors. Depending on when you ask the founder, the perceived value add may vary a lot. At the same time, it would be unusual if founders thought their investors were key to their success in these fundamental areas, when they are the ones in the trenches day in and day out. In a sense, rather than looking at the findings as "VCs overestimating their value", another way to look at it is: "founders rank VC impact somewhere in the middle to bottom of everything on their list." Founders tend to themselves and realize their success is a result of their ingenuity, and not VCs paving their way. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/4LDWDGSv2vVniQ8h8dC25c/74c9dc31502c8fed85577e78b239e752/image_53.png) This was confirmed when we asked in which areas founders want more help from their VCs. Fundraising is the clear outlier. Helping to run the biz comes much later. So what do we take away from this? Clearly, founders and VCs need to have more discussions and alignment on expectations at the start of their relationship. This also means founders meaningfully DDing their investors to ensure the best match. VC referencing is essential for any founder raising. Quality VCs show their value both in good and tough times. ## Most important factors when picking your VC. We asked founders and VCs to rank what's most important when deciding which VC firm to partner with. The top five reasons are the same for VCs and founders, but with some significant differences in weighting. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/54UFhFggr0BFVrjCeUnxxk/d442e4e69fc5e37fa0f6d05ec03d9100/image_54.png) VCs realize personal chemistry is important but maybe underestimate quite how much. Founders rated it nearly 25% higher and made it number one on their list. Sector experience sees a smaller gap but is still much higher ranked fo

articles.title: Creandum London, 6 months later
articles.author: Peter Specht
articles.excerpt: Eight people, one big community, and even more investments
articles.text: # 8 people, 1 big community, and even more investments When I first met the Creandum team in January 2021, it was clear that they were serious about [putting deep roots in London](https://medium.com/p/f20b7f749d12). The ambition was to establish an equally large and important office to those in Stockholm and Berlin. 8 months in, I am proud to see that we are well on our way to accomplish this. ### A phenomenal team We are now 8 people, including 5 investors and 3 portfolio/ operations. In building a high performing team, it was important to us to combine the advantages of local hires with the benefits of shipping in Creandum superstars from other regions. That gives us the best of local knowledge and networks with the consistency and continuity of Creandum culture. That includes Creandum Partner, [Peter Specht](https://www.creandum.com/team/peter-specht), in London after 5 great years in our Berlin office and Associate [Nick Lawitschka](https://www.linkedin.com/in/nikolauslawitschka/?locale=de_DE), who joins having most recently worked as a Founders' Associate at an early stage startup and JP Morgan London before that. London has also become a hub for our non-investor team, particularly in talent and marketing. Head of Talent, [Michelle Coventry](https://www.creandum.com/team/michelle-coventry), has already developed a Net Promoter Score that puts us to shame and Marketing & Comms Manager, [Felicitas Hagen](https://www.creandum.com/team/felicitas-hagen), is expanding our marketing operations to do even more for the portfolio on the ground. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/7BAjo9BdS0Am1WZoC6O6aa/512c794c18c6eacbff1ebd2dfc3d9bd5/image_48.png) ### Our London portfolio is expanding Our London office may be new - but our presence is not. We have made 14 investments in this ecosystem over the past years, making it our second-largest behind DACH. It has been incredible to connect more closely with our local founders on the ground, enable them to meet each other and spend time with us in person helping grow their businesses. We are also very grateful for the support they have given us to meet new people and close new deals, and in the past 6 months we have added an additional 3 London companies to [the funds' portfolio](https://www.creandum.com/portfolio/). ### Thank you for the welcome! We have been astonished by the welcome from local founders, angels and VCs and are delighted to have been able to work closely together and develop the start of what we believe will be long term relationships. London has truly opened up post covid, and we want to extend a warm thank you to all of us who have met and welcomed us over the past months! This all became clear in person when we hosted our first get together for our local founders and ecosystem. It was great to thank everyone and officially celebrate our presence in London, as well as seeing you all meet and form even stronger bonds. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/28Bpv69CIIRglKRBCnA0LC/53e92ba5b65c7a997738d27a5230fb11/image_49.jpg) ### What is next? This is just the beginning. We just raised a [$500m fund](https://medium.com/p/9806a930c22) and we are ready to partner with many more UK based Seed/ A stage founders. And of course, we will embark on the dreaded London real estate search to find a larger permanent office soon. Stay tuned, the best is yet to come. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/5wTClpsi09MHfMUnzvxWBi/7291744aaa6d27f6f421629bffab9ccc/image_50.jpg)

articles.title: Project Eaden’s technology makes saving the world an indulgence
articles.author: Carl Fritjofsson
articles.text: ### Project Eaden's technology makes saving the world an indulgence As human beings, we neither want to compromise on our current life nor give up on our pleasures. This is why climate change is such a challenging fight. No one wants to give up on the quality of life. Instead, we are looking for alternative ways to keep enjoying life while doing good for the environment. At Creandum, we believe that technology and innovation are the only path forward. We saw the huge potential behind this thinking in our 2020 [deep dive into Climate Tech](https://blog.creandum.com/time-to-cool-the-planet-creandums-perspective-on-climate-tech-1d863dd983f4) and [mapped the market of innovative businesses that promise to have a positive impact on climate](https://medium.com/creandum-family/europes-leadership-in-climate-tech-c7ecba25a303). We made our first investment related to climate somewhat indirectly when we [backed the world's most ambitious cheese company: Stockeld dreamery](https://blog.creandum.com/cheeses-creandum-backs-noquo-foods-7aa762da546e), as the food industry happens to be one of the major contributors to co2 emissions worldwide. Meat, and especially beef, is an even larger bad guy when it comes to co2e emissions which naturally led us to look for innovation in this industry. However, available options are often not attractive enough for many people. Hence, we knew we needed something truly revolutionary here that doesn't come with a compromise. Today, we're honored to announce Creandum's backing of [Project Eaden](https://www.projecteaden.com/) - "the Tesla of sustainable food". ### Say hi to full taste and zero guilt. Imagine you're eating a steak. Think of the flavorsome taste and tender, juicy texture that seems to melt in your mouth. Can you feel it? Then you know what we experienced when trying the first prototype created by Project Eaden. This "how-do-they-do-that" taste explosion is exactly what we have been looking for. Just like Tesla builds a completely new experience: A different technology for products that enhance the pleasures of life without compromise or guilt. Project Eaden has designed a technology platform using proprietary technology to produce never before seen foods. Their first creation is the one thing no other next-generation food company has succeeded with - a _sustainable_ piece of steak with a mouthwatering taste, texture, and looks. ### The team? A dream! Behind Project Eaden is a world-class team that covers all dimensions of a successful food company building: [David Schmelzeisen](https://www.linkedin.com/in/david-schmelzeisen/), [Hubertus Bessau](https://www.linkedin.com/in/hubertus/), and [Jan Wilmking](https://www.linkedin.com/in/janwilmking/). ![The Project Eaden founders want to make saving the planet a pleasure not a compromise (from l.t.r.: Dr.-Ing. David Schmelzeisen, Hubertus Bessau and Jan Wilmking).](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/1g3ZZb5nTdKguAeyNIotT8/3a03f54587fa6af41683a00e4a2a0f27/image_47.jpg) For the tech, we have David who's a Ph.D. from RWTH Aachen bringing a mind-blowing technical innovation into the world of foods. Hubertus is a well-known face in Germany's food industry since his time as co-founder of [mymuesli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mymuesli), where he has proven to master marketing and distribution in a competitive food category. And Jan perfectly complements the team as the operations and managerial leader, who has seen true scale as one of the execs behind the success of Zalando. We've known Jan for a number of years, and this is in fact the second time Creandum has tried to invest into his entrepreneurial path, and luckily the second time Jan brought us along. ### Bold ambition and big words require substantial financing. Saving the world takes time and resources. As such we're happy to announce that Creandum is leading Project Eaden's first financing round. This €8m seed round will enable the team to bring their first product to market. Together with Magnetic VC, Atlantic Food Labs, and a broad list of top-quality angels, we couldn't be more excited to support this best-in-class team with their truly world-changing ambition. This is the day you heard about Project Eaden for the first time, but it won't be the last. Project Eaden is here to create paradise on earth. We can't wait to show you how. Welcome, Project Eaden!
