articles.title: Financial plan
articles.author: Peter Specht
articles.excerpt: Template by Creandum
articles.text: In every fundraising process, sooner or later, investors want to talk numbers. Besides the great J-curved charts predicting revenue in colorful pitch decks this usually means it is now time for a look under the hood. To understand key assumptions and value drivers of the business in more detail, the VC usually requests a business plan or financial plan. To help you get this right [Maximilan Grohmann](https://www.linkedin.com/in/maxgrohm/) and me put our thoughts together and built a more detailed [spreadsheet template](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1KluUePvlMCu-F8w4p2MXbvUhXy7wqtKjWLdRL71ANkM/edit?usp=sharing) with having Series A in mind ([FIND HERE](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1KluUePvlMCu-F8w4p2MXbvUhXy7wqtKjWLdRL71ANkM/edit?usp=sharing)). Over the years on the receiving side of such plans, we observed that the quality of such business plans for early stage ventures (Creandum predominantly looking at Seed and A rounds) varies a lot. However, whilst the pitch deck is often seen as the most important to prepare for fundraising, a well put together business plan in many cases will be equally important. If the deck is for getting your foot into the door, then the business plan (as well as any other materials you will share in the data room later on) will actually help you make it through the door frame to the other side. In the following, summarized 5 tips we also give to entrepreneurs in our portfolio when preparing the business plan for fundraising. ### 5 key tips for your business plan model 1. **Think of the model as another chance to present your company.** Well-prepared materials are usually a good indicator for investors of how things are running on the inside. You want to present a well-structured, thought-through, and aesthetically appealing model, so try to avoid sharing files designed for internal use only, which may be harder to understand for outsiders or poorly formatted. 2. **Be comprehensive but pragmatic.** Make sure you provide sufficient granularity of the data you are showing. The core KPIs driving your business should be easy to find and understand. Make sure the data you are presenting is really relevant for the reader. Be pragmatic and simplify certain standard line-items if they are not as important to your business specifically. Especially since many variables will be hard to forecast beyond 6–12 months in early stage companies, a too complex model could potentially be even less reliable than a slightly simpler one. 3. **Make it as easy as possible for the reader to understand your model.** Think about the way you want to present the output of your model. You should make sure you present individual line-items, sections and entire sheets in an order that intuitively makes sense to the reader. Consider guiding the reader through the model with a "how to read me" section in the beginning as well as useful comments throughout for things like abbreviations and core assumptions. 4. **Be transparent.** Do not mislead the reader of your model. Whenever possible, use standard ways to calculate certain KPIs. Do not make too many random adjustments or invent fancy new KPIs that might make your numbers look stronger than they are. Ideally, give the reader the opportunity to easily understand your calculations by using formulas rather than hard-coding final values. 5. **Base your case on reasonable assumptions.** The previously mentioned points around transparency and traceability become even more relevant when talking about your assumptions of the main drivers of your business case. Rather than driving your model using black box top-line MoM growth assumptions make sure you identify the key variables which are actually driving **your** business case and build on those. ## Business / Financial plan model template To make all of this a bit more tangible, we have created an exemplary dummy model /for a fictitious B2B SaaS business raising a Series A or later(**[CLICK HERE](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1KluUePvlMCu-F8w4p2MXbvUhXy7wqtKjWLdRL71ANkM/edit?usp=sharing) for the template**). This model was inspired by the best practices of many great and more detailed financial models we have seen over the past years. Even though you might be able to use a lot of that for your own business, please keep in mind that the main purpose is to provide a rough idea of how such a model can look like Disclaimer: It is not intended to be a plug-and-play template which you can just fill with your own data and you are ready to go - each individual business is just too different for that. The intention of this model is to provide a rough orientation of how such a model could look like, how you can structure and format it. However, if you actually find a few parts which you can directly implement in your own model, that is great too of course! Even though it is a fairly straightforward model - in the following you can find some short explanations and background on the different sections of the model. **Cover sheet** ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/3CSbtvvUOLiLxXR5qst9dn/b86c24d0e9f695f612aa8a7418e1bea0/image_41.png) This is the first thing the reader of your model will see. Here, you make the very first impression and set the tone for what is coming next. A nicely formatted cover sheet with a logo your company color etc. give the reader a good feeling when opening the model for the first time. **How to read me** ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/1yAPsNgaQYthAApCYkKDVE/1ede971828589908fee8d01895f7e1c2/image_42.png) As mentioned earlier, every model will be slightly different and company specific. Things that might be super intuitive for you will take other people minutes or hours to understand or might even lead to an extra round of Q&A which costs time and energy in already intense fundraising processes. Use such a section to provide any background information you think is necessary for the reader to really understand your model the way you want them to. Ex

articles.title: The secret weapon to higher-quality software — Creandum backs Better Stack
articles.author: Carl Fritjofsson
articles.text: Venture firms look for startups everywhere and anywhere. Oftentimes our trusted network serves as a strong qualifier, and hence warm introductions are most efficient. But many times it can be very random how we find startups we get excited about. This time, Creandum investment manager [Lauri](https://www.linkedin.com/in/laurilehtmaa/), who's a developer at heart, was targeted by an ad for a new type of observability service. Intrigued by their marketing, he started playing around with the tool and quickly got blown away by how incredibly user-friendly its onboarding and product experience was. Switching back to his VC mindset, he proactively knocked on the founders' door and asked about the company's plans ahead. And that is how we met Creandum's latest portfolio company [Better Stack](https://betterstack.com/). ### Observability what? Within the world of software, development observability is the practice of monitoring and measuring the current state of your system. Basically, observability is core to any software product that cares about customer experience or even just their top line, as it really tells you in real-time (or often 15 minutes too late with legacy products) if your stuff is working or not, and whether your business is operational or not. Most well-known observability players are companies like Datadog, New Relic, Splunk, and AppDynamics. These impressive giants generate incredibly high-quality revenues, due to strong lock-in effects and account expansion potential. Public markets historically have valued these types of companies some of the highest in the world, when looking at enterprise value / next twelve-month revenue. At the time of writing Datadog is the second-highest valued company in the world in terms of EV/NTM revenue (at ≈19x only after Snowflake at 21x). These are the type of companies VCs dream to back, so when we see a seismic market shift that can generate the next observability winner we pay attention. ### Why now and why Better Stack? Most existing observability solutions were built using technologies from 10–15 years ago (such as Elastic's ELK) and are still very capable at solving the work they were designed for. However, as with all software categories, when the world evolves and software engineering practices mature, many legacy tools become slow in performance, feature bloated, and cumbersome to use. And with continued demands on performance, increasing breadth and depth of tech stacks, these legacy solutions also become increasingly expensive solutions. Better Stack comes to save the day by simply offering a faster and cheaper observability stack. The only way to win against the powerful market leaders mentioned above is through 10x lower cost and 10x better performance. Better Stack does this by recreating the observability stack on top of [ClickHouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ClickHouse) (a revolutionizing open-source database management system) and other state-of-the-art technologies. The technical implications of this are many, and as an example with Better Stack companies may be able to move all their data from what's called ["cold" to "hot storage"](https://www.dataversity.net/cold-vs-hot-data-storage-whats-the-difference/), giving them completely new ways to monitor, analyze and manage their infrastructure and look at things in a much bigger picture than just the latest snapshot of an error. Furthermore, Better Stack is delivering their products in a seamless developer experience (DX) - something which has been completely lacking in this category until now. The user love we see for Better Stack is second to none in the observability space. At Creandum, we pride ourselves as VCs who deeply care about product experiences, and Better Stack not only redefined what beautiful and intuitive observability products look like but ultimately Better Stack customers will be empowered to build better products themselves. Instead of having to spend time on obtaining a PhD in setting up their observability stack –which is more of a necessary evil rather than core to their product offerings. Past winners in developer tools were built on feature breadth, but we believe that the future will be built on superior DX, collaboration, and equipping developers with joyful experiences and best practice, rather than tool boxes filled with all the tools in the world. Think Netlify, Vercel, Supabase, and many others - all replacing individual services within the product catalogs of cloud service providers with dramatically better packaging and developer experience, unlocking both superior productivity and peace of mind in software delivery. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/1mBsn2NwinpaKmEQw6UknR/8d010b2bb9662ce630beb41fd0765431/image_39.png) Currently, Better Stack is offering 2 products: [Better Uptime](https://betterstack.com/better-uptime/) (a monitoring and incident reporting service) and [Logtail](https://betterstack.com/logtail) (a log management solution), and the world can look forward to other complementary products in the future. ### The dynamic duo. These products come from a very special founding team: [Juraj](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jurajmasar/) is an exceptional individual combining a deep technical background paired with a commercial mind thinking about distribution and growth hacking - a rare combination. Juraj is complemented by [Veronika](https://www.linkedin.com/in/veronikakolejak/) who shares an equal technical depth as well as brings the operational muscles to the team. In a nutshell - a great complementary founding duo. ![The Better Stack team.](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/1kEuHK6ZVGE9Xs6KrsSZay/10bb3b70dab0fc78b590c9b25bb18dab/image_40.jpg) Today, we're honored to welcome Better Stack to the #CreandumFamily and announce that the fund is leading the company's $17M Series A. We can't wait to see Juraj and Veronika scale this far and beyond and redefine what we know as observability. P.S.: The [team is hiring](https://betters

articles.title: Creandum promotes Beata Klein to Principal
articles.author: Peter Specht
articles.text: We love to meet entrepreneurs at an early stage and support them along the way to help their companies rise and shine. The same goes for our people: We try to identify talent at an early stage and help them grow and develop within our firm. Today, we're happy to announce that [Beata Klein](https://www.creandum.com/team/beata-klein), who started at Creandum as Associate, is being promoted to Principal. 8 months ago, [she moved from Stockholm to London](https://medium.com/creandum-family/creandum-london-f20b7f749d12) and has been a crucial contributor to Creandum's activities in the UK and [across the Nordics](https://medium.com/creandum-family/denmark-in-2021-the-b2b-saas-capital-of-europe-d1d39d7b1776). Given her tremendous contribution as an Investment Manager and the numerous deals she was part of, having her step up another level was more than deserved. Beata joined us in early 2020, luckily shortly before the pandemic, so we still had a few weeks to get to know each other in the office and benefit from her uplifting personality from the get-go. Beata had just moved back from Vietnam where she not only ate hundreds of Pho soups but also co-founded an ed-tech company. Before her entrepreneurial adventure, she was a trainee within the Kinnevik Group and worked closely with the CEO at Tele2 for a year. She holds an MSc degree from Chalmers University of Technology. During the past 2.5 years, while we have had the pleasure of working with Beata, we continue to be astonished by this fast-moving, always energetic, powerhouse. Beata is not only extremely well structured but she is also a relentless teammate with the guts to take risks and believe in companies at the earliest stages. Beata has played an instrumental part in diligencing and winning many deals, including Craft, Kive, Scapin, Vue Storefront, and many others. More than that she sourced a handful of deals for the fund such as Passionfroot, Tesseract and more yet to be announced. While you might not have met her in person, you've probably seen one of her famous [Twitter threads](https://twitter.com/axeliaklein). Beata now has her own "Twitter corner" in our monthly newsletter. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/7eX0kMJEkw2RKoeR7Gsp47/b0d78390ef836116fa6852b55ca0b296/image_38.png) Beata, thank you for everything and it is a true joy to have you become a senior member of the investment team. We are looking forward to the next chapters with you! Beata will continue her work in the ecosystem and lead deals across Europe. Ping her if you are off to something exciting.

articles.title: User Experience (UX)
articles.author: Peter Ramsey
articles.excerpt: The hidden superpower you should know about
articles.text: When evaluating the Creandum funds' [portfolio](https://www.creandum.com/portfolio/), one thing stands out: **we back teams who build great products**. This is true for most stages in a company's trajectory, from roaring products that have real customers, to grand ideas scrawled on a napkin (or usually, pitch deck). **We back teams who build great products, and UX is the founder superpower to demonstrate their vision.** Often we're evaluating tamed iterations of a wilder dream, which begs the question: how can we invest in pre-seed deals, whilst caring so much about a highly-finessed product. The underlying thesis is that we want founders to understand _how_ to build great stuff, and that they're capable of crafting an experience which serves their vision. This may sound intuitive and cliched, but it's often at odds with what happens. Deadlines, internal pressures and poor hires act as barnacles on a ship, pulling down on your trajectory. In short: **life gets in the way**. <iframe src="https://cdn.embedly.com/widgets/media.html?src=https%3A%2F%2Fgiphy.com%2Fembed%2FNTur7XlVDUdqM%2Ftwitter%2Fiframe&display_name=Giphy&url=https%3A%2F%2Fmedia.giphy.com%2Fmedia%2FNTur7XlVDUdqM%2Fgiphy.gif&image=https%3A%2F%2Fi.giphy.com%2Fmedia%2FNTur7XlVDUdqM%2Fgiphy.gif&key=d04bfffea46d4aeda930ec88cc64b87c&type=text%2Fhtml&schema=giphy" title="" height="244" width="435"></iframe> I should introduce myself: I'm [Peter Ramsey](https://twitter.com/PeteRamsey), and while I'm not helping Creandums portfolio (I'm an [entrepreneur-in-residence](https://www.creandum.com/team/peter-ramsey)), I run [Built for Mars](https://builtformars.com) - a trifecta of a UX consultancy, design studio and a 12,000+ strong UX community. I've been lucky enough to run UX audits and experiments for (_probably_) billions of users, between my clients like Stripe, Klarna and Notion. I obsess over the tiny stuff. So let me give you a 60-second overview of what UX is, and why it should become your next superpower. ### 1. What is UX? Let's cover some terminology first: - **UX** (user experience): this is **how stuff _works_**. - **UI** (user interface): this is how stuff _looks_. I'm genuinely a terrible UI designer (ask anyone at my design studio), yet I've built a career optimizing UX, through tiny improvements. They're totally different skills. For example, plenty of apps have fantastic aesthetic designs (gradients, rounded corners, awesome illustrations), but are horrible to use. Have you ever tried using Amazon Prime's TV app? It _looks_ pretty good, but it's so unperformant that I don't bother scrolling much. Here's an abstract representation I like: ![Note: I couldn't find original source for this image :(](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/zZE6XsZ1dk6swjkfqj95Q/19483536ba70e41b354d7325ca285d62/image_36.jpg) What I (and UX in general) try to answer is this: "_**why aren't people using my perfectly paved path"**_. One answer could be that walking diagonally is simply a shorter distance. But, it may also be that the treeline provides much-needed shade during summer. Or, that after heavy rain the pavement puddles, whereas the grassy verge absorbs the water quickly. In fact, there could be hundreds of rational observations, none of which are impacted by how aesthetically pleasing the edging on the pavement is. In other words: the edge cases of usage may look nothing like the idealistic scenario, and so the ‘happy path' may fail horribly. To be clear, a great product needs both a carefully curated UI and UX. So the paving is also important - I'm being facetious to make a specific point. ### 2. Why we care about UX Firstly, let's address the obvious: - Helping users quickly **identify the _value_ of your product**, and cutting the fat, will **decrease your churn** (or, **increase your conversion rates**). - Because of this, your unit economics improve, which all investors _love_ to see. - People enjoy using products that _feel_ good and are more likely to share it with their friends (i.e., greater velocity of **referrals**). - Great experiences, in an industry full of mediocre ones, can _**be your USP**_. You may not be reinventing banking - just making it easier to do. But I've seen other benefits, which people rarely discuss. Here are three more: - Potential employees will likely visit your website prior to an interview, and it'll set an **impression of your entire organization**. Do you have a buggy app that barely works on mobile? That says something about your management. - Having a beautiful UX encourages developers and designers to care more, and anecdotally, will incentivise individuals to raise their standards. It's **easy to be sloppy** with releases when your whole app sucks. On the other hand, nobody wants to be the developer who released the _only bug_. - Even if the product generates the same utility (with a bad experience), competitors and potential acquirers may value your start-up more, because _creating good stuff is hard_. That's why we care. **It's also why you, a**nd every other VC / investor, should care. If you've got the UX bug, the slide below is a snippet from [this](http://pitch.com/public/a26f8091-a92d-47c0-b1ef-2b6de5cc4a76) presentation I made a few months ago, titled: _The ROI of investing in UX during a recession_. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/68Wh0LqLL7oQqxt28tEPLa/9ebf9fb208d3bceaf9f99e6ed30555df/image_37.png) _Or, if you really really really want to learn more about UX, I routinely publish free analysis on [Built for Mars](https://builtformars.com/). If you're on track building a great product, get in touch with the [Creandum team](https://www.creandum.com/team/)!_

articles.title: Creandum backs Timberhub
articles.author: Peter Specht
articles.excerpt: Redefining timber trading
articles.text: When it comes to disrupting an established industry, it's hard to beat going for one that's existed for over 2000 years. For extra points, make sure it's not only vast but complex and thus we arrive at timber. Timber is one of the largest commodities traded worldwide, with the global market expected to reach [$870bn in 2022](https://www.thebusinessresearchcompany.com/report/forestry-and-logging-global-market-report). Despite its critical nature, the timber industry itself continues to run on manual processes, paper-based logistics and small networks of relationships. But to meet the needs of this evolving market, the industry is changing: that's why we're so excited to be backing the seed round for [Timberhub](https://www.timberhub.com/), as it builds a new digital platform for the timber industry. ## Building a sustainable industry Wood is so ubiquitous in our lives, it can be easy to forget the immense scale of logistics, planning and processing involved. And right now the demands on this system are growing, particularly when it comes to buildings. The modern construction industry accounts for [39% of CO2 emissions](https://www.iea.org/reports/global-status-report-for-buildings-and-construction-2019#:~:text=The%20buildings%20and%20construction%20sector,as%20steel%2C%20cement%20and%20glass.), but building in wood could lead to a [26.5% reduction in global warming potential](https://www.vox.com/energy-and-environment/2020/1/15/21058051/climate-change-building-materials-mass-timber-cross-laminated-clt). Accordingly, [timber needs are expected to triple over the next 30 years](https://greshamhouse.com/news-media/global-timber-outlook/), with climate-conscious countries leaning more towards wood to meet their climate targets. France, for example, has mandated that all new public buildings be [50% timber or other natural materials from this year](https://www.bdcnetwork.com/france-mandate-all-new-public-buildings-be-50-timber-or-other-natural-materials), while the EU has backed its own [Build in Wood](https://www.build-in-wood.eu/) programme. ![The Timberhub founding team.](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/1584tTeTUbIPysXqLE5Vrr/019dc5df6bb69f2165040fc0a35a396a/image_34.png) ## Sanding off the edges Timberhub aims to redefine the market by connecting sawmills with timber buyers, such as pallet manufacturers, construction companies and sellers while managing procurement, payments and transportation of timber materials through its digital B2B marketplace. The platform improves efficiency, (global) access and scale for the industry. Manufacturers and buyers can input exactly the products they're after - dimensions, materials, finishes, lead time etc - and Timberhub connects them to relevant suppliers with the right products at the best price and quickest delivery. Their platform then handles the payment, transport and documentation, so both sides can focus on service. In an era of increasing supply chain scrutiny, Timberhub also provides direct insight into the source of the timber, ensuring that forestry remains reliable, sustainable and ethical. In doing so, Timberhub helps sawmills expand their customer reach and create more efficient orders, while buyers benefit from more competitive pricing, shorter lead times and reduced administrative burdens. ## Planting the seeds of growth The timber market has all the classic markers of a sector ripe for B2B marketplace disruption - [a topic I've covered before](https://blog.creandum.com/the-decade-of-b2b-marketplaces-and-what-we-are-looking-for-fdd116e67138) - particularly huge scale, fragmented supply and demand and a lack of transparency. ![Tag lines of what we look for in b2b marketplaces and Timberhub scoring on it (almost all )](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/7cwR0No66jMsRNvUVaa3dr/badee4314b7a7385520d7d199563fca1/image_35.jpg) But it's notable that it's taken until now for a business to truly capitalise on this potential, and that's down to the remarkable team at Timberhub. Founded earlier this year by former Uber EMEA Head of Pricing, [Ion Sergis](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ionsergis/?originalSubdomain=nl), former Exponent Engineering consultant [Thomas Androutselis](https://www.linkedin.com/in/tommy-androutselis-27930aa2/), [Giannis Androutselis](https://www.linkedin.com/in/giannis-androutselis-80967a200/) and [Dimitris Pagkratis](https://www.linkedin.com/in/dimitrispagkratis/), the leadership team have brought together a unique combination of tech, marketplace, construction, logistics and timber expertise to tackle this ancient industry. Since raising their €1.5m pre-seed round five months ago, market adoption has been rapid. Timberhub has managed to successfully onboard top industry customers and build strong collaboration and trust. Timberhub's team now operates in 15 countries in Europe, ranging from small manufacturers to large construction companies - while also onboarding two of the largest European sawmills, alongside a large number of small and medium operations. The new funding from their seed round will be used to further develop their product, adding new features such as tracking transportation, adding financing options and improving user experience to streamline orders and selling for all stakeholders as they grow their customer base. ## Building a greener future It's always exciting to find a team that has built the right product at the right time. This is truly a platform of the moment, providing the right technological capabilities at a time when the world needs it most. Timberhub is poised to create the technological ecosystem that will accelerate decarbonisation through the seismic timber adoption our world so urgently needs. We're proud to be co-leading their €5.8 million seed funding round with [HV Capital](https://www.hvcapital.com/), supported by existing investors [Speedinvest](https://www.speedinvest.com/) and the founders of [Sennder](https://www.sennder.com/fr). We're proud to welcome Timberhub to the #Creand

articles.title: Founder Coaching
articles.author: Michelle Coventry
articles.excerpt: Explore our coach directory
articles.text: Lately, I've been asking our portfolio founders and operators who excel in their roles as a starting point to help others access great coaching recommendations quickly. I don't assume someone else's endorsement would be an excellent match for you, but I have compiled a handy **Coach directory** along with some tips to find your own. ## Good-to-knows **Coaching Isn't "One-Size-Fits-All".** Coaching is highly personal, and connecting with someone who suits your style is essential. I've observed that doing the work to find the right partner pays forward, so we curated a list to help others get started fast. **Understand Your Objectives.** Before you meet with coaches, consider what you're hoping to achieve. Are you looking for someone who has ‘walked a mile in your shoes' or has experienced a similar journey to you on the challenges and potholes you may encounter? Perhaps you're looking at how to master a specific outcome and need coaching on forming a plan. Maybe you're just looking for an independent, trusted sounding board? Here are some ideas that may trigger working with a coach on: - _You just took on capital and are now looking at managing a board or an executive team for the first time._ - _You are experiencing conflict or concern around relationships with your co-founders._ - _You must have a crucial yet difficult conversation with a critical team member and need coaching on the best approach._ - _You want to be intentional about scaling your culture and seek guidance on how to do it purposefully._ - _You are time-poor yet wish to unlock the motivations of each individual on your team to speed up a healthy dynamic._ It turns out many founders feel unsure and overwhelmed about diagnosing what they need - a great connection with a coach will open your mind up to growth opportunities in a psychologically safe way. **Find a Value-Adding Fit.** While your coach doesn't need to have been a founder before, it can be helpful, especially if you're sitting in the often lonely CEO seat or a first-time founder managing everything life throws at you. All coaches are highly skilled in empathizing and understanding. If they have worked in a scaling tech company or with other founders, this is a good signal they appreciate your context. **Explore the Methodologies.** As part of your introductory call, ask how they typically work to set clear expectations. For example: - How frequently will you engage? - How will they structure your sessions? - Will they need to interact with other members of your team? - How long do they find themselves working with an individual on average? Every coach is unique and will likely possess a variety of approaches in their toolkit. Get a sense of what a partnership will look and feel like to help you understand how to optimize your time working together. If working across your team, alignment can create a more powerful and robust coaching experience rich with context. Still, some coaches prefer to focus their energy on CEOs and founders alone. Seek out the right fit for you. **Book an Introductory Connection / Trial Session.** Effective coaching demands a complete level of trust on both sides; it's a mutual bilateral engagement that creates a foundation to explore topics and situations that may be awkwardly bespoke and personal once you dig in. Most will offer a 30 or 60-minute connection call. Set up a call with 2 or 3 potential practitioners on your list. Observe whether they listen, ask questions, can connect the dots and share helpful insight. Make sure you vibe; you're looking for someone you're comfortable holding you to account and help lead you to positive change by pushing you outside of your natural comfort zone. **Talk to References cautiously.** Seek recommendations yet stay unbiased. What worked well for a friend may not work for you. Listen for their adaptability, experiences and strength of the partnership they have previously encountered with others. If curious, _**I do**_ have a coach. Every ‘athlete' does. I can't emphasize enough the importance of having someone on your bench dedicated to your success. Enjoy the journey; those around you will thank you for your time and effort invested. _Onwards!_ I'm also curious about hearing about your experiences and feedback - connect with me [here.](https://www.linkedin.com/in/michellecoventry/) __[Find the coach directory here](https://airtable.com/shrmLQ2tzTX3VLJwc)__ ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/6dlQFuHKC7zuNxxXFiDvrm/5dde71f617c1a9b42b6f9a8410b7b0f8/image_28.png) _We're all ears if you have coach recommendations; drop me a line at talent@creandum.com._ **Explore more:** - [Trillion Dollar Coach ](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Trillion-Dollar-Coach-Leadership-Handbook/dp/B07NBRF5VB/ref=sr_1_1?adgrpid=1177577851324485&hvadid=73598818961970&hvbmt=be&hvdev=c&hvlocphy=41766&hvnetw=s&hvqmt=e&hvtargid=kwd-73598749593637%3Aloc-188&hydadcr=18488_2211407&keywords=trillion+dollar+coach&qid=1653912263&sr=8-1)(a personal fav from the Valley legend Bill Campbell) - No time? articles.title: Creandum backs Enode
articles.excerpt: Reinventing digital energy infrastructure
articles.text: The recent vogue for Scandi culture has brought its fair share of minimal design, chilly thrillers and hygge-ified cafes to the global stage. Less discussed, and far more important, has been their approach to energy. The Norwegian market is one of the most advanced in terms of energy sophistication. Despite being Europe's number one gas supplier and a major global crude oil producer, Norway has made sustainability a key domestic capability and now [accounts for 10% of electric vehicle sales worldwide](https://www.norwegianamerican.com/norway-teslas-biggest-market/) while meeting [98% of its electricity needs from renewable sources](https://www.iea.org/reports/norway-2022/executive-summary#:~:text=users%20lower%20consumption.-,Energy%20efficiency,the%20dominant%20source%20at%2092%25.). With Europe and the rest of the world facing a looming energy crisis, there's a pressing need for new solutions to the way we approach energy systems. That's why we're so excited to be partnering with [Enode](https://enode.io/) as they build the digital infrastructure for the future of this key industry. As energy prices rise and consumers look to reduce their carbon footprint, more people are looking to take control of their energy at point of consumption. At the same time, the increasing electrification of our day-to-day lives has brought a range of new energy hardware into homes, including cars, home chargers, home batteries, heating and cooling systems. These new systems give users the ability to track their energy usage in real time, but this requires a new kind of infrastructure for energy companies. This means thinking beyond pipelines, pylons and plugs and considering how to manage the flow of usage data for consumers. Most energy companies lack the resources to do so - that's where Enode comes in. Founded in 2020 in Norway by serial entrepreneurs [Henrik Langeland](https://no.linkedin.com/in/henriklangeland), [Thorvald Thorsnes](https://no.linkedin.com/in/thorvald-thorsnes) and [Nikolai Heum](https://no.linkedin.com/in/nikolai-hiring-heum-a3057144?trk=public_profile_browsemap), Enode aims to do for energy companies what Tink and Plaid have done for API-first open banking. Their platform enables energy providers to integrate electric vehicles, thermostats, solar inverters, and other energy hardware directly into their apps - all through a single API. ## The challenge of green data While nearly every industry now involves an element of software development, energy management faces its own unique challenges. The market for home energy hardware - known as distributed energy resources (DERs) - has been growing rapidly, with the global market expected to be worth [$580.8bn by 2027](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/distributed-energy-generation-industry). It's also highly fragmented, with different models of vehicle, battery, heat pumps and chargers all using unique interfaces. Companies looking to create consumer-facing energy management apps at scale face the task of building and maintaining thousands of connections. Enode allows these energy companies to connect to and control the fast-growing demand from energy hardware, providing real-time energy insight and control to consumers, EV fleet managers, e-mobility companies, smart home providers and utility providers. In addition to information-flow-based connections, the Enode API also offers value-add services, such as optimization and aggregation capabilities, to build services such as smart charging, intelligent energy management for households and demand response solutions. For energy companies, this provides the opportunity to go beyond simple energy provision and distinguish their service based on experience and end-user control at a time when customers need it most. ## Powering forward Enode have quickly distinguished itself in the sector through the depth and range of its integrations among Europe DERs. While competitors focus on certain verticals, such as EV integrations, Enode has built the most rapid, comprehensive and efficient solution for new and incumbent energy players to provide more value to their customers across a range of use cases. Through their API, companies can access over 20 hardware brands and over 400 devices across EVs, home chargers, heat pumps, solar panels and more. [CEO Henrik](https://www.linkedin.com/in/henriklangeland/), [COO Thorvald](https://www.linkedin.com/in/thorvald-thorsnes/) and [CTO Nikolai](https://www.linkedin.com/in/nikolaiheum/) are all serial entrepreneurs and have built an ambitious, efficient and effective team. They were part of the 2021 Y-Combinatorcbatch and officially launched the company in early 2022. Since we met the small and scrappy Enode team in April, they scaled the global remote team to 25, now sourcing top talent from around the world. The fresh funding will be used to extend their team focusing on product and commerce and accelerate their expansion to new markets, including the US. We're thrilled to be leading this $15m Series A round, joined by the US funds Lowercarbon, BoxGroup, MyClimateJourney and Skyfall Ventures, as well as angel investors from Tink and the vast energy space. As global uncertainty, high prices and climate concerns grow, this winter is likely to advance the energy management sector even further. Incumbent and new players will have to find new ways to meet consumer demands for control and user experience while managing their own efficiency. With an unbeatable technology platform, Enode is poised to become the digital infrastructure foundation for the API-first future of energy. _If you want to be part of that growth journey, [Enode is hiring](https://enode.notion.site/Enode-Job-Board-ae9ee15eb6bb4a23a7f47b77aeccdf2a)_!

articles.title: Europe’s most significant early-stage founders’ compensation report
articles.author: Michelle Coventry
articles.excerpt: In partnership with Slush, we surveyed how founders compensate themselves and wrote up our findings into a report which you can find here
articles.text: _**‘How much should I pay myself?'**_ - a question we've received many times from [the founders we have backed at Creandum](https://creandum.com/commitments) across the early stages. Market benchmarks tend to kick in from Series B onwards, but before then, there is very little to compare against. What is "normal" for the different sizes, stages and sectors? What role does geography play? Can they expect a pay rise after fundraising and, if so, how much? To add value to the European startup ecosystem, we wanted to close this information asymmetry. Hence, in partnership with our friends at [SLUSH](https://www.slush.org/events/helsinki/), we set out to build **Europe's largest database on early-stage founders' compensation**. On top of sharing our key findings from this survey, we used the data to build a [Compensation Calculator](https://foundercomp.creandum.com/) to serve for founders' individual requests. The idea is not to provide a definitive answer, but rather to give early-stage founders a more informed, data-backed idea of what compensation is "normal" for their business and situation. Let's dive in: ### Methodology Our aim was to build **Europe's most significant founders' compensation data set**. We sent the flare-up for Europe's incredible founders, with the help of drawing from Slush's diverse community. After two weeks, we exceeded our goal of 500 and spoke to almost 650 entrepreneurs across 47 European cities that we combined into 8 regions. We removed incomplete or unclear responses. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/3FAWyMBhkh5slbZVpejVdk/d857c9f5816475f527ef616d7fc41748/image_19.jpg) ### How do VCs think about founders' compensation? _It's a balancing act._ ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/12cVvPylNJ8Md3oUOsrjts/d58b00f215a8d450cc608d88e3fd709f/image_20.png) Keeping funds within the company means swifter profitability, demonstrates discipline, shows an "all in it together" mentality, and an ability to focus on their product and services rather than fundraising. This is all the more important in the early stages because you need to give away a lot of equity for the money you raise. Series A is typically 10% and that only grows with more investment. The lower your expenses, the longer the run rate, and the better it is for you, your co-founders and your business. Of course, "pay yourself just enough to not think about money" has as many answers as there are founders. The compensation needs and expectations of a founder straight out of university with no dependents, versus one who's come from a big bank and has three kids, will be very different. So use your investors as a sounding board. This research and our Compensation Calculator provide a good benchmark and a starting point for this conversation. Your investors and talent partners can then help you navigate the nuance of your particular situation, providing the necessary distance and context, sharing information about the space in which you and your business are operating, and what they've seen with other portfolio companies. They will help you figure out what you and your business actually need to get through the next stage of growth and hit the milestones successfully. ## The key takeaways from our survey - **Founder salaries are higher in more advanced ecosystems**, with the UK out in front. - There's a **big gender pay gap** in super early-stage startups - but it's there throughout. - **The number of co-founders is the single biggest diluter of equity.** - **Fintech continues to be the stand-out**, in terms of how much founders get paid. ### Salaries by stage No surprise, but **_as a company matures_ a_nd goes through progressive funding rounds, founder salaries tend to increase_**. But what does that mean founders are actually taking home? ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/4qZEsZyZEwzhereAL9bNqW/2789c7a580a47d4e91fc367cd4803944/image_21.jpg) We found that on average (mean), bootstrapped and Pre-Seed founder salaries are around €50,000. By Series B this has climbed to almost €150,000. So when considering your own compensation, straying too far above these salaries can act as a red flag to investors, particularly in the earliest stages. But once you've raised a couple of rounds, and proved you can hit critical targets, you can start to compensate yourself more. A new funding round is generally viewed by VCs as a significant de-risking of the company because you've achieved certain milestones, you've grown the company to a certain size and, based on those accomplishments and the new funding, you can reach the next milestones in that journey. So the growth of compensation is a reflection of how much you've put into the company at that point - a back payment for the blood, sweat and tears you've poured into the business. ### Salaries by funding But how are salaries impacted by the actual amount raised? **_Are heavily funded startups paying their founders considerably more?_ _Yes_ _and no_**. For companies that have raised up to €1m, the average founder salary is below €50,000. However, once a company has cumulatively raised over €50m, founder salaries are around €155,000 on average. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/5XNPq78Z7RdVPh6dAJDnmv/852d5c92105e36d085257c731fc80564/image_22.jpg) Salaries do tend to grow in line with funding, but they plateau at around the €11m mark at an average of €125,000. The median figures, however, are a little more linear, which perhaps tells a different story, or this could just be an outlier in our statistics. Then they tend to stay at that level until funding tops the aforementioned €50m. ### Salaries by location _**At pre-seed and seed stages, location has little to no impact on salary.**_ But from Series A onwards, it's all about the UK, where founders make almost €70,000 more than founders in any other region. This makes sense, as salaries in general tend to align more with the US. And there's a higher volume of well-funded startups in the UK plus a rich ecosyste

articles.title: Welcome back, Jakob!
articles.author: Peter Specht
articles.text: At Creandum, we love to keep close ties not only with our portfolio companies but also with our former employees, interns and other outstanding people we got to work together with. Hence, it's no exemption that people return to Creandum after having gained other experiences elsewhere. We are excited to welcome Jakob Stein back to the Creandum family as Associate and recent addition to our growing Berlin team. Exactly two years ago, we first said goodbye to Jakob after his internship with us to let him develop further as an operator. Today, we are more than happy to have him back at the mothership. When Jakob joined us for the first time in 2020, he won our hearts with his positive energy, fun character, proactivity and strong opinions, he's not afraid to share. Back then, no one in the team was as excited about how strong the market came back in Q4 2020 when COVID seemed over as him. He dives into every single deal as if it was his first and last, every time all over again. Jakob's career in the startup ecosystem started by co-founding Q-Summit and working at the Lufthansa Innovation Hub and early-stage fund HTGF. After his time with us as Visiting Associate, he joined our portfolio company cargo.one following his passion for aviation and marketplaces. At cargo.one, Jakob quickly took ownership within the product team and, after a while, became the first "cargonaut" to have boots on the ground across the pond. Spending time in Chicago, Toronto, and Mexico City, he built up both team and sales and left the company as Team Lead North America. Jakob studied at the University of Mannheim and London Business School. At Creandum, he will grow our DACH coverage and bring his experience in internationalization, marketplaces, and vertical SaaS to life. Outside of work, Jakob enjoys backpacking to extraordinary places such as Brunei, Bolivia, Zimbabwe, and North Korea. Coming from cargo.one, his aviation geek DNA will help us find both the best and the cheapest flights for our future offsite and vacations across the team. Jakob, welcome back to the family! Off to new adventures!

articles.title: Creandum welcomes Hanel Baveja as Principal in London
articles.author: Peter Specht
articles.text: At [Creandum](https://www.creandum.com/), our investment efforts go far beyond the borders of Europe and with our US office and [our General Partner Carl based in San Francisco](https://medium.com/p/6b12aeec6805), we have always had a strong presence in the American market. Now, as the European tech ecosystem continues to flourish, it's the first time we have a US native crossing the pond to join Creandum: We are thrilled to welcome [Hanel Baveja](https://www.linkedin.com/in/hanelbaveja/) as Principal to join us in our London office! Hanel brings a wealth of experience and a diverse background to our organization, having spent the past three years as an early-stage investor at [Union Square Ventures](https://www.usv.com/) in New York City. During her time at USV, Hanel worked closely with portfolio companies in various sectors including Zanskar, Slope, Mundi, Floodmapp, Sofar Ocean and Mindset. Hanel's career in venture capital began at Insight Partners, an NYC-based growth-stage software-focused fund, where she was part of the investment team. She also worked on the business development team at Vettery. In addition to her professional experience, Hanel has a unique background. Originally from Ann Arbor, Michigan, she studied Economics and Creative Writing at Harvard (with an intermission studying Art History and French in Aix-en-Provence, France) before moving to New York City. Her varied background and interests, including being a short story editor, writer, and camp counsellor, add a new dimension to our team and we are excited to see her bring her fresh perspectives to Creandum. We've got to know Hanel as a highly thoughtful and outgoing individual, who is deeply invested in working with early-stage entrepreneurs across various industries. As we continue to expand our focus on emerging new sectors like AI or climate tech, we look forward to Hanel's contributions in helping us dive deeper into these areas. She will also help us further dig into the French startup ecosystem. Furthermore, Hanel's expertise and extensive network in the US market will be a valuable asset to our efforts in providing the best possible support to our portfolio companies as they navigate and thrive in this crucial market. Hanel joins our London office as the 10th employee, where she will support our investment team, talent and marketing functions. [The London team has rapidly grown in the past 1.5 years](https://medium.com/p/522c146c17a0), since we opened our office in August 2021. We're delighted to have Hanel strengthen our team efforts on the ground while working in close collaboration with the wider Creandum team across our other key hubs Stockholm, Berlin and San Francisco. Welcome to the Creandum family, Hanel! You rock _If you want to stay updated on her professional journey, follow her on Twitter: [@hanelbaveja](https://twitter.com/HanelBaveja)_

articles.title: Welcome, Janick and Richard!

articles.text: We are thrilled to announce that [Janick Wagner](https://www.linkedin.com/in/janick-wagner-1759b5153/) and [Richard Keuntje](https://www.linkedin.com/in/richardkeuntje/) have joined [Creandum](https://creandum.com/) as analysts. Janick, and Richard, we are looking forward to continuing the work with you across our hubs in Stockholm, Berlin, London and San Francisco.

articles.title: Gender Diversity in Tech Positive signals yet slowed down progress
articles.author: Carl Fritjofsson
articles.text: For years Creandum has been a champion of pushing better gender diversity in tech. We have made it a [key priority at the firm](https://www.creandum.com/diversity/) as we believe this will give us and our portfolio companies a competitive edge in the long run. As part of that, one initiative we have been running since [2018](https://hackernoon.com/diversity-inside-european-vc-more-work-needed-c545353b7e4c) is the _**Creandum Diversity Index**_, where we measure gender diversity across our portfolio companies, under the premise of what gets measured gets done. We're starting to have some interesting timelines for this data (check here for 2018, [2019](https://blog.creandum.com/diversity-inside-european-vc-2-0-limited-progress-made-f89479fe3738), [2020](https://blog.creandum.com/a-small-sign-of-progress-on-gender-diversity-in-tech-915c85ac9221), and [2021](https://blog.creandum.com/under-the-hood-of-diversity-2021-creandum-diversity-index-14caa8a6dd4e)) and for 2022, we analyzed 59 portfolio companies, accounting for a total of 13k employees. Overall, it can be said that despite turbulent macroeconomic conditions, we see positive signals from the portfolio as well as in our own ranks. The progress has slowed down unfortunately, but at least there are only very few declining figures. Let's look at some of the specifics. ### Women employees across all portfolio companies: 45% (+/-0) Across the portfolio, the amount of female employees has remained at 45%. Although the perfect balance may be 50% we actually feel fairly happy about this number, as this can be compared to the tech industry in general where women make up about [33% of the workforce](https://www.luisazhou.com/blog/women-in-tech-statistics/). We also see a stong progress in our portfolio since we started measuring this in 2018. ![% of women across all portfolio companies.](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/7nyP5aJE7cmdSV5gza0ISB/cc679363f0ce6059d2bff9ec1b7beebc/image_9.jpg) ### The larger the company, the better the gender balance If we analyze the percentage of women in different-sized companies, we can see that the larger the companies, the nearer they are to reach gender balance. ![% of women employees sliced by number of employees.](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/1H20Oi5sG0N50oUMTYahnJ/0da8ca25ec62995a1e9e605c4977f1ae/image_10.jpg) ### Women in management: 28% (+/- 0) A number we keep pushing hard for is the number of females on the management team. The reason for this is that we see that **companies that have women in leadership positions positively affect the overall number of women across the organization**. In 2022 despite remaining at a stable number we, unfortunately, have not seen the progress we had hoped for and the number has come down since 2020. ![% of women in management / leadership.](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/5la9gplnM4u7Z5nVXIrZHb/507f83b74de5dc6ff23beb79e7c6022f/image_11.jpg) Still, we're pleased to continue seeing almost half of our portfolio companies having more than 25% women in management and an increasing amount of companies (10%) having 50% women in leadership roles. ![% of companies who has x% of women in leadership / management.](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/3Fm8GeGOahbr39u5uqKnYZ/18fe43c3b7bd9eaf23e13a2675326fd4/image_12.jpg) ### 15% of women in board positions (+2%) We also see the number of women board members continuing to slowly increase. After a 3% increase in 2021, an uptick of 2% absolute is still not massive, but we're aware that for this metric to move, we need a lot of patience. In particular, in respect of the stagnating numbers of women in management positions, we're glad that this percentage is still going in the right direction. ![% of board seats filled by women.](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/6qcxOZS7Jf8Viwn5RRZQmQ/86308041c1241eabf2c594ceeab8fd0e/image_13.jpg) The fact that almost half of our portfolio companies have at least 1 female board member remains stable, but what's more positive is that almost a third of companies have at least a quarter of the board being female. 8% of our portfolio companies have 50% women board members. ![% of companies who has x% of women in board seats.](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/nntxO6VflHDWRPMkmUUFJ/12ebd55523228400e0cddbf5c45f0197/image_14.jpg) ### Pay Gap. As for pay gap, for every dollar a man earns, a woman gets $0.83, even topping the prior peak from 2020 which is a promising improvement. ![Pay gap.](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/4d0t1YjEiZesx6uuKh95IF/6c0c71be11d955237938a94a6b001b17/image_15.jpg) ### Looking in the mirror: Looking at inside [Creandum](https://www.creandum.com/team/), our work seems to be paying off. Our hiring and promotions resulted in positive developments of us reaching our own DE&I goals. Since 2021, we have significantly improved our team's gender mix. We have achieved two major milestones: Our team of checkwriters, including General Partners, Partners, and Principals has reached 40% women-to-men ratio, which is within our definition of a balanced team. Further, we have even exceeded our goal of reaching gender equality across the entire organisation with 52% women, a number that jumped up from 42%. Where we are still behind our targets is within our partner group, with only 1 out of 8 being a woman. ![Women ratio and targets across the Creandum organisation](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/5GwzRmKwS2Ebj4JXurNIod/49bd2ac5d36709abbfd728f662a1fe77/image_16.png) ### % of invested companies with a female founder, by fund Last, but not least, we wanted to be transparent on where we're standing with our target of investing activities. We set a target for CVI that at least one out of four companies backed should to have diverse founding teams with at least one female co-founder or CEO. About one year into the fund's deployment we are close at 21%, and this has steadily been going up with each fund. ![% of companies backed by Creandum with diverse teams (>1 woman co-founder/CEO).](

articles.title: Creandum’s female checkwriters
articles.author: Carl Fritjofsson
articles.excerpt: How they are transforming the VC and tech industry
articles.text: International Women's Day is a great opportunity to remind the ecosystem of the crucial, much-needed female movement within the Venture Capital industry, which has notoriously been non-diverse. This movement has a massive impact on gender balance across the entire tech industry, including improving the likelihood that female entrepreneurs receive investment. **[According to Pitchbook](https://pitchbook.com/media/press-releases/pitchbook-report-on-women-in-vc-finds-growing-number-of-female-checkwriters-could-bolster-female-founded-startups-disproportionately-impacted-by-pandemic),** female checkwriters are more likely to invest in female founders. In the [Creandum funds' portfolio](https://www.creandum.com/portfolio/), we have a proof point: for our latest fund, [Creandum VI](https://blog.creandum.com/creandum-vi-half-a-billion-for-early-founders-before-its-obvious-9806a930c22), our target was that at least one out of four investments should have at least one female co-founder or CEO. Nearly one year into the fund's deployment and we are close to this (21%), a number which has steadily increased with each fund. This is in line with our increasingly gender-diverse team of checkwriters, meaning people in investment decision-making roles such as General Partners, Partners and Principals. [In 2022, the team has reached a 40% women-to-men ratio](https://blog.creandum.com/gender-diversity-in-tech-positive-signals-yet-slowed-down-progress-80c25e1d5182?source=collection_home---4------0-----------------------), which is within our definition of a gender-balanced team. At Creandum, we have achieved this major milestone through hard work, strong diversity measurements and variousinitiatives (more on our [updated DE&I policy here](https://www.creandum.com/diversity/)). But the work is far from done, as we have more targets to reach such as gender equality across the partner group. Today, we want to highlight this much needed trend that should bode well for female founders and those wanting to pursue a career in the industry. Let's shine a light on Creandum's female checkwriters - we hope that this will inspire others. ### [Sabina Wizander](https://www.creandum.com/team/sabina-wizander) **Partner, based in Stockholm** ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/7fNSpWxXdjCNinAkpYHEIj/234bf52e9dad41f6b3166a47d531e94f/image_5.jpg) Sabina is our first and so far only female partner on the team. She broke into VC after having been at McKinsey. Two years in with Creandum from 2015 to 2017, she joined one of our most exciting companies at that time: the HealthTech company Kry. At Kry, she held different C-level positions and helped to take the company to 150M EUR revenue from Series A to D. Sabina returned to Creandum in 2021, this time armed with invaluable operator experiences that shaped her investing mindset for the better. _"Having seen the fundraising process from the other side of the table as an operator has made me very humble as an investor in how you use the founder's time and what type of questions you ask."_ In addition to HealthTech, Sabina has a passion for ClimateTech, the Metaverse and the Creator Economy, leading deals in Scapin, Passionfroot and Enode. Want to experience Sabina's enthusiasm and ambition? Check out [Venture Europe's latest podcast episode](https://open.spotify.com/episode/4z2VQ7SE8n2ptso4ztnaxk), or read the interview on [Sifted](https://sifted.eu/articles/creandum-new-partner-wizander/). ### [Gemma Bloemen](https://www.creandum.com/team/gemma-bloemen) **Principal, based in London** ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/5Ar3bvcWY7NwpfSF66obyz/6b99224470303c0262b0dee562e1c18a/image_6.jpg) Gemma is our gem from the Netherlands. Before joining Creandum in 2021, she gained significant experience on the operating side as COO at Elder, a UK home care marketplace, as well as in a senior management role at Uber where she was part of scaling the growing local UK team from 20 to 250 people. In addition, Gemma is one of Europe's most active [female Angel investors](https://sifted.eu/articles/female-angel-investors-europe/). Similar to Sabina, Gemma is a former McKinsey consultant. articles.text: Amazon Web Services launched in 2006 and set off a wave of infrastructure cloud computing. Since then many other cloud providers have come to market as well as a host of products and services to manage and operate your infrastructure. More or less every modern software company relies on cloud computing today, however, this heterogeneous market has created an environment defined by its complexity, littered with redundancies and inefficiencies. The result of this is cloud computing is expensive. One study from a16z found that cloud spend for software companies can be as high as [80% of their revenue costs](https://venturebeat.com/datadecisionmakers/the-real-cost-of-cloud-computing/). That's unsustainable - especially in the macro environment we're in today. Hence, many software companies are looking for remedies for this. Some are even trying to repatriate their workloads from the cloud to on-prem, but this comes with another list of challenges. Instead, what most companies do is throw bodies at the problem by hiring DevOps specialists (more on these guys in a moment ). Cue the world of automation: what if there was software that could manage this for you? Like really cut your [cloud costs](https://cast.ai/cloud-cost-optimization/) by an average of 60%, while also improving performance? Enter: CAST AI—Creandum's latest portfolio company. ### DevOps... what? First, a quick word on DevOps. It's essentially a framework to help IT teams and developers better deliver the speed and quality of software deployment. Higher velocity. Quicker iterations. Increased performance. Everything. Atlassian did a great summary of it [here](https://www.atlassian.com/devops) if you want to read more. As cloud computing - and its costs - has grown, so has the need for DevOps teams and specialists. Between 2015 and 2019, job postings for DevOps roles [grew by over 400%](https://www.indeed.com/lead/impact-of-tech-talent-shortage). [90% of business](https://www.bain.com/globalassets/noindex/2021/bain_report_technology-report-2021.pdf) leaders cite DevOps as a top strategic priority. But filling these positions isn't easy and, as such, a huge skills gap exists. Only 12% of businesses describe their DevOps capabilities as mature. This is where CAST AI comes in. It's an automated DevOps platform that allows software businesses to optimize their cloud infrastructure far better than a human ever could. And the results are incredible. ### Why CAST AI and why now? CAST AI's entry point into this world is by focusing specifically on Kubernetes (K8s) platform, specifically to deliver an autonomous Kubernetes _(Kubernetes is Google's open-source container orchestration system and the most popular mainstream approach for software developers to build their cloud infrastructure)._ Its first product was an automated cost optimization solution for K8s which, on average, reduces cloud computing costs by 6o%. In minutes. Powered by AI, it analyses multiple data points to find an optimal cost-performance ratio. The platform delivers a cost-efficient, high-performing, and resilient infrastructure for all types of Kubernetes workloads. It's since added a cost monitoring service and security insights so companies can detect, monitor and prioritize any K8s vulnerabilities. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/1HxJBGXDyyU45uU9vrl8HD/4016ef38f3504a10c354a15ca66dad45/image_3.png) All of this is hugely beneficial to most companies, in both the short term and the long term, and therefore of great interest to everyone here at Creandum. In the short term, the current macro-environment has got every company looking through their [cloud costs](https://cast.ai/cloud-cost-optimization/) and removing anything unnecessary. CAST AI does that - and then some. This frees up vital cash but it also aids faster growth and reduces engineer effort and the need to hire expensive DevOps personnel. But over time, by using CAST AI, companies are able to automatically scale up and down their clusters based on real-time demands, improving the delivery and performance of the application. Again, fully automated without human intervention. Instant payback from lowered cloud bills, while enhancing performance is the 10x improvement we look for at Creandum. ### Strap on for explosive growth. This appetite is backed up by growth that is almost unheard of in this sort of macro market. CAST AI went to market less than 18 months ago and has seen quarter-by-quarter revenue growth of over 220% and already worked with some of the biggest customers in the world, including Iterable, OpenX, Branch, and more. This strong, clearly defined customer base demonstrates a clear target audience and proves that there's a real hunger and demand in the market from large and small companies. ### A winning, experienced team. The CAST AI founders, [Yuri Frayman](https://www.linkedin.com/in/yurifrayman/), [Leon Kuperman](https://www.linkedin.com/in/itexecutivecto/), and [Laurent Gil](https://www.linkedin.com/in/laurentgil/), are all serial entrepreneurs with successful exits to Google, Oracle, and Comcast. CAST AI was born out of the frustrations they had with their previous startup, Zenedge, where they first-hand experienced an ever-growing cloud bill. They tried many things to optimize their infrastructure and spending, and realized there was a real opportunity to build a standalone product for this specific problem. After selling the company, the founders teamed up again to found CAST AI. ![](//images.ctfassets.net/vx9l0f5sup17/1H9iJ4WdJMOgEfMRrVoGtB/26f45418227d14fde49f3df80cce29ad/image_4.png) Needless to say, we couldn't be more excited for a seasoned team of serial founders who have successfully worked together for many years and have lived through the pain they are solving for. As such, we're happy to announce that Creandum has led CAST AI's latest round, raising $20M!
